title: Scientists Develop Water-Powered Miniature Rotors
content: Reliably generating controlled miniature rotations has long been a challenge: Chemical propulsion systems wear out, and methods that use electric or magnetic fields require complex setups. A team from KIT's Institute of Microstructure Technology (IMT) and the Suzhou Institute of Nano-tech and Nano-bionics (SINANO) at the Chinese Academy of Sciences has now demonstrated that flow at a water surface alone is sufficient to rotate a floating object in a fixed direction. Their research is published in the journal Science Advances.
summary: Researchers from the KIT and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have demonstrated that water-surface vortices can drive tiny rotors without the need for electricity, magnets, or chemicals. Their study, published in Science Advances, shows that a floating object can be rotated in a fixed direction solely by the flow at the water surface.

title: ValuePair Friendship App Launches with Unique Matching System
content:
A new social platform has been launched, aiming to revolutionize the way people connect with each other. The platform, currently in open beta, requires users to register and complete an onboarding process, answering a series of meaningful questions designed to help the system find a suitable match. These questions are based on research from various studies, including those by Aron, Hall, Byrne, Finkel, and Hazan, which have been used to create a set of 14 questions that users must answer when a match is found. The answers are revealed immediately, and both parties must agree to form a connection before a chat can be opened.

The platform's creator, a senior developer, was motivated to build this project due to the shallow nature of traditional friendship and dating apps, which often rely on browsing through profiles or swiping through pictures. The goal of this new platform is to encourage more meaningful conversations by providing a base for discussion through the prepared question sets. Users can also create custom question sets to play through with their connected matches, helping to keep the conversation engaging. The platform has been running for 14 days, with around 150 users signing up, and has received positive feedback from its early adopters. The creator has been using Reddit as a primary marketing strategy, posting about the idea and concept rather than directly advertising the platform, which has proven to be effective in attracting new users.

The platform's success, albeit still in its early stages, is a promising sign that there is a demand for more meaningful and substance-based social connections. With its unique approach to matching and conversation starters, this platform has the potential to fill a gap in the market and provide a more fulfilling experience for its users. As the platform continues to grow and develop, it will be interesting to see how it evolves and whether it can maintain its momentum and attract a larger user base.
summary: ValuePair is a friendship app that uses a matching system based on meaningful questions to connect users with similar values and interests. The app has gained around 150 users in its open beta phase, with users providing positive feedback on the app's unique approach to forming connections.

title: Ukraine Welcomes Daria Kaleniuk to Lead Anti-Corruption Action Centre
content:
François Picard welcomed Daria Kaleniuk, Executive Director of the Anti‑Corruption Action Centre, to discuss Ukraine’s evolving wartime challenges. Kaleniuk emphasized that the conflict now extends beyond the battlefield to the nation’s institutions, arguing that battlefield victories and democratic resilience are inseparable from comprehensive reform of the defence establishment.

While acknowledging President Zelensky’s decision to appoint a younger, reform‑oriented commander‑in‑chief, Kaleniuk noted that this change represents only “half” of the necessary transformation. She stressed that the more consequential battle lies in governance, requiring deeper anti‑corruption measures and institutional overhaul to support Ukraine’s long‑term stability and democratic development.

The meeting underscored the importance of aligning military reforms with broader governance reforms. As Ukraine continues to confront both external threats and internal institutional challenges, the partnership between national leaders and anti‑corruption advocates will be crucial to ensuring sustained progress and resilience.
summary: François Picard welcomed Daria Kaleniuk, Executive Director of the Anti-corruption Action Centre, to discuss Ukraine’s defense reforms. Kaleniuk emphasized that battlefield success and democratic resilience require deep reform of the defense establishment and governance.

title: Dating Apps Impact Relationship Satisfaction and Economic Aspects of Desire

Swipe right for interest; swipe left to move on. What once involved the drama of meeting someone—glances, hesitation, approaching, rejection, discovery—has been compressed into almost "gamified" interfaces. summary: Dating apps like Tinder have become a common way for people to meet potential partners, often using a gamified interface to swipe through profiles. title: Can a MUD evaluate LLMs? A $99 proof of concept
content:
Researchers Explore MUD-Based Evaluation of Large Language Models

In a novel experiment, a group of researchers has investigated the potential of using text-based games, also known as MUDs (Multi-User Dungeons), to evaluate the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs). By leveraging these early text-based games, the researchers aimed to assess the capabilities of LLMs in a unique and challenging environment. Utilizing personal computers and just $99 in API credits, the team conducted an extensive experiment, running their test on nights and weekends over several months.

The study's results revealed a fascinating leaderboard, but more surprisingly, the measurements of each LLM on four behavioral dimensions highlighted inconsistencies in the models' performance. When two of the dimensions, which heavily relied on an LLM classifier, were removed, one of the frontier models fell significantly in the rankings. Moreover, an analysis of the agreement between the classifier and a second judge showed a wide range of per-model agreement, from 85% to 22%. The aggregate kappa value of 0.04 for probe detection indicated that the instrument was noisy, but it did not pinpoint which models were affected. Notably, the most impacted model shared a model family with the classifier, raising questions about potential bias.

While the study's findings are intriguing, the researchers emphasize that this is merely a proof of concept and not a validated benchmark. The paper, data, and code are publicly available under open-source licenses, allowing others to review and build upon the work. The team is currently designing Phase 2 of the experiment, which aims to address limitations such as limited human raters, a small environment, and a single objective. By incorporating human baselines, multiple judges, and more objectives, the researchers hope to create a more robust evaluation framework for LLMs.
summary: Can a MUD evaluate LLMs? A $99 proof of concept.

title: French modelling scout linked to Epstein found dead
content:
Daniel Siad, a modelling scout who had been linked to the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, was found dead at his residence outside Paris, prosecutors announced on Wednesday. The body was discovered on Monday evening, and the Nanterre prosecutor’s office said an autopsy will be conducted to determine the cause of death.

Siad’s name appeared almost 2,000 times in the files released by the U.S. Department of Justice that detail Epstein’s network, underscoring the depth of his connections to the financier’s circle. While the circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear, authorities are treating the case as a matter of public interest and will investigate any potential links to the broader Epstein investigation.

The investigation is ongoing, and no further details have been released at this time. The report was provided by FRANCE 24’s Emerald Maxwell.

title: Bento: Offline HTML Slide Tool
content:
New Offline Slide Tool Emerges: Bento Simplifies Collaboration and Editing

A team of developers has recently created Bento, a groundbreaking offline slide tool that streamlines collaboration and editing processes. This innovative solution utilizes web frontend technologies and coding harnesses like Claude Code to provide a seamless experience. By packaging all necessary features, including animations and shared editing capabilities, into a single HTML file, Bento eliminates the need for manual code editing or cloud login requirements.

Bento offers a range of features that make it an attractive alternative to traditional slide tools. Users can edit, present, print, and save slides directly within the browser, with the option to share files via email or Airdrop. The tool also supports live collaboration, allowing multiple users to edit slides simultaneously without the need for a cloud connection. This is made possible by an encrypted blind relay, which enables shared editing without compromising data security. Existing PowerPoint files can be easily transformed into Bento slides using Claude or ChatGPT.

Bento is available for public testing, with a gallery of sample decks and a live guestbook for users to experience shared editing and collaboration firsthand. The tool's code is MIT licensed and can be accessed on GitHub. With its focus on offline functionality and data security, Bento is poised to revolutionize the way teams create and collaborate on slide presentations.
summary: Bento is a single HTML file that allows users to create, edit, and share slides offline, with features including animations and live collaboration. The open-source tool is available on GitHub and can be used directly in a browser, with no installation or cloud login required.

title: E Jean Carroll documentary showcases her fight against Donald Trump
content:
Documentary Sheds Light on E Jean Carroll's Resilience in the Face of Trump's Allegations

In a remarkable display of courage and determination, former advice columnist E Jean Carroll continues to battle through an ongoing series of legal disputes with Donald Trump. Despite the former president's attempts to silence her and shift attention away from the allegations, Carroll remains a steadfast advocate for accountability. At the age of 80, she has already secured two civil suits against Trump, a testament to her unwavering resolve in the face of adversity.

The documentary "E Jean Carroll" by film-maker Ivy Meeropol offers a poignant portrayal of Carroll's life and career, from her rise to fame as a wisecracking advice columnist in 1980s and 1990s New York media to her current role as a vocal advocate for women's rights. With a career that has spanned decades, Carroll's experiences provide a unique perspective on the evolution of the #MeToo movement and the challenges faced by women who have come forward with allegations of abuse. The documentary also sheds light on Carroll's complicated past, including her initial skepticism towards high-profile cases involving Bill Clinton and Clarence Thomas.

Through Carroll's story, the documentary highlights the ongoing struggle for justice and accountability in the face of powerful figures who seek to silence and intimidate their accusers. As Carroll continues to push forward in her pursuit of justice, her documentary serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of standing up against abuse and holding those in power accountable for their actions.
summary: E Jean Carroll, a former advice columnist, is the subject of a documentary film by Ivy Meeropol, which follows her ongoing legal disputes with Donald Trump. Carroll, in her 80s, has successfully defended herself in two civil suits against Trump, who has accused her of sexual violence.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Concertgoers Wearing 'Pit Diapers' to Get Close to Artists
content:
Concertgoers' Behavior Raises Concerns Over Fandom and Personal Boundaries

In recent weeks, several high-profile concerts have been marred by incidents of audience members engaging in behavior that is both disturbing and inconsiderate. Artists such as Olivia Rodrigo, Noah Kahan, and Morgan Wallen have all spoken out about the issue, with Rodrigo revealing that she has been exposed to unpleasant odors from fans lining the barriers at her shows. Kahan, meanwhile, posted a plea on social media for concertgoers to use the bathroom instead of soiling themselves in the crowd.

The problem appears to be more widespread than initially thought, with reports of fans urinating on others and even defecating in the crowd becoming increasingly common. The issue has sparked a wider conversation about the boundaries of fandom and the need for personal responsibility. While some fans may have genuine medical needs that require special accommodations, the sheer number of incidents suggests that a culture of disregard for others has taken hold. As one fan's unfortunate experience at a Morgan Wallen concert demonstrated, this behavior can have serious consequences, with police now investigating the incident.

The proliferation of "pit diapers" and other specialized products designed to mitigate the effects of inconsiderate fans speaks to a deeper problem. Concert organizers and artists are calling for greater awareness and consideration from fans, emphasizing the need to respect personal boundaries and use the facilities provided. As the music industry grapples with this issue, it remains to be seen whether a cultural shift can be achieved, and whether fans will learn to prioritize the comfort and well-being of those around them.
summary: Fans have been wearing "pit diapers" to concerts, which are designed to allow them to urinate without leaving their spot in the front row. This trend has been linked to several incidents of audience members urinating or defecating on others during recent concerts.

title: Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender film adaptation released on Paramount+
content:
A Feature-Length Sequel to 'Avatar: The Last Airbender' Faces Uncertain Release. 

Paramount Pictures has announced a two-city theatrical release for the animated sequel film, 'Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender,' despite initially planning a wider theatrical run. The movie, which was initially scheduled to premiere in theaters, was later downgraded to a direct-to-streaming release on Paramount+. However, due to a leak of the film online ahead of its scheduled debut, the studio has opted for a limited theatrical release in two cities, concurrent with its streaming premiere on Paramount+. This strategy is reportedly aimed at ensuring the film meets the eligibility criteria for this year's Academy Awards.

The decision to release the film in a limited capacity follows a troubled production history for the 'Avatar: The Last Airbender' franchise. The original animated series, which aired on Nickelodeon from 2005 to 2008, was adapted into a live-action film by M. Night Shyamalan in 2010. Although the movie was a commercial success, it received widespread criticism from fans and critics alike. A subsequent live-action adaptation, released as a Netflix series in 2020, received a more positive response. The new animated sequel, which takes place years after the events of the original series, is the latest attempt to bring the beloved franchise to the big screen.

The theatrical release of 'Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender' is set to coincide with its premiere on Paramount+, marking a rare instance of a major film receiving a limited theatrical run in an effort to qualify for awards consideration. The decision reflects the complex and often challenging process of adapting popular animated series into live-action films, as well as the evolving landscape of the film industry.
summary: The animated film Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender is a continuation of the Nickelodeon series, following the characters years after the events of the show. The movie is now available on Paramount+ and is also receiving a limited theatrical release.

title: Reading Becomes a Trendy Pursuit Among Celebrities and Fashion Brands

Earlier this year, Coach collaborated with Penguin to produce miniature literary bag charms – fully readable micro-versions of books, from I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings to Sense and Sensibility. Miu Miu hosts a Literary Club; Chanel its Rendez-vous littéraire. Being bookish is now sexy, we’re told. I-D magazine recently ran a piece on the Whitney Review – a literary journal based in New York – proclaiming its team part of the “hot literati reshaping criticism”. The founder describes the Review as “sexy, surprising, stubborn”, and its contributors “curious and beautiful” (corroborated by an accompanying shoot in which the Whitney team look more like a bunch of models than anything else). But the piece raised eyebrows in the comments section of i-D’s Instagram page: “the definition of vacuous and vapid”, writes one user; “No room for ugly literati, only HOT”, says another. Should we be sceptical about reading’s voguish turn? Continue reading...

title: Elon Musk's Backlash Over The Odyssey Fails to Hurt Box Office
content:
Renowned film director Christopher Nolan's latest release, The Odyssey, has achieved a significant box office milestone despite facing a targeted online backlash led by tech mogul Elon Musk. The movie, an adaptation of Homer's epic poem, has been met with widespread critical acclaim for its visually stunning action sequences, dark magic, and unexpected cameos, including a dolphin. The film's success serves as a testament to the enduring power of Nolan's storytelling and the resilience of his work in the face of online criticism.

At the center of the backlash was Elon Musk, who took to his social media platform to express his discontent with the movie's casting choices, specifically the inclusion of Lupita Nyong'o and Elliot Page. Musk claimed that the casting was a ploy to satisfy new Oscar diversity requirements, a notion that has been thoroughly debunked by industry experts. Despite Musk's efforts to rally support for his cause, his claims were met with widespread skepticism, and many online users began to ridicule his interpretation of Hollywood and The Odyssey. The irony was not lost on critics, who pointed out that Musk's own social media platform was filled with misinformation and conspiracy theories.

The Odyssey's success serves as a reminder that online backlash can be a double-edged sword. While it may generate attention and publicity, it can also backfire and galvanize support for the targeted individual or project. In this case, Musk's efforts to take down The Odyssey only seemed to bolster its reputation and attract more viewers. As the film continues to break box office records, it is clear that Nolan's work has resonated with audiences and will endure despite online criticism.
summary: Elon Musk criticized Christopher Nolan's film The Odyssey for its casting choices, claiming it promoted racial animus. Despite the online backlash, the film achieved a strong weekend box office performance.

title: Microbes Organize in 3D Structures in Liquid Cultures

Scientists are increasingly recognizing that the relative spatial arrangement of microbes plays a role in digestion, immunity and overall health.

title: Musk Announces Grok Imagine to Produce Historically Accurate Odyssey Film

A link in the same tweet shared a three‑minute clip that the user said was generated by Grok Imagine, depicting a scene between Odysseus and the nymph Calypso.

Musk’s announcement comes amid a broader criticism of Christopher Nolan’s recent blockbuster adaptation of the Odyssey, which he has repeatedly denounced for its casting choices. While the film has been commercially successful, Musk has used his platform to argue that the production deviates from the source material. By positioning his AI‑generated version as a more faithful retelling, he seeks to differentiate it from Nolan’s interpretation and appeal to audiences interested in a historically grounded portrayal of the ancient narrative. The project’s release timeline remains tentative, and no official production schedule has yet been disclosed.
summary: Elon Musk says his AI platform Grok Imagine will create a historically accurate adaptation of Homer's Odyssey before the end of the year. He shared a three‑minute clip generated by the system featuring a scene with Odysseus and Calypso.

title: Meta Launches Content Seal AI Watermarking Tool
content:
Meta introduced its “Content Seal” in July as a response to a March directive from its Oversight Board, which urged the company to use internal tools to curb the spread of deceptive generative‑AI content. The new watermarking system, embedded invisibly in images produced by Meta’s Muse model, is intended to flag AI‑generated media and signal its origin to users and third‑party tools.

Industry observers note that Content Seal resembles earlier efforts such as SynthID, yet it has been described as a marginal addition to Meta’s broader AI ecosystem. The announcement placed the watermarking feature in a brief footnote, and critics point out that more established standards—like the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity’s C2PA Content Credentials—already offer robust, interoperable labeling solutions. As a result, many analysts remain skeptical about the efficacy and transparency of Meta’s approach.

While Meta has committed to deploying its own tools to address misinformation, the limited visibility and perceived lack of rigor in Content Seal suggest that the company may still rely on external frameworks to achieve broader industry acceptance and regulatory compliance. The effectiveness of the watermarking system will likely be judged in the coming months as it is tested across Meta’s platforms and by third‑party verification services.
summary: Meta introduced Content Seal in July to watermark images generated by its Muse model. The tool was announced after the Oversight Board urged Meta to deploy its own detection tools in March.

title: Mars Had Underground Magma Rivers
content: Finding widens selection of rocky planets that may once have been habitableMars once had rivers of magma bubbling beneath its crust, new research suggests. They used the seismic data to analyse a mysterious boundary 15 miles (24km) below the surface of Mars. Their findings, published in Nature Astronomy, showed that the most likely cause for this boundary was molten rock pooling deep underground and stretching sideways for hundreds or even thousands of miles. summary: Researchers at the University of Oxford have found evidence that Mars once had rivers of magma bubbling beneath its crust. title: Art Historian Didier Rykner Criticizes Macron’s Louvre Expansion Plans
content:
Stuart Norval announced the appointment of Didier Rykner as a new contributor to La Tribune de l’Art, highlighting the art historian’s dual expertise as an investigative journalist and founder‑editor of the publication. Rykner, known for his critical assessments of museum policies, has articulated a pointed critique of the Louvre’s current strategic direction, asserting that the institution’s primary challenge stems from the misallocation of resources rather than a shortage of funding.

In his analysis, Rykner acknowledges the necessity of ongoing security enhancements but warns that the museum’s historic fabric is at greater risk due to a politically motivated architectural expansion that diverts funds from essential conservation work. He argues that leading museums should prioritize the preservation of collections, building integrity, and visitor experience over high‑profile construction projects, framing the issue as a question of stewardship versus ambition in cultural governance.
summary: Didier Rykner, an art historian and founder of La Tribune de l’Art, argues that the Louvre’s resources are being misallocated toward a politically driven architectural expansion. He says the museum should prioritize preservation of its historic fabric and collections over prestige projects.

title: Enzyme Functionality Enhanced Beyond Water Boiling Point
content: Enzymes are proteins that can be harnessed for chemical manufacturing, but they are typically restricted to mild temperatures because proteins unfold and lose their function under heat. summary: Researchers have discovered a method to encapsulate enzymes in a porous organic polymer, protecting them from heat damage. This breakthrough enables enzymatic reactions to occur efficiently at temperatures above 100°C, allowing for new possibilities in chemical manufacturing.

The research, titled "Stochastic Wage Suppression on Gig Platforms and How to Organize Against It," develops a mathematical model motivated by digital labor markets, including crowdwork, ride-hailing and food delivery. It shows how a buyer that posts prices and can wait for workers to accept them may keep payments very low when some workers are willing to accept tasks at very low prices.

title: Hemodialysis mortality risks by blood type
content: Do you know your blood type? It is important information used for blood transfusions, but few realize that blood types could also be linked to disease risks. Other noncardiovascular conditions are also associated with ABO blood types, such as certain cancers and infectious diseases. Researchers at PSI and the University of Zurich have now examined the BRAF protein in greater detail, gaining valuable insights into its complex regulation.

title: Students unearth rare, centuries-old pot at Florida Spanish mission site
content: Some 400 years ago, a member of the Indigenous Potano-Timucua tribe scooped up some clay and carefully molded it into a modest vessel, small enough to rest in the palm of their hand. summary: Astronomers have discovered a black hole stirring a gas cloud containing a neighboring galaxy named MQN01 J004131.9-493704, nicknamed the "red potato". The galaxy is located in the early universe and has been observed by NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory and James Webb Space Telescope.

title: Researchers Study Immune Cell Behavior in Sepsis Response
content: Despite the best efforts of intensive care unit (ICU) staff and physicians and the most advanced life support, Dr. Bryan Yipp, witnesses many deaths in the ICU attributed to sepsis. "Sepsis is the body's overwhelming immune response to an infection, and sometimes that response can cause death," says Yipp, a critical care physician and clinician-scientist at the Cumming School of Medicine. "While many cases involve people with long-term illnesses, seemingly healthy people can be at work or home one moment and then, within hours, be admitted to the ICU."

title: Childhood Air Pollution Exposure Linked to Higher Metabolic Risk
content: Although the effects of air pollution on respiratory diseases are well established, its effects on cardiometabolic health are often overlooked. This population-based European cohort study led by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal), a center supported by the "la Caixa" Foundation, suggests that higher exposure to air pollution during childhood at home and at school may increase the risk of metabolic syndrome. title: Biological sex influences cancer development in lung and other cancers
content: Biological sex factors into cancer in ways you might not expect. summary: Research has found that biological sex plays a significant role in the development of lung adenocarcinoma and other cancers, with notable differences in incidence rates between males and females. title: New Antibiotic Candidates Target Vitamin Supply in Resistant Bacteria
content: Bacteria have spent decades evolving resistance to virtually every antibiotic we have thrown at them. To stay ahead, new drugs must hit targets that existing antibiotics have never touched. A research team at the Helmholtz Institute for Pharmaceutical Research Saarland (HIPS) has now developed a series of synthetic drug candidates that do exactly that: By blocking an essential molecular supply system, these molecules cut off the bacteria's supply of essential vitamins and starve them to death. The team published its findings in two studies in the Journal of Medicinal Chemistry.
summary: Researchers at the Helmholtz Institute for Pharmaceutical Research Saarland have developed synthetic antibiotic candidates that target a previously unexplored area of bacterial biology. These candidates block the supply of essential vitamins to bacteria, starving them to death and potentially offering a new approach to combating antibiotic-resistant infections.

title: New Gene Therapy Offers Hope for Rare Form of Childhood Epilepsy
content: SCN2A-related developmental epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) is a rare, severe form of childhood epilepsy and one of the most common causes of monogenic autism. The condition is caused by single mutations in the sodium voltage-gated channel alpha subunit (SCN2A) gene, which controls the flow of sodium ions into neurons. These mutations promote abnormal brain excitability, resulting in uncontrolled seizures along with developmental delays, autism, movement problems and gastrointestinal issues. Most of these mutations are de novo (not inherited from a parent) and arise spontaneously.
summary: SCN2A-related developmental epileptic encephalopathy is a rare, severe form of childhood epilepsy caused by mutations in the SCN2A gene, leading to uncontrolled seizures, developmental delays, and other health issues. Most of these mutations are de novo, arising spontaneously rather than being inherited from a parent.

title: Blood Flow and Vascular Health Linked to Alzheimer's Protein Spread
content: Alzheimer's disease is not only about the accumulation of toxic proteins in the brain. A growing number of studies indicate that the health of cerebral blood vessels may also play a decisive role in the onset and progression of the disease. A reduction in blood flow, vascular damage and the accumulation of amyloid beta, one of the key proteins associated with Alzheimer's, in fact feed into one another in a pathological cycle.
summary: A new brain model suggests that reduced blood flow and vascular damage contribute to the spread of amyloid beta, a key protein associated with Alzheimer's disease. The model proposes a pathological cycle where blood flow, vascular health, and amyloid beta accumulation are interconnected factors in the onset and progression of Alzheimer's.

title: Twitch introduces parental controls to block teen livestreams
content:
Twitch has rolled out new parental‑control features that let guardians link their children’s accounts and manage how teens use the platform. The update, aimed at users aged 13 to 17, allows parents to block their children from broadcasting, disable private messaging (Whispers) and prevent them from sending or receiving direct messages. In addition, parents can set flexible daily limits on screen time and receive a weekly email that summarizes their teen’s activity, including the channels watched and hours spent.  

The controls are designed to give parents a clearer view of their child’s streaming habits while giving them the tools to set boundaries. By linking a parent’s account to a teen’s, the platform provides a dashboard for monitoring and adjusting permissions, and the weekly email offers a concise report of viewing patterns. These measures are part of Twitch’s broader effort to improve safety and transparency for younger users.  

With the new features in place, parents can now more effectively supervise their children’s use of Twitch, ensuring that minors are not broadcasting or engaging in private chats without oversight. The platform’s updated policy reflects a growing emphasis on responsible content creation and user protection in the streaming community.
summary: Twitch has added parental control features that let guardians link accounts of users aged 13 to 17 and manage settings. The tools allow parents to block livestreaming, disable private messaging, and receive a weekly email summary of their teen’s activity.

title: Nintendo's Splatoon Raiders Review: A Disappointing Single-Player Experience
content:
Nintendo's highly anticipated single-player spinoff, Splatoon Raiders, is set to hit shelves on July 23, with a price tag of £41.99. The game marks a departure from the series' traditional multiplayer format, offering a more solo-focused experience for fans of the quirky and colorful Splatoon series. However, initial impressions suggest that the game is best enjoyed when played cooperatively with up to three others, highlighting a clear design bias towards team-based gameplay.

While the game's single-player mode is certainly playable, its structure is tailored towards team-based missions, where players can work together to complete objectives and upgrade their equipment. The game's hideout ship serves as a hub for character customization and play style tweaking, allowing players to fine-tune their approach before embarking on repeatable missions. This cooperative focus is reminiscent of the series' multiplayer roots, where teamwork and communication are key to success.

Despite its potential, Splatoon Raiders falls short of the series' usual inventive and playful standards. The game's lack of innovation and uninspired design may leave fans of the series feeling underwhelmed, particularly in comparison to the multiplayer experience. Nevertheless, fans of the Splatoon series will still find something to enjoy in Splatoon Raiders, and its cooperative focus makes it an excellent option for playing with friends or joining forces with strangers.
summary: Splatoon Raiders is a single-player focused spinoff in the Splatoon series, allowing players to complete missions solo or cooperatively with up to three others. The game features a structure tailored for team play, with players upgrading equipment and tweaking playstyle before embarking on repeatable missions.

title: Brain Waves May Hold Key to Understanding Reality
content: Your brain has something surprising in common with the ocean: waves. Electrical activity washes over the brain's surface, creating what are called traveling brain waves, or neural traveling waves. These waves cause real differences in your behavior and attention and—again, like ocean waves—can have variable causes, from intrinsic activity to environmental inputs.
summary: Traveling brain waves, also known as neural traveling waves, are electrical activities that occur on the brain's surface. These waves can influence behavior and attention, and their causes can vary from internal brain activity to external environmental factors.

title: Geopolitical Economic Order Framework Developed
content: A new paper published in Global Strategy Journal develops a geopolitical-economic order framework suggesting that the extent of geopolitical competition incentivizes states to create one of two types of economic order: a market-based order built on laissez-faire and mutually beneficial voluntary exchanges, and a state-based order focused on state power and government intervention in the economy.
summary: A new paper in the Global Strategy Journal presents a framework for understanding geopolitical-economic order. The framework suggests that states create either market-based or state-based economic orders in response to geopolitical competition.

title: Study suggests Milky Way may have undergone major disk orientation flip
content: The Milky Way may have undergone a dramatic change in orientation during its history, according to new research that helps explain a long-standing mystery about our galaxy. Using supercomputer simulations of galaxies like the Milky Way, a team of astronomers from Durham University found that galaxies with slowly rotating stellar halos are more likely to have experienced a major "disk flip," in which the galaxy's disk changed its orientation by more than 90 degrees.
summary: Astronomers using supercomputer simulations found that galaxies with slowly rotating stellar halos are prone to undergo major disk flips of more than 90 degrees. The research suggests the Milky Way may have experienced such a dramatic orientation change in its past.

title: Scientists Uncover Flu Virus Hijacking Mechanism
content: Scientists uncovered how influenza A commandeers human cells, including a surprising strategy that dissolves tiny structures in the nucleus and releases proteins the virus may use to reproduce. The detailed molecular map could reveal new drug targets and help researchers study dangerous flu strains such as H5N1.

title: Scientists Discover New Solar Cycle Turning Point for Early Storm Predictions
content: A newly discovered turning point in the Sun’s 11-year cycle could allow scientists to predict future solar activity years earlier than before. At this “switch-off” point, the most violent space weather abruptly ends, and the remaining number of sunspots offers clues about the next cycle’s strength. Early projections suggest Solar Cycle 26 may be moderate, but a clearer forecast is expected in about two years.
summary: Researchers have identified a new phase in the Sun's 11-year cycle, which may enable earlier predictions of solar storms. This "switch-off" point, occurring at the end of each cycle, provides clues about the strength of the next cycle, potentially allowing for more accurate forecasts.

title: Midlife TV Watching Linked to Reduced Brain Volume
content: Watching television very often in midlife may be linked to troubling brain changes decades later. In a study of about 1,700 adults, frequent TV viewers later showed smaller brain regions involved in memory, decision-making, and visual processing, along with more signs of damage in the brain’s white matter. Surprisingly, sitting itself did not appear to be the main issue, since people who spent long hours seated at mentally engaging jobs often showed healthier brain patterns.
summary: A study of 1,700 adults found that frequent TV watching in midlife is associated with smaller brain regions involved in memory, decision-making, and visual processing. The research suggests that the link may be due to the type of activity rather than the amount of sitting itself.
author: Science Daily

title: Astronomers Discover Atmosphere on Rocky Planet in Habitable Zone
content: Astronomers have found the first confirmed atmosphere around a rocky planet in another star’s habitable zone. The planet, LHS 1140 b, revealed its atmosphere through helium slowly leaking into space. Located 48 light-years away, the world may have preserved its atmosphere for billions of years, making it a promising target in the search for potentially habitable planets.
summary: Astronomers have confirmed the presence of an atmosphere around the rocky planet LHS 1140 b, located 48 light-years from Earth. The atmosphere is believed to be preserved due to slow helium leakage into space.

Researchers found that its people were largely descended from local Yellow River farming communities, but also had genetic ties to distant southern and steppe populations, pointing to extensive prehistoric contact.
summary: Researchers have extracted ancient DNA from the 4,000-year-old Shimao settlement in China, shedding light on the origins of its inhabitants. The findings indicate that the people of Shimao had genetic ties to local farming communities and distant populations from southern and steppe regions.

title: A touchscreen and light make the new X4 Pro the best version of Xteink’s tiny e-readers
content:
Xteink's Latest E-Reader, the X4 Pro, Brings Touchscreen and Lighting to the Table

Xteink has unveiled its latest e-reader, the X4 Pro, which boasts a range of upgrades over its predecessors, including a touchscreen and built-in lighting. While the device's hardware has been improved, the software still lags behind, making navigation and usage a tad frustrating. However, a glimmer of hope lies in the form of the CrossPoint Reader software, which will be available at launch and promises to vastly improve the user experience.

The X4 Pro features a 4.26-inch, 800 x 480 E Ink screen, making it an extremely pocketable device that is slightly smaller and thinner than Xteink's first e-reader. The addition of a touchscreen has simplified navigation, and the device now feels more intuitive to use. The screen light is another significant upgrade, allowing users to read in bed without the need for a lamp. However, the software still has room for improvement, with issues such as inconsistent touchscreen sensitivity and limited font options.

Despite its limitations, the X4 Pro remains the best tiny e-reader on the market, thanks in part to the upcoming release of the CrossPoint Reader software. This free firmware alternative will provide a more polished user experience and is set to be compatible with all of Xteink's future devices. With a price tag of $99, the X4 Pro is a worthwhile investment for those prioritizing portability and a more enjoyable reading experience.
summary: A touchscreen and light make the new X4 Pro the best version of Xteink’s tiny e-readers.

title: France to ban social media for children under 15
content:
French lawmakers are set to vote on a bill on July 21 that would prohibit children under 15 from accessing social‑media platforms. The proposed legislation would extend France’s regulatory reach to the same services that are already restricted in Australia, where a ban on users under 16 for Facebook, Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube took effect in December.

The French measure follows growing concerns about the mental‑health and safety implications of early exposure to online content. By aligning with Australia’s precedent, the bill aims to curb the influence of social media on minors while providing a legal framework for parental control and platform compliance.

If passed, France would become the second country after Australia to impose a statutory age limit on social‑media use, signalling a broader international trend toward stricter protection of young users in the digital age.
summary: French lawmakers are expected to approve a bill on July 21 that would prohibit social media access for users under 15. The measure would make France the latest country to follow Australia’s December ban on platforms for under‑16s.

title: Meta Smartglasses Could Enable Covert Child Filming
content: The company argues that it’s for individuals to ensure they don’t ‘actively exploit’ this technology. That won’t keep children safeIt took me a while to realise what the man sitting next to me on the train was doing. He was flicking through pictures of a little girl on his phone; zooming in on some, cropping the images. Hardly unusual, of course, except that on closer inspection the pictures were very clearly of the toddler sitting opposite us, playing with her parents. On a crowded train of people mostly staring obliviously at our own phones, a stranger had been covertly photographing that little girl over and over again. And if it hadn’t been for that very visible phone screen giving him away, he wouldn’t have been caught. That encounter was a while ago but my memory was jogged last week listening to a clip of Meta’s VP of wearables, Alex Himel, talk fondly to the BBC about using his new smartglasses to film his daughter singing in a talent contest. They let him capture the memory without having to watch her through a screen, he said, freeing him to be “kind of living in the moment, head up and hands free”. So far, so sweet. But what about the risk of creeps potentially using them to film other people’s daughters covertly, heads up and hands free? Meta’s smartglasses have a tiny flashing warning light on the frame to indicate when the wearer is recording, but the technology is still new enough that many people don’t think to look for it. And in the age of AI, stolen images of children matter. Taken in real life or scraped from the internet, they’re the raw material for generating realistic-looking child abuse material of the most extreme and disturbing kind. title: Open-Source Index Maps Museum Artifacts' Origins and Destinations
content:
A new open‑source platform called ex‑situ is mapping museum artefacts as connecting arcs between their places of origin and the institutions that hold them. Developed by designer‑developer H. Burakyel, the project began as a Master’s thesis in 2022 and has since grown to index more than 100,000 objects from eight major collections, including the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Victoria & Albert Museum, and the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin. The system uses a flat data model to avoid imposing institutional taxonomies, and it stores only URLs to original images, keeping the responsibility for content with the source institutions. The front‑end is built with Next.js and Deck.gl, the back‑end uses Strapi, and a Python ETL pulls data from museum open‑access APIs. A recent addition allows researchers to export provenance data for filtered sets of artefacts.

The platform’s design emphasizes an “origin‑first” search interface that reveals the historical journey of objects, linking Western and Euro‑American collections with their original sites in the Middle East, Asia, Africa, and the Americas. By treating the index as a connective tissue rather than a hoster, ex‑situ avoids duplicating institutional data and instead directs users straight to the source. The project is released under AGPL‑3.0 and is available on GitHub, with a live demo accessible at exsitu.com. Burakyel has expressed a need for community input on scaling performance, code contributions, and data pipelines for museums lacking open‑access APIs.
summary: Open-Source Index Maps Museum Artifacts' Origins and Destinations.

title: University of Illinois opens 64-acre Alma Mater Plots for long-term crop research
content:
A few miles south of the main quad at the University of Illinois Urbana‑Champaign, researchers have begun the Alma Mater Plots, an unprecedented agricultural experiment comprising 64 individually tile‑drained one‑acre (0.4‑hectare) fields. The scale and design make it the largest tile‑drained plot network of its kind in the United States, positioning the university as a hub for large‑scale field research.

Scientists are working closely with regional farmers to determine the specific crops and management practices to be tested, aiming to generate data that directly benefits Illinois and Midwest agriculture. By aligning experimental priorities with growers’ needs, the project seeks to improve productivity, sustainability, and resilience across the Corn Belt, offering a valuable resource for both academic inquiry and practical farming applications.
summary: The University of Illinois Urbana‑Champaign has created the Alma Mater Plots, a collection of 64 one‑acre tile‑drained fields that represent the largest agricultural experiment of its type. Researchers are working with Midwest farmers to select the crops and practices that will be studied over the next 150 years.

title: A pioneer and a superstar, Kevin Keegan’s achievements were extraordinary
content: The former England manager may be remembered by many for his ‘I’d love it’ rant in 1996, but that should not obscure the remarkable nature of his football careerKevin Keegan, who has died aged 75, is the only British player to win the Ballon d’Or twice, was the star of Liverpool’s first European Cup-winning team, a messianic figure at Newcastle United as a player and coach, forging a team so memorable that Fifa’s president wrote to commend him, and was the captain and then manager of the England men’s national team. And yet, as Keegan would ruefully reflect, he will principally be remembered by many for an emotional outburst that precipitated Newcastle’s historic failure in a Premier League title race, a TV interview which presaged the coming era of the modern game. Keegan’s “I’d love it” rant of April 1996, directed at Alex Ferguson, became a meme before the modern meaning of the word and social media even existed, repeatedly played on Sky Sports and becoming indelibly marked in the minds of multiple generations, many not even born when it occurred. It frequently tops polls as the most memorable moment in Premier League history and foreshadowed an era where digital clips and personality narratives would dominate football coverage. Continue reading...
summary: A pioneer and a superstar, Kevin Keegan’s achievements were extraordinary.

title: Scientists Develop New Method to Study Protein Folding in Living Cells
content: Protein aggregates are associated with the development of diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. These are found more often in certain areas of cells known as membraneless organelles. Do these organelles promote this protein clumping, or do they protect the cell by temporarily absorbing the aggregates? Professor Simon Ebbinghaus and Mailin Becker from Ruhr University Bochum, Germany, set out to answer this question with their new, self-developed method, "confocal Fast Relaxation Imaging," or cFReI. They report their findings in the journal PRX Life.
summary: Researchers at Ruhr University Bochum in Germany have created a new imaging technique, "confocal Fast Relaxation Imaging," to measure protein folding in living membraneless organelles. The study aims to understand the role of these organelles in protein aggregation, which is linked to diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's.

title: Scientists Discover Mechanism Behind Eukaryotic Single-Celled Organisms' Magnetic Sense
content: How do microorganisms orient themselves to find the optimal habitat? Scientists have thoroughly investigated so-called magnetotactic bacteria, which use the Earth's magnetic field as a biological compass. Some eukaryotic single-celled organisms—that is, more complex organisms like ciliates, which, unlike bacteria, have a cell nucleus—also possess this capability. But how they acquire it has largely remained a puzzle.
summary: Scientists have been studying how eukaryotic single-celled organisms develop their magnetic sense, a biological compass that helps them navigate their environment. Research has shown that some of these organisms, such as ciliates, possess this capability, but the underlying mechanism of how they acquire it has been unclear.

title: Cells Use Rapid Protein-Control System to Survive Heat
content: The planet is getting hotter, and life will need to adapt to rising temperatures to survive. One way cells adapt to changing conditions is by synthesizing new proteins. That works well when the environment changes slowly, but if a crisis hits, like a sudden temperature increase, cells cannot wait for new proteins to be built. Instead, cells rely on chemical modifications that can rapidly turn proteins on or off, similar to how a light can be turned on or off without having to buy or throw away a bulb each time.
summary: Cells adapt to changing conditions by synthesizing new proteins or using chemical modifications to turn existing proteins on or off. When faced with sudden temperature increases, cells rely on rapid chemical modifications to control proteins, as synthesizing new proteins takes too long.

title: LG Monitors Auto-Install McAfee Ads on Windows PCs
content:
LG’s UltraGear 34GX900A‑B monitor has been found to install LG’s own software automatically on Windows 11 PCs. A video from Gamers Nexus shows that, upon first connecting the monitor to a new computer, Windows Update silently downloads LG driver updates and the LG Monitor App Installer without prompting the user for permission or displaying a notification.

The installer does not provide any direct control interface; instead it simply redirects users to LG’s suite of applications and, in several cases, to McAfee antivirus. Reports of this behavior date back to 2024, and recent complaints on Reddit highlight intrusive pop‑up ads that appear in the bottom‑right corner of the screen, promoting both LG and McAfee products. The Verge has reported on the issue, noting that LG has not yet issued a formal response.

While the auto‑installation may be intended to keep drivers current, the lack of user consent and the promotion of third‑party software raise concerns about privacy and user experience. Users of the 34GX900A‑B and similar models are advised to monitor Windows Update behavior and consider disabling automatic driver installations if they wish to avoid unexpected software installs.
summary: LG's 34GX900A-B monitors silently install the LG Monitor App Installer through Windows Update without user permission, directing users to LG and McAfee apps. The issue, reported since 2024, was confirmed by Gamers Nexus with user complaints of pop-up ads.

title: PlayStation replica ornament released with three coin batteries included
content:
A recent piece from The Verge highlights the technical intricacies behind the familiar PlayStation boot sequence and the personal challenges that can arise with older hardware. The iconic startup sound is actually a multi‑part chime that begins with a synth‑driven section announcing “Sony Computer Entertainment” on a white background. The familiar echoing chimes and the color‑filled PlayStation logo only play once the console successfully reads the disc, a step that can be thwarted by hardware faults.

The article recounts a user’s experience with a malfunctioning disc spindle, which had disassembled early in the console’s life. As an eight‑year‑old, the owner attempted a risky repair by supergluing the spindle, a makeshift fix that illustrates the limited DIY resources available at the time. The piece also notes that the accompanying ornament—likely a decorative item related to the console—requires three 1.5‑volt coin batteries, which are included in the box.

In closing, the story underscores how seemingly minor hardware issues can interrupt the nostalgic ritual of starting a PlayStation, while also reminding readers of the practical steps—such as battery replacement and spindle repair—needed to keep older systems operational.
summary: The decorative PlayStation replica ornament comes with three 1.5‑volt coin batteries in the box. When powered, it plays the console’s signature multi‑part boot chime.

title: SpaceX added to Nasdaq-100 and its effect on index funds
content:
Index funds, which track broad market indices rather than individual securities, have long been regarded as a low‑risk investment vehicle for retirement accounts and other long‑term portfolios. The Nasdaq‑100, a capitalization‑weighted index of the 100 largest non‑financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, is a common benchmark for many such funds. Recent developments have seen SpaceX, the aerospace firm founded by Elon Musk, fast‑tracked for inclusion in the Nasdaq‑100 ahead of its anticipated $1.77 trillion initial public offering, prompting questions about the potential impact on funds that replicate the index.

Analysts note that the mechanics of index fund construction mitigate the risk of a single company’s volatility affecting overall fund performance. Because the Nasdaq‑100 is weighted by market capitalization, SpaceX’s addition will proportionally increase the fund’s exposure to the aerospace sector without fundamentally altering the index’s diversification. Consequently, the inclusion of a high‑profile, potentially overvalued stock is unlikely to destabilize the broader index or jeopardize retirement savings that rely on these funds. The situation underscores the importance of understanding how index methodologies distribute risk across constituent holdings.
summary: SpaceX has been included in the Nasdaq-100 index, causing index funds that track the Nasdaq-100 to hold its shares. The inclusion is not expected to significantly destabilize those index funds.

title: Senegal backs former president Macky Sall for UN Secretary‑General candidacy
content:

The decision marks a reversal of an earlier position in which officials had refused to endorse Sall, citing allegations of political repression and human‑rights violations during his 2012‑2022 tenure.

The shift followed Sall’s weekend visit to Dakar, during which he met with President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and other senior officials. Government spokespersons said the meeting clarified Sall’s commitment to multilateralism and addressed prior concerns, prompting the endorsement. Senegal’s backing adds another African voice to the expected field of candidates, though the final selection will be made by the UN General Assembly after a recommendation from the Security Council.
summary: The Senegalese government announced it will support former president Macky Sall’s bid to replace UN Secretary‑General Antonio Guterres. title: Spain's Prime Minister Sanchez visits Algeria to restore diplomatic ties
content:

The trip is aimed at repairing diplomatic relations that have been strained since 2022, when Madrid abandoned its long‑standing neutrality on the Western Sahara dispute and publicly supported Morocco’s claim to the territory, a move that provoked strong criticism from Algiers.

The diplomatic thaw began last year after Algeria reinstated a friendship treaty it had suspended over the same issue, signaling a willingness to re‑engage. Sanchez’s visit is expected to focus on restoring bilateral cooperation and addressing lingering tensions stemming from the Western Sahara row, with both governments indicating a desire to move beyond the dispute toward broader collaboration.
summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez visited Algeria on Monday, his first trip there in four years. The visit aims to repair relations strained after Spain supported Morocco's claim over Western Sahara, a dispute that led Algeria to suspend a friendship treaty which it reactivated last year.

title: Shania Twain Releases Seventh Album 'Little Miss Twain'
content: (Republic Nashville)The country legend’s seventh album revisits her troubled early life but plays it safe with zany humour and fluffy songs about young love‘When I was a kid, I started on stages just like this,” Shania Twain told the 200 fans sardined into a London pub back in June, trailing her seventh album Little Miss Twain. A reintroduction to the Canadian country legend, the record mines memories from her Ontario childhood for hints of the arena-filling star she would soon become. Over wistful Mellotron and pedal steel, the title track marvels at little Eilleen, as she was called back then, escaping the rural north and making it big in Nashville. Yet, somehow, it all feels inevitable – as if Twain’s career was conjured into being by the conviction of her mother, who drove her to those tiny bars in a beaten-up Chevy. And yes, from the vantage point of 2026, it’s difficult to imagine it going any other way. Twain’s icon status is certified by five Grammys and the way her free-spirited hits have become karaoke classics – not to mention the fact that her 1997 album Come on Over remains the highest-selling studio album by any female artist in history. Continue reading...
summary: Shania Twain's seventh album, 'Little Miss Twain', revisits her early life in Ontario, Canada, and features a mix of country and rootsy influences. title: Matilda' Film Adaptation Celebrates Themes of Justice and Triumph
content: The latest in our series of writers picking their most meaningful comfort watches is a tribute to the inspiring power of the 1996 Roald Dahl adaptationWhen I think about what makes me feel good, it isn’t fantasy or escapism; it’s justice, morality and triumph – sizing up to a bully bigger than you and prevailing against the odds. I never fail to be charmed by the story of an underdog, someone who shouldn’t win but finds a way through resilience, determination or sometimes a genius loophole and a little bit of magic, and no film hits those attributes harder for me than Danny DeVito’s Matilda. The zany adaptation of Roald Dahl’s 1988 children’s novel came out in cinemas in December 1996, four months after I came into the world. The film, set (unlike the supremely British source text) in a leopard-print-clad edition of suburban California, focuses on the titular character (played by Mara Wilson), who grows up unseen and unheard by her grifter, TV-obsessed parents, Harry and Zinnia Wormwood, played by DeVito and his then-wife Rhea Perlman. Continue reading...
summary: The 1996 film adaptation of Roald Dahl's 'Matilda' tells the story of a young girl who stands up to her neglectful and abusive parents, using her intelligence and determination to overcome adversity. The movie, directed by Danny DeVito, stars Mara Wilson as the titular character and DeVito as her father, Harry Wormwood.

title: Rodri's Performance Key to Spain's World Cup Success
content: Much of what Rodri does is indefinable – his great skill is simply being, existing in the right spacesYou don’t need to be long in the US before somebody, finding you’re here to cover “the Fifa” as so many Americans so demoralisingly call it, will tell you that the USA would obviously win it all the time if only their best athletes weren’t distracted by more local pursuits: American football, basketball, eating enormous sandwiches and the like. If you’re really lucky they’ll start shouting names at you with a detailed rundown of height, weight, sprint speed, what they can bench and other fascinating statistics. At which you wonder whether the 5ft 7in Lionel Messi has ever done a bench press. Rodri probably has, but he’s still nobody’s idea of a great athlete. He’s tall without being physically imposing. He’s not quick. He ambles about games being in the right place. Occasionally he leans into people or passes the ball 10 yards. It would be difficult to put together a highlights reel of his performance in the World Cup final that would convince a neophyte that he was the defining player – but he was, and was rightly named player of the tournament as well. title: Louisiana Weakens Air Monitoring Amid Industry Pressure
content: Lawmakers weakened community air monitoring as industry pushed back against greater scrutinyKimbrelle Kyereh lives just a few hundred feet from the massive chemical storage tanks in St Rose, in south-eastern Louisiana. Oily fumes sometimes drift into her home, bringing headaches, nausea and insomnia. On one such night, she grabbed her son at 3am and fled to an all-night Ihop. In 2023, after years of coping with the noxious odors, Kyereh began collecting air samples in her yard for a local environmental justice group. But soon after, Louisiana passed an industry-backed law that sharply restricted how that kind of data could be used. Ten of Louisiana’s heaviest air-polluting facilities, based on self-reported data shared with the EPA, operate without a single public air monitor within five miles. This list includes Dow Chemical’s plastics factory in Plaquemine, which is about eight miles from the nearest air monitoring station. The station measures only ozone even though the plant releases an array of toxic pollutants including ethylene oxide, a known carcinogen. No public monitors measure ammonia – despite the fact that CF Industries’ Donaldsonville plant emits more than 7m lb of the hazardous chemical each year, according to EPA data. The three chemicals that researchers have concluded “together account for the large majority of total cancer risk” in the area – ethylene oxide, chloroprene and formaldehyde – aren’t monitored by the state at all. Continue reading...
summary: Louisiana lawmakers passed a law restricting the use of community air monitoring data in 2023, which was backed by industry groups. The state lacks public air monitors near several heavily polluting facilities, including Dow Chemical's plastics factory and CF Industries' Donaldsonville plant.

title: Endothelial cells aid immune response to cancer metastases
content: It has long been suspected that endothelial cells, the specialized cells lining the inner walls of blood vessels, play a key role in determining how the body's immune system responds to tumors. Researchers at the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) in Heidelberg and the Medical Faculty Mannheim of Heidelberg University have now identified, in mouse studies, a specialized population of blood vessel lining endothelial cells that enable an effective immune defense against cancer metastases in the liver. The findings could pave the way for novel combination therapies for cancer.

Their results matched both theoretical predictions and simulations performed with a quantum computer. The method could open new paths for exploring quantum dynamics and materials.

title: Hollywood Press Tours Shift Towards More Light-Hearted and Gimmicky Approach
content: From playing would you rather to ranking snacks, A-listers navigating the promo trail are now forced on a set schedule of sillinessThis summer, we’ve been blessed with new movies from the legendary director Steven Spielberg and one of his biggest and most beloved successors, Christopher Nolan. In both cases, the movies have been heavily sold on the directors’ names, and, befitting two of the most famous film-makers to ever do it, Spielberg and Nolan have been making the press rounds. This has meant a wealth of interviews and insights – a bonus feature unfolding alongside the selling of the actual movies that will delight movie nerds the world over. So at first, when I saw a 60-second video of Christopher Nolan answering a barrage of yes-or-no questions come across my social-media feed, of course I stopped and watched as a famously buttoned-up (if obviously still passionate) film-maker attempted some spontaneity with no danger of follow-up questions (or obligation to follow-up answers). From this, there is admittedly plenty of information to be gleaned: he has no designs on retiring, Tarantino-style. He will not make another superhero movie or a TV show. He’s fine with people watching movies on their phones or laptops. He will neither confirm nor deny that Interstellar is his favorite of his films. He will also neither confirm nor deny that he would like to make a Star Wars movie. (Perhaps the most intriguing, given that you’d rather expect that to be a firm “no”.) Continue reading...
summary: A-listers, including Christopher Nolan and Steven Spielberg, have been participating in promotional activities with a focus on lighter and more entertaining content. title: Global rise in sadistic online exploitation of children reported
content: Global increase in cases of predators coercing children to harm themselves or produce child sexual abuse materialCases of predators coercing children into producing sexual photos and videos of themselves have surged globally in the past year, a cruel phenomenon known as “sadistic online exploitation”, child safety experts and law enforcement officials warn. In cases of sadistic online exploitation, perpetrators target vulnerable teens on social media platforms and online games. These predators then compel their victims into producing child sexual abuse material (CSAM), harming themselves and others, or, in extreme cases, attempting suicide. In the US, call or text the Childhelp abuse hotline on 800-422-4453 or visit their website for more resources and to report child abuse or DM for help. For adult survivors of child abuse, help is available at ascasupport. Org. In the UK, the NSPCC offers support to children on 0800 1111, and adults concerned about a child on 0808 800 5000. The National Association for People Abused in Childhood (Napac) offers support for adult survivors on 0808 801 0331. In Australia, children, young adults, parents and teachers can contact the Kids Helpline on 1800 55 1800, or Bravehearts on 1800 272 831, and adult survivors can contact Blue Knot Foundation on 1300 657 380. Other sources of help can be found at Child Helplines International Continue reading...
summary: Cases of predators coercing children to create sexual images and videos have increased worldwide over the past year. Child safety experts and law enforcement officials warn that this exploitation is targeting vulnerable teens on social media and online gaming platforms.

Their shows blend avant‑garde techniques with cultural references, underscoring the genre’s role as a mirror for societal fears and hopes.

The curated lineup reaffirms Haute Couture’s enduring relevance, demonstrating how its distinct French heritage continues to inspire international designers to explore new aesthetic and thematic territories while maintaining the meticulous standards that define the craft.

title: Daily Caffeine Intake Linked to Heart Health

We urgently need a plan to navigate the ethical implicationsIn January, the AI company Anthropic published a new constitution for Claude, its most advanced large language model (LLM), which contained the comment: “We are caught in a difficult position where we neither want to overstate the likelihood of Claude’s moral patienthood nor dismiss it out of hand.” A month later, Anthropic’s CEO Dario Amodei went on a podcast and said his company couldn’t rule out the possibility that Claude was conscious. Philosopher David Chalmers, who coined the phrase “the hard problem of consciousness”, has said there is a significant chance of conscious LLMs within a decade. And what about Claude itself? When asked during testing to estimate the probability that it is a moral patient, meaning that its wellbeing matters in its own right, it gave numbers ranging from 5% to 40% and stressed how uncertain it was. Modern AI systems are extraordinarily complex, and they are advancing fast. In terms of structural complexity and computational scale, by some measures a few are already in the range of a mouse brain, and at recent growth rates, they could reach the range of a human brain within five to 10 years. Continue reading...
summary: Experts consider potential consciousness in AI models.

title: 50 Years After Viking 1 Landed on Mars, NASA's Findings Revisited
content:
The latest newsletter opens with a reflection on scientific progress, noting that recent breakthroughs often stem from recognising overlooked details rather than discovering entirely new phenomena. It then turns to current political and international developments, highlighting a mix of domestic policy shifts and global security events that shape the present landscape.

In the United Kingdom, Labour leader Andy Burnham is set to replace Keir Starmer as prime minister, with plans to cancel the digital ID card scheme and redirect funds toward cost‑of‑living measures. Meanwhile, the country’s political scene is also marked by the resignation of Hungary’s president, Tamás Sulyok, following a constitutional amendment approved by the ruling party. Internationally, Russia launched a large‑scale ballistic missile attack on Kyiv, causing casualties and widespread damage, while the United States intensified strikes on Iran after the death of an American service member. In Africa, seven U.S. aid workers quarantined in Kenya after the U.S. government imposed travel restrictions amid an Ebola outbreak. The United Nations and other international bodies are also active: a New York court will hear the third session of former Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro on “narco‑terrorism” charges, and the International Criminal Court is set to vote on whether to dismiss prosecutor Karim Khan amid allegations of sexual misconduct.

These events underscore a world in flux, where scientific insight, domestic policy, and international security intersect. The newsletter’s concise overview provides readers with a snapshot of the most pressing issues—from Mars exploration milestones to geopolitical tensions—highlighting the interconnectedness of progress and vigilance in the contemporary era.

title: England Secure Back-to-Back Wins with Feyi-Waboso's Impact
content:
England Secures Back-to-Back Wins, but Ill Discipline Persists

In a highly energetic and dramatic match against Argentina, England emerged victorious with a 31-24 win, claiming their first back-to-back Test victories since November. The standout performance was undoubtedly that of fly-half Manny Feyi-Waboso, who has cemented his status as a genuine world-beater. Feyi-Waboso's exceptional skill and playmaking abilities were instrumental in England's success, and his contributions have undoubtedly lifted the team's overall performance.

However, despite this notable achievement, England's ongoing disciplinary issues remain a pressing concern. The team has accumulated 14 yellow cards in 10 games this year, a worrying trend that continues to plague their campaign. Fly-half Fin Smith, known for his candid and forthright analysis, has expressed his frustration with the team's inability to break this habit. Smith's comments serve as a stark reminder that England still have a long way to go in terms of reaching their full potential.

As the season draws to a close, England's coaches and players will need to address their ill discipline and work on developing a more cohesive and disciplined team culture. With a talented player like Feyi-Waboso at the helm, there is no reason why England cannot achieve greater success. But until they can overcome their recurring disciplinary issues, their progress will remain hindered.
summary: England secured a 31-24 win over Argentina, their first back-to-back Test victories since November, with Manny Feyi-Waboso making a significant impact on the team. The win, however, was overshadowed by England's ongoing disciplinary issues, with four yellow cards taken in the game.

title: 5.5‑Magnitude Earthquake in Peru Kills at Least Five
content:
A 5.5‑magnitude earthquake struck the Andes region of Peru on Saturday night, killing at least five people, injuring more than 20 and displacing roughly 300 residents, officials said Sunday. The tremor’s epicenter was located 2 km (1.2 miles) west‑south‑west of the town of Sicaya in Huancayo province, at a depth of 10 km (6.2 miles), according to the U.S. Geological Survey.

Emergency crews were dispatched to the affected area after the quake, which occurred at 9:24 p.m. local time, caused several buildings to collapse and left many families without shelter. Local authorities are coordinating rescue operations and providing temporary accommodation for those displaced, while medical teams treat the injured. The incident underscores the region’s vulnerability to seismic activity, and officials have urged residents to remain vigilant for aftershocks as recovery efforts continue.
summary: A 5.5‑magnitude earthquake struck the Andes region of Peru on Saturday night, with its epicenter 2 km west‑south‑west of Sicaya in Huancayo province at a depth of 10 km. The quake killed at least five people, injured more than 20 and left about 300 residents displaced.

title: The Clapper Smart Home Gadget
content:
The Clapper, a voice‑activated switch that became a viral household gadget, has been the subject of a new episode of Version History on The Verge. The show traces the product’s evolution from its original name, The Great American Turn‑On, to its eventual launch alongside one of advertising’s most iconic campaigns. Despite early reliability issues—users reported the device sometimes failed to respond or even fried nearby electronics—the Clapper’s simple, hands‑free appeal helped it capture a sizable market.

In the episode, The Verge’s David Pierce and Victoria Song interview Allison Marsh, a former product manager who helped steer the Clapper from prototype to mass‑market release. Marsh explains how the team addressed the device’s erratic behavior, refining its sensitivity algorithms and improving power management to reduce the risk of overheating. She also discusses the strategic partnership with a major advertising agency that produced a memorable commercial, which played a key role in turning the Clapper into a pop‑culture phenomenon.

The segment concludes by noting the Clapper’s legacy: it sparked a wave of smart‑home accessories that prioritize convenience over complexity, and it remains a case study in how a quirky, imperfect product can achieve mainstream success through effective marketing and iterative design.
summary: The Clapper was a smart home gadget that often malfunctioned and could damage devices. It became a viral sensation despite its flaws, thanks in part to a successful advertising campaign.

title: Meta AI glasses raise privacy concerns as celebrities promote them
content:
Meta Platforms has introduced a new line of AI‑enabled smart glasses that incorporate a suite of safety features marketed to protect users from unwanted recording. The devices, which integrate health‑tracking sensors, smartphone notifications and voice‑activated controls, are positioned as an evolution of wearable technology for everyday use. According to Meta, built‑in alerts and privacy safeguards are intended to notify wearers when the glasses are actively recording, and to allow users to disable cameras or microphones with a single gesture.

Critics, particularly women's advocacy groups, have highlighted persistent privacy and safety concerns, noting that the presence of discreet recording equipment could be exploited in public spaces such as bars, streets or transit hubs. Reports suggest that the technology may enable covert surveillance, potentially compromising personal agency and increasing the risk of non‑consensual filming. As the devices move toward commercial release, regulators and consumer‑rights organizations are calling for clearer guidelines and stronger enforcement mechanisms to address these privacy challenges.
summary: Meta has released AI-powered smart glasses that can record video and audio. Critics say the devices pose privacy risks, especially for women, while celebrities such as Kylie Jenner have endorsed the product.

title: Emma Hayes praises Spain's collective culture after semi-final win over France
content:
Spain’s semi‑final win over France at the World Cup has been described by analysts as a triumph of collective play over individual flair. The Spanish side advanced by exploiting shared spatial awareness and timing, rather than relying on the star power of players such as Rodri, Lamine Yamal, or Pedri. Their performance has been framed as evidence of a long‑term culture that prioritises teamwork and positional understanding.

Key to Spain’s success was the midfield’s ability to create numerical superiority in critical zones. By maintaining a disciplined shape, the team generated repeated four‑versus‑two advantages, allowing them to control the tempo and dictate the flow of the game. This approach, rooted in training from a young age, emphasises mastery of time and space, enabling the squad to adapt to opponents’ tactics while preserving cohesion across all positions.

With the final set for Sunday, commentators point to Spain’s collective methodology as the foundation for their projected success. The nation’s emphasis on coordinated movement and shared responsibilities is expected to give them a strategic edge, reinforcing their reputation as one of the most exceptional teams in modern football.

title: England defeats Argentina 31-24 in controversial finale

England secured a 31‑24 victory over Argentina in a match that saw the visitors score five tries while the hosts were denied a late comeback by a TMO decision.
