title: Startup creates real-time AI tutor for children aged 4‑9
content:
A startup has announced the completion of an AI‑driven tutoring platform designed for children aged four to nine, offering instruction in reading, mathematics, English as a second language and additional subjects. The developers highlighted that creating an effective educational dialogue required a redesign of the conventional tool‑use loop, leading to the construction of a custom “tutor harness” that combines a streaming interpreter for real‑time action execution with an asynchronous planner model that anticipates conversational steps and initiates learning‑focused calls. The system is also equipped with a safety layer that evaluates each interaction without disrupting the flow of the lesson, aiming to ensure that instructional decisions are made at the optimal moment rather than merely providing rapid answers.

The team described the platform as a response to the broader challenge of integrating artificial intelligence responsibly into early childhood education, emphasizing that the architecture balances responsiveness, pedagogical relevance, and safety. The announcement, posted on Hacker News, has attracted considerable attention, with the discussion thread receiving over 60 points and dozens of comments seeking technical clarification and offering critical feedback. The developers indicated openness to further input from the community as they continue to refine the tutor’s capabilities.
summary: The team spent the past year building an AI tutor that teaches reading, math and ESL to kids aged 4‑9 using a streaming interpreter and asynchronous planner to make real‑time decisions. A safety system checks every interaction without interrupting the conversation flow.

content: OpenAI's Fidji Simo is departing her full-time role as the company's AGI chief and is transitioning to being a "part-time advisor," she said on X. title: ‘A counter-narrative of history’: Schomburg Center’s 100 years of celebrating Black culture
content: A Puerto Rico-born New Yorker’s relentless collecting on the African diaspora is still the core of a Harlem institutionGrowing up in Puerto Rico in the late 19th century, Arturo Alfonso Schomburg was told by his teacher that Black people had no significant history or accomplishments. He spent his life disproving the narrative by collecting art, books and artefacts that showed the opposite. At 17 years old, Schomburg settled in New York, where he used his collections to write articles about Black history for periodicals such as Negro World. In time, he became known as a pre-eminent historian and intellectual of the Harlem Renaissance.“Schomburg always sought to collect the global Black experience,” said Barrye Brown, curator of manuscripts, archives and rare books at the Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture. “When you look at what he was collecting, you see his vision of what the African diaspora is like … it is all around the world, it’s multilingual; there’s so many different experiences represented.” Continue reading...
summary: ‘A counter-narrative of history’: Schomburg Center’s 100 years of celebrating Black culture.

title: England secure T20 series win against India with dominant performance
content: Fourth T20i: England, 159-1 beat India, 158-6, by 9 wicketsBrook scores 79, Salt 59 to win with six overs remainingEngland’s recent heatwave continued in Bristol, India wilting to lose their cool, the game and the series in what turned into another bizarrely one-sided encounter. Timid with the bat, poor in the field, error-prone with the ball and swift to accept the inevitability of defeat, this was a complete horror show from the world champions and a performance of complete dominance from Harry Brook’s burgeoning team, who won by nine wickets and will overtake their opponents as world No1 if they win the final game of the series in Southampton on Saturday. Two days earlier it was England’s bowlers who shredded their opponents on their way to a 125-run win at Trent Bridge. This time, well as their bowlers performed to limit India to 159, it was their batters – and one of them in particular. Chasing an obviously under-par total, England started slowly and awkwardly and Jos Buttler was dismissed early for eight – the former captain’s form is a genuine issue, and he has not scored an international half-century in this format since the Old Trafford runfest against South Africa last September, a run of 18 innings in which he has averaged just 15.16. But his departure brought out his successor, Brook scooped his second ball for six, and from that moment there was no stopping him. Continue reading...
summary: England won the fourth T20I against India by 9 wickets, securing a series victory with a dominant performance that saw them chase down a target of 159. Harry Brook top-scored for England with 79 runs, while Phil Salt contributed 59 runs to help his team win with six overs remaining.

title: GitHub Insights Tool Devthropology Offers Detailed Codebase Analysis
content:
New Tool Analyzes GitHub Data to Provide Deeper Insights into Codebases

A new project called Devthropology has been launched, offering a unique perspective on GitHub data. Built on top of GitHub pull request data, Devthropology aims to provide faster performance, more detail, and a focus on how work moves through a codebase. The tool's main entity is a contributor, which can be viewed from two sides: authoring pull requests and reviewing or giving feedback to others. This allows users to see repository-wide statistics, user interactions, contribution trends, file health, and collaboration patterns.

The tool offers a range of features, including a homepage that provides a high-level summary of the repository, a file explorer that builds a graph of files to track renames and moves, and a trends page that showcases the velocity of contributions and the impact of AI on shipping code. The relationships page displays a graph of interactions between contributors, weighted by PR activity, while the contributors page allows users to search for contributors and view their lifetime metrics. Additionally, the author/reviewer reports page provides a handful of metrics showing the performance of a contributor from both sides of a PR.

Devthropology has been built out of curiosity and a desire to see different insights into codebases, with the goal of providing an improved GitHub Insights page. The project has been tested on a few demo repositories, which were selected for their patterns of smaller contributor sets and more activity per contributor. The developer behind Devthropology is seeking feedback and can be contacted via email at hey@devthropology.com.
summary: Devthropology is a GitHub-based tool that provides in-depth insights into codebases, including contributor activity, file health, and collaboration patterns. The tool offers a range of features, such as repository-wide stats, user interactions, and contribution trends, with the goal of improving code health and velocity in the AI era.

title: Google will now tell you if an ad was made with AI
content:
Google has rolled out a new feature to its "My Ad Center" platform, allowing users to identify ads that were created or edited using artificial intelligence. The update, announced on Thursday, adds a label under the "how this ad was made" tab, which can be accessed by tapping the three dots or info button on ads. This feature provides users with greater transparency into the advertising process, particularly in regards to the use of AI technology.

According to Google, the "created or edited with AI" label will be automatically applied to ads made using the company's own generative AI advertising tools. However, ads created with AI elsewhere will require manual labeling by the advertiser. This distinction acknowledges the varying degrees of AI involvement in ad creation, while still providing users with a clear understanding of the technology used in each ad. The new feature is part of Google's ongoing efforts to promote transparency and accountability in online advertising.

The introduction of this feature is seen as a significant step in regulating the use of AI in advertising, particularly as the technology continues to evolve and become more widespread. By providing users with more information about the ads they see, Google aims to promote a more informed and discerning online advertising experience.

title: Study finds 6‑9% of transmasculine people experience pregnancy
content: A recent review of published research provides some evidence that a small but noteworthy minority of transmasculine people (trans, nonbinary, and other gender-expansive people who were assigned female at birth) have pregnancies (6%–9%) and children (4%–9%), including after transition. The systematic review published in Acta Obstetricia et Gynecologica Scandinavica also found possibly higher miscarriage rates and very little evidence on postnatal depression rates in transmasculine people who became pregnant.
summary: The systematic review in Acta Obstetricia et Gynecologica Scandinavica reported that 6%–9% of transmasculine individuals have been pregnant and 4%–9% have children, including after transition. title: Most veterans and service members who die by firearm suicide never disclose their intent
content: Most veterans and U. S. Military service members who die by firearm suicide don't disclose their suicidal intentions in the month before their death, according to Rutgers researchers. Their study, published in The Journal of Crisis Intervention and Suicide Prevention, examined the patterns of 28,600 individuals with a history of military service who died by firearm suicide between 2013 and 2021. Using data from the National Violent Death Reporting System, researchers sought to understand how often service members and veterans communicated suicidal thoughts before their deaths, and when they did, whom they chose to tell.
summary: Most veterans and service members who die by firearm suicide never disclose their intent.

title: Meta Updates Smart Glasses to Disable Camera After Tampering
content:
Meta Updates Smart Glasses with Tamper Detection Feature

In response to growing concerns over user privacy, Meta has announced a software update for its smart glasses that will disable the camera when it detects tampering with the device's privacy LED light. The move comes as a result of public backlash over the company's smart glasses, with some users expressing dissatisfaction over the lack of robust security measures. The update is aimed at addressing the issue of modders who have been physically modifying the glasses to disable the LED light.

According to Meta, the new feature will trigger a camera shut-off when it detects that the privacy LED light has been tampered with or destroyed. This is a significant improvement over previous measures, which only prompted users to uncover the recording light when they blocked it with tape or other objects. The update is part of Meta's efforts to discourage tampering with the LED light, and it is expected to enhance user confidence in the device's security features.

The update is seen as a step in the right direction for Meta, which has faced criticism over its handling of user data and device security. By introducing a tamper detection feature, the company is demonstrating its commitment to protecting user privacy and addressing concerns over the misuse of its smart glasses technology.
summary: Meta has announced a software update for its smart glasses that will disable the camera if the privacy LED light is tampered with or destroyed. The update aims to prevent users from bypassing the light, which is designed to indicate when the camera is recording.

title: Brainstem neurons map whisker touch into object distance, reveals mouse study

title: Scientists Develop Quantum Control Method Using Tiny Carbon Rings
content: Quantum states can be precisely controlled with the help of tiny carbon rings measuring only a few nanometers in size. This is made possible by a class of rarely used electromagnetic dipoles called toroidal moments. Using computer simulations, physicists at Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg (MLU) have now found a way to generate and control these nanostructures without any loss. The findings are published in npj Computational Materials and create new opportunities for quantum computer technology.

This is the first study to examine the trustworthiness of AI faces created by the latest diffusion technology. It was led by Alexis McGuire, with Paul Taylor and Sophie Nightingale from Lancaster University, Maty Bohacek from Stanford University, and Hany Farid from the University of California, Berkeley.
summary: Researchers have found that images of faces created by artificial intelligence are viewed as more trustworthy than genuine faces, according to a study led by Lancaster University. title: New Sunlight-Powered Method Reduces Hazardous Oxidant Risk in Chemical Synthesis
content: Researchers at the University of Osaka developed a light-driven method for synthesizing Davis reagents that generates the hazardous oxidant mCPBA only on demand and consumes it immediately. Kinetic analysis showed no detectable accumulation of the oxidant, improving process safety. The reaction proceeds at room temperature in non-halogenated solvents and can use sunlight or LEDs, offering a safer, greener and scalable alternative for pharmaceutical-related synthesis. The work is published in the journal Green Chemistry.
summary: Researchers at the University of Osaka developed a light-driven method for synthesizing Davis reagents that generates the hazardous oxidant mCPBA on demand. This new method consumes the oxidant immediately, eliminating the risk of accumulation and improving process safety.

title: England cricket test spurs heat policy and willow tree planting initiative
content:
A century‑old oak that has long shaded the grounds of England’s most iconic cricket venues is now being used to safeguard the sport’s future. The tree, which has provided shade for players and spectators alike for hundreds of years, has been repurposed as part of a new heat‑mitigation strategy aimed at protecting the health and safety of those on the field during the sweltering summer months.

Late June’s heatwave forced a cascade of cancellations across the UK: horse races were called off, a temporary village was erected to give shade at the Wimbledon qualifiers, and school sports days and the national rounders tournament were all axed. At Trent Bridge, where England faced New Zealand in the third Test and Ben Stokes delivered a memorable final performance, the England and Wales Cricket Board activated its extreme‑heat policy. The board implemented measures to reduce exposure, including adjusted playing times and increased hydration breaks, to cope with temperatures that the historic open ground was not designed to handle.

The ECB’s swift response underscores a growing recognition that climate extremes will increasingly impact sporting events. By leveraging the natural shade of historic trees and instituting stricter heat‑management protocols, the board aims to preserve both player welfare and the integrity of the game in an era of rising temperatures.
summary: During the third Test between England and New Zealand at Trent Bridge, the ECB activated its extreme heat policy to safeguard players and fans. The board also announced a program to plant willow trees to provide shade for future matches.

title: Scottish Village Fears Loss of Properties and Green Land Over AI Datacentre Plans
content: Suspicions grow in Lanarkshire that local people have been misled on supposed benefits of the huge developmentRevealed: landmark Scottish AI project has no prospect of meeting renewables promiseWhat are Britain’s AI growth zones and are the plans feasible or ‘complete bunk’? The promise was that a Scottish community would be transformed by massive investment and empowered to chase “the jobs of the future”. Instead, local people in Lanarkshire fear they may have to sell their properties and lose green belt land because of the errors of a badly planned AI datacentre complex, even as those jobs and investments never arrive. title: Mars express captures dozens of dust devils in Mars valley
content: Dust devils are a regular feature on Mars. Just like those found on Earth, these mini whirlwinds form when parts of Mars are warmed by the sun, causing air above the surface to swirl upward and carry dust with it. But in Mars' lower gravity (38% that of Earth), these devils grow much larger, reaching up to 8 km (5 miles) in height and speeds of up to 45 meters per second (150 feet per second). They are also a major part of Mars' meteorological cycles, playing a key role in distributing dust across the planet.
summary: Mars express captures dozens of dust devils in Mars valley.

Her title defence is gaining momentum, and her victory over Pliskova is a significant step towards her goal of retaining her title. Swiatek's statement that "Today I felt like it was a normal day at the office" highlights her calm and collected approach to her game. Her confidence and skill are a potent combination, and she will be looking to build on this momentum as she progresses through the tournament. As the competition intensifies, Swiatek's ability to perform under pressure will be put to the test, but for now, she remains a strong contender for the title.

content: A pioneering food additive that can stop people from gaining weight has appeared on the EU's Novel Food List, indicating its safety for human consumers. It maximizes the known benefits of a high-fiber diet, helping people feel fuller for longer, with the aim of reducing the daily calorie surpluses that can drive long-term weight gain.

title: Bottlenose Dolphins in Adriatic Sea Rely on Trawlers for Food
content: Bottlenose dolphins in the Adriatic Sea are spending much of their time following trawlers to scavenge for food, scientists say. The Adriatic seabed has been plowed by bottom trawlers for decades, resulting in ecosystem damage. Many apex predators are no longer present there. Only bottlenose dolphins are left, and the frequency of their presence around fishing trawlers—up to 76% of the trawlers inspected by scientists off Marche, Italy, were followed by dolphins—suggests they may be struggling to hunt normally.
summary: Bottlenose dolphins in the Adriatic Sea are increasingly following trawlers to scavenge for food, according to scientists. This behavior suggests the dolphins may be struggling to hunt normally due to the damaged ecosystem caused by decades of bottom trawling.

title: Glaciers Transported Rocks Across the Alps 24,000 Years Ago

For the first time, researchers at the University of Lausanne (UNIL) have reconstructed the journeys of these giant rocks across the entire Alpine region using a simulation. The model makes it possible to visualize the paths taken by millions of rocks that helped shape today's landscapes.
summary: Researchers at the University of Lausanne used a simulation to reconstruct the journeys of giant rocks carried by ice across the Alpine region 24,000 years ago. The simulation visualizes the paths taken by millions of rocks that helped shape today's landscapes in the Swiss Alps.

title: New Musical 'CrazySexyCool' Brings TLC's Story to the Stage
content: CrazySexyCool, the celebrated playwright’s new show in DC, is a vibrant love letter to the hits and sisterhood of the R&B trioCrazySexyCool, an ambitious new musical about the visionary 90s trio TLC at Arena Stage in Washington DC, aspires to make good on its title and then some. Crammed with platinum sing-alongs and tabloid-chronicled plot twists, it follows the legendary girl group – Lisa “Left Eye” Lopes, Rozonda “Chilli” Thomas and Tionne “T-Boz” Watkins – through more than a decade of success and struggle, resulting in a teeming production that includes piles of era-defining R&B hits, deep racks of vintage Cross Colours T-shirts and a claw-foot bathtub filled with Nikes set aflame. At its most outrageous, CrazySexyCool seems to be testing the tensile strength of the jukebox musical itself. Then again, this is TLC. The truth was outrageous. And that makes for a busy, dizzying, detail-minded show. Throughout the various dramas unfolding onstage, the musical’s three leads – Holli’ Gabrielle Conway as T-Boz, Jade Milan as Left Eye, Stoney B Woods as Chilli – exude a poise that feels as cool and congenial as the real TLC did when they ruled the radio three decades ago. At a weeknight performance of CrazySexyCool in late June, audience members seemed as if they had been reunited with old friends, singing, laughing, shouting affirmations and dancing in their seats. Continue reading...
summary: The musical "CrazySexyCool" is currently playing at Arena Stage in Washington DC, featuring a cast of three leads portraying the R&B trio TLC. The show, written by Kwame Kwei-Armah, includes a collection of the group's hit songs and explores their success and struggles over a decade.

title: GolemUI: Open-Source Library for Dynamic Form Generation
content: We're a team of three friends who have been working with forms and Open Source for a decade, and we joined forces together to create something where we can apply all of our experience. We recently released GolemUI, an Open Source library to generate forms dynamically from JSON definitions, with a typed layer to simplify authoring. This library has a lot to offer. These are the main characteristics:1. A JSON engine. The form is governed by a JSON definition that you can store in a DB, version, diff, or generate it with LLMs as a validated JSON.2. We provide also 28 headless components (and growing) that you can style with CSS variables. We offer APIs so you can drop in Material, Shoelace, or your own components.3. A DX typed authoring layer on top to write forms programmatically, that generates JSON. So you don't have to write it.4. The same definition can render the UI components in React, Angular, Vue, Lit, or Vanilla JS.5. We also have a deterministic MCP that has tools for to validate the model's output, generate JSONs or code, and ensure that the definition returned by the LLM is always valid. You can find more information here:Happy to hear any feedback from you and answer any questions! Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=48748182 Points: 7 # Comments: 0
summary: GolemUI is an open-source library that allows developers to generate forms dynamically from JSON definitions, featuring a typed layer for simplified authoring. The library includes 28 headless components and supports integration with various frameworks, including React, Angular, and Vue.

title: Rhythm Heaven never misses a beat
content:
Nintendo's Under-the-Radar Series Makes a Long-Awaited Return

After a decade-long hiatus, Nintendo's popular yet lesser-known Rhythm Heaven series is set to make its highly anticipated return with the release of Rhythm Heaven Groove on the Nintendo Switch on July 2nd. This marks the fifth installment in the franchise, which has maintained a remarkable consistency in delivering high-quality gaming experiences. Despite being overshadowed by more prominent Nintendo franchises, Rhythm Heaven has earned a dedicated following for its unique blend of music and gameplay.

Rhythm Heaven's minigames, often described as bizarre and humorous, challenge players to test their timing and rhythm skills through a series of short and engaging levels. Similar to WarioWare, the series' fast-paced nature and diverse gameplay mechanics have captivated fans worldwide. The fact that this series has managed to maintain its quality and consistency over the years is a testament to Nintendo's commitment to innovation and creativity.

As fans eagerly await the release of Rhythm Heaven Groove, they can expect more of the same addictive and entertaining gameplay that has made the series a beloved favorite among gamers. With its unique approach to music-based gameplay, Rhythm Heaven has proven itself to be a reliable and enjoyable experience, and its return is sure to bring joy to fans of the series and newcomers alike.
summary: Rhythm Heaven never misses a beat.

title: Scientists Convert Methane into Liquid Chemicals Using Abundant Catalyst
content: Scientists at the U. S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Brookhaven National Laboratory and their collaborators have demonstrated a promising new approach for converting methane—the primary component of natural gas—into liquid chemicals that are precursors for many industrial chemicals and fuels. The research, described in a paper just published in Advanced Functional Materials, shows how molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), an earth-abundant industrial catalyst, can be used with minimal tweaking to selectively convert methane into methyl peroxide and other liquid oxygenate compounds at temperatures below 100°C (212°F). Methyl peroxide is a precursor for making methanol, an energy-dense liquid fuel that can be transported easily.
summary: Researchers at the Brookhaven National Laboratory have developed a method to convert methane into liquid oxygenate compounds using molybdenum disulfide. This process occurs at temperatures below 100°C and produces methyl peroxide, a precursor for the energy-dense liquid fuel methanol.

title: Director sentenced to more than two years for defrauding Netflix out of $11m
content:
Hollywood Writer-Director Carl Rinsch Sentenced to Two and a Half Years in Prison for Defrauding Netflix

In a recent court ruling, Carl Rinsch, a well-known writer-director, has been sentenced to two and a half years in prison for defrauding Netflix out of $11 million. The conviction stems from a never-finished sci-fi series titled White Horse, for which Rinsch requested the substantial sum of money to complete the project. However, according to prosecutors and trial testimony, the director diverted the funds into his personal account, misusing them for personal expenses.

Prosecutors alleged that Rinsch used the diverted funds to purchase luxury items, including high-end cars, watches, clothing, and household goods. Specifically, it was revealed that he spent $638,000 on two mattresses. The charges against Rinsch include federal wire fraud and other related counts. Despite receiving support from notable figures such as Keanu Reeves, who asked the court to show leniency, the conviction ultimately led to the significant prison sentence.

Rinsch's conviction and sentencing serve as a reminder of the importance of accountability in the entertainment industry. The case highlights the consequences of misusing funds and the need for transparency in financial dealings, particularly in high-stakes productions. The writer-director's reputation, once associated with notable films like the 2013 samurai fantasy film 47 Ronin, has been tarnished by this conviction.
summary: Director sentenced to more than two years for defrauding Netflix out of $11m.

In a recent court hearing, Elon Musk's behavior has drawn comparisons to a child throwing a temper tantrum. The incident occurred during a case in which Musk sued Sam Altman and OpenAI, instead of seeking professional help to address his concerns about AI failures. Musk's testimony was marked by outbursts and accusations towards the opposing lawyer, Bill Savitt. When questioned by Savitt, Musk claimed that the lawyer's inquiries were "designed to trick me," and at one point, he even stated that Savitt was asking "unfair questions."

Savitt, known for his mild-mannered demeanor, countered Musk's accusations by assuring him that he was doing his best to ask fair questions. The contrast between Musk's emotional outbursts and Savitt's calm composure has led some to draw humorous comparisons to a scene from a children's cartoon. The exchange has sparked widespread attention and commentary, with many observers expressing surprise at Musk's behavior in a high-stakes legal setting.

The incident has raised questions about Musk's ability to manage stress and pressure, particularly in situations that require a level head and composure. While the outcome of the case remains to be seen, the spectacle has provided a rare glimpse into the billionaire entrepreneur's behavior under scrutiny.
summary: Lawyer Bill Savitt has successfully defended against Elon Musk in two notable cases, including Musk v. Altman, where Musk sued OpenAI. Savitt's cross-examination style was described as mild-mannered and soft-spoken, but effective in questioning Musk.

title: World Cup Balances Exciting Football with Off-Field Controversies
content:
The 2026 World Cup, despite its numerous controversies, has successfully captivated audiences worldwide with its thrilling matches on the pitch. Despite initial concerns and criticisms regarding authoritarian leaders, corruption scandals, and human rights issues, the tournament has demonstrated its enduring resilience. From the exploitation of migrant workers to military dictatorships, the World Cup has overcome numerous challenges in the past, and it appears to be doing so again.

The situation with Iran's national team has been particularly noteworthy. Despite their impressive unbeaten run, the team faced significant obstacles, including restrictions on their movements, a lack of access to their full support staff, and even a change in training camps. These circumstances undoubtedly hindered their performance, and it is remarkable that they were able to progress as far as they did. The controversy surrounding the treatment of the Iranian team highlights the complexities and challenges faced by teams from countries with restrictive governments.

The World Cup's ability to transcend its controversies and deliver captivating football will undoubtedly continue to be a major draw for fans around the globe. As the tournament progresses, it will be interesting to see how the issues raised by the Iranian team and other concerns are addressed. For now, however, the focus remains on the action on the pitch, where the football has undoubtedly stolen the show.
summary: The 2026 World Cup has seen a mix of thrilling football matches and controversies, including criticism of high ticket prices and restrictive immigration policies. The Iranian national team faced unique challenges, including restrictions on their training and travel, which may have impacted their performance in the tournament.

title: Researchers develop method to guide AlphaFold with experimental data
content: The AI-based program AlphaFold predicts a protein's 3D structure with remarkable accuracy. However, it tends to reduce heterogeneous structures to a single dominant conformation, or shape, and overlooks experimental conditions that can alter local structure. Researchers at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) and international collaborators have now developed a way to guide AlphaFold with experimental data. Their approach, published in Nature Biotechnology, paves the way for improved future predictive models.

title: Bash4LLM+ Provides Lightweight Bash Wrapper for LLM API Access
content: Bash4LLM is a single-file Bash wrapper for interacting with LLMs from the terminal. I created it because I wanted something simple that worked without installing Python, Node, or any other runtime. It uses only Bash, curl, and jq. You can send prompts, start a small chat, process files line by line, stream output, and save session metadata in JSON format. I tried to make it safe and predictable: no use of the system /tmp, no use of eval. Groq is supported by default, and other providers can be added with dedicated Bash scripts in the extras/providers/ folder. Example: echo "explains the command: ls -l" |./bash4llm Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=48710827 Points: 12 # Comments: 8
summary: Bash4LLM+ is a single‑file Bash script that enables terminal interaction with large language model APIs using only Bash, curl, and jq. It supports prompt submission, chat sessions, line‑by‑line file processing, streaming output, JSON metadata storage, and includes built‑in Groq support with additional providers addable via extra scripts.

title: Mountains Identified as Potential Sources of Hydrogen Gas
content: Researchers assessed likelihood gas was produced during creation of Alps, Pyrenees and Baetic mountainsHydrogen gas is anticipated to play a central role in phasing out fossil fuels, particularly in industries that are proving more challenging to decarbonise, such as chemical production, shipping and steelmaking. But producing hydrogen synthetically is energy intensive and costly. In order for the hydrogen economy to take off, we need to find reliable natural sources of this gas. Could it be hidden in the mountains? Researchers used plate tectonic simulations to investigate the Pyrenees, Alps and Baetic mountain ranges to assess if their mountain-building processes were likely to have resulted in hydrogen being produced and stored. Their findings, published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth, showed that the Alps and Pyrenees could be strong natural hydrogen exploration sites. Continue reading...

The hollow fiber filter physically removes bacteria and protozoa that cause diseases, as well as dirt and microplastics, and has a lifespan of 4,000 liters (1,000 gallons). Meanwhile, the activated carbon filter removes things like odd tastes and smells. It has a lifespan of just 100 liters (25 gallons), and a two-pack of replacements can be had for $13 a pop. — Thomas Ricker, Deputy Editor Roborock Q10 S5 Plus Where to Buy: $549.99 $264.99 at Amazon The Roborock Q10 S5 Plus has many high-end features, including good obstacle detection and navigation, as well as automatic carpet detection. It also lifts its mop pad 8mm to go over rugs, none of which are features you’ll find in other bots at this price. My main caution with this robot is that it is very wide, so it is not great for more cluttered homes, but it will do well in open-plan spaces. — Jennifer Pattison Tuohy, senior reviewer Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 Where to Buy: $499.99 at Asus (256GB) For a fairly affordable Chromebook that’s still solid, stick with the tried-and-true Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 for about $400. It’s got an older 12th-gen Intel processor, 8GB of RAM, and a basic 1080p screen. But it’s one of the cheapest Chromebooks around with the “Plus” designation, meaning it’s one of The Good Ones. — Antonio G. Di Benedetto, Reviewer, Laptops Nothing Ear (a) Where to Buy: $99 $53.2 at Amazon (black) $99 $56 at Amazon (yellow) $99 $56 at Amazon (white) When looking at Nothing’s Ear (a) earbuds, it’s easy to focus all your attention on the catchy yellow color or their fun, super compact carrying case. But at their $99 price, the company’s entry-level earbuds provide a ton of features, including active noise cancellation, a low-latency mode for gaming, multipoint Bluetooth pairing, and a decent IP54 dust- and water-resistance rating. — Chris Welch, former Senior Reviewer Kodak Mini Shot 3 Retro Where to Buy: $169.99 $131.99 at Amazon (with eight sheets) $169.99 $129.99 at Walmart (with eight sheets) $169.99 $159.99 at Kodak (with eight sheets) Kodak’s hybrid Mini Shot 3 Retro is all about fun. The camera’s accompanying mobile app lets you apply frames, stickers, filters, and a wide range of customization options to photos, making it great for scrapbooking. There’s even a beauty feature in the app to conceal blemishes, as well as a set of Snapchat-like filters you can use to add, say, dog ears, making it a fun instant camera to use as a mini photo booth of sorts at parties. — Sheena Vasani, Commerce Writer Kindle Paperwhite (12th-gen) Where to Buy: $159.99 $124.99 at Amazon (with ads) $159.99 $134.99 at Best Buy (with ads) If you mostly buy ebooks from Amazon, you’ll want a Kindle, and the 12th-gen Kindle Paperwhite is the best choice for most people. It’s $70 cheaper than the Kobo Libra Colour — my top non-Amazon e-reader — yet offers many of the same features, including a spacious 7-inch 300pi display with rich contrast levels. Unlike Amazon’s entry-level Kindle, it also features IPX8 water resistance and an adjustable warm frontlight that reduces blue light, which may interrupt melatonin production. The $199.99 Signature Edition Paperwhite also supports wireless charging, a rare feature in an e-reader. — Sheena Vasani, Commerce Writer Corsair Scimitar RGB Elite Where to Buy: $79.99 $49.99 at Best Buy For most people, a gaming mouse only really needs to be good at pointing and clicking on an enemy’s head. But for anyone who plays MMORPGs like World of Warcraft or Final Fantasy XIV, if you can add a bunch of buttons to your mouse, that’s free keybindings, baby. There are tons of mice out there with an entire keypad’s worth of thumb buttons — the Razer Naga pioneered the genre. I’ve tried all of them, and the Corsair Scimitar RGB Elite is the best. It’s the one that feels best in my hand — partly because you can adjust the position of the number pad, which is important during long raids and dungeons. — Jackie Thomas Sonos Five Where to Buy: $599 $449 at Amazon The Sonos Five isn’t just Sonos’ best-sounding speaker; it’s at the top of the pack compared to all competitors. From an audio quality perspective, it beats the HomePod, the latest Echo Studio, and other mass market speakers — both those that are smart and not. Can you find better hi-fi bookshelf speakers? Absolutely, but those aren’t natively tied into music services like Sonos gear is. The Five is a hefty unit and takes up a decent amount of desk space. But once you throw some music on, its powerful stereo output is enough to handle any dinner party or weekend get-together. — Chris Welch, former Senior Reviewer

title: David Hockney's private funeral attended by only two mourners
content:
David Hockney’s funeral, held last week, was a private affair attended by only two people, in accordance with the artist’s final wishes. The British painter, who died at the age of 91, had requested that only his partner and great‑nephew be present at the ceremony, with memorial services planned in the locations where he had lived and worked.

The mourners were 61‑year‑old partner Jean‑Pierre Gonçalves de Lima and 33‑year‑old great‑nephew Richard Hockney, a photographer who had assisted the artist and often modeled for him. Both men serve as trustees of the David Hockney Foundation, established by the artist in 2008 to preserve and promote his legacy.

The limited attendance reflected Hockney’s desire for a quiet farewell, while the foundation will oversee the broader memorial events that will celebrate his life and work across the cities that shaped his career.
summary: The funeral of artist David Hockney was held privately, with only his partner Jean-Pierre Gonçalves de Lima and great-nephew Richard Hockney in attendance. Both mourners are trustees of the David Hockney Foundation.

title: Tottenham Spends £230m in Summer Transfer Market
content:
Tottenham Hotspur’s summer transfer spending of £230 million marks a dramatic departure from the frugal strategies of former owner Daniel Levy, signaling a new era under the ownership of Joe Lewis and his family. This unprecedented outlay, fueled partly by cash injections linked to the recent sale of high-value art from the Lewis collection, has drawn attention to the club’s evolving financial approach. Sotheby’s London auction of 25 modern and contemporary artworks, raising £300 million—including a £41.5 million sale of Amedeo Modigliani’s Seated Nude With Necklace—has sparked speculation about whether the proceeds are being funneled into the club’s ambitious recruitment drive, which includes targets such as Brighton & Hove Albion’s Jan Paul van Hecke.  

While no direct link has been confirmed between the art sale and Tottenham’s transfer activities, the timing and scale of both transactions suggest a strategic realignment. The club, ranked 17th in Premier League performance metrics over the past decade, is now prioritizing rapid reinvention through high-profile signings, a stark contrast to the cost-conscious model that defined its previous ownership. This shift raises questions about the sustainability of such spending and the long-term vision behind it. As Tottenham navigates this transition, stakeholders will scrutinize whether the influx of capital—whether from art collections or other assets—can translate into on-field success and elevate the club’s status in European football.
summary: Tottenham Hotspur is spending a record £230m in the transfer market, largely funded by the club's owners, the Lewis family. The significant investment has raised questions about the club's strategy and goals, with some speculating about the source of the funding, including possible sales of the family's assets.

title: Arthur Fery Reaches Wimbledon Semifinals

He is, even more extraordinarily, only the fourth player to do it at any grand slam tournament in the open era, after Goran Ivanisevic, Henri Leconte and Jimmy Connors. Continue reading...

title: Western Europe records hottest June on record
content:
Western Europe experienced its hottest June on record, with surface air temperatures averaging 3.06 °C above the long‑term mean, according to the EU’s Copernicus climate monitoring service. The heatwave, driven by rising carbon emissions, coincided with the United Kingdom’s third consecutive heatwave of the year and widespread wildfires in France and Spain.

Scientists warn that the sustained temperature rise poses significant risks to human health, ecosystems and infrastructure. The extreme heat has intensified fire danger, leading to record‑breaking wildfire activity across the continent. The economic and environmental costs of these fires underscore a growing failure to adapt to a warming climate.

The June heatwave and accompanying wildfires illustrate the escalating impact of climate change on Europe’s landscapes and societies. Continued monitoring and adaptation measures are essential to mitigate the growing risks associated with higher temperatures and fire frequency.
summary: Temperatures across Western Europe rose 3.06 °C above the decade average in June, making it the hottest month on record for the region. The heatwave triggered wildfires in France and Spain and prompted scientists to warn of risks to people, ecosystems and infrastructure.

title: Study finds fully virtual BCBA-delivered ABA improves adaptive functioning in autism
content:
A study jointly conducted by AnswersNow and the Clemson Center for Behavior Analysis at Clemson University and published in JMIR Pediatrics and Parenting reports that fully virtual applied behavior analysis (ABA) services administered by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) are a feasible alternative to traditional in‑person therapy for families of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The research evaluated 504 participants who received remote ABA interventions, measuring changes in adaptive functioning over the study period.

Results indicate that 76 percent of the children demonstrated measurable progress in adaptive skills, and families reported high satisfaction with the virtual format. The findings suggest that remote ABA delivery can maintain therapeutic effectiveness while offering greater accessibility for families, potentially expanding service options for the ASD community.
summary: A study by AnswersNow and the Clemson Center for Behavior Analysis, published in JMIR Pediatrics and Parenting, evaluated fully virtual ABA services delivered by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst for families of children with autism. Among 504 participants, 76% demonstrated measurable progress in adaptive functioning, indicating the approach is feasible and well‑received.

title: Osaka researchers develop probe to trace Alzheimer's lipids at single‑cell level
content:
Researchers at Osaka University have unveiled a new analytical method capable of detecting subtle chemical differences between adjacent cells within the same tissue. The technique, detailed in the latest issue of Analytical Chemistry, offers unprecedented precision and stability in profiling cell‑by‑cell diversity, allowing scientists to map the unique molecular signatures that distinguish individual cells that appear morphologically identical.

By capturing these hidden variations, the method promises to deepen understanding of how diseases originate and propagate at the microscopic level. The ability to resolve intra‑tissue heterogeneity could enhance studies of tumor development, inflammatory processes, and other pathologies where cellular individuality influences disease dynamics, providing a powerful tool for future biomedical research.
summary: Researchers at the University of Osaka have created a new technique that can detect Alzheimer's‑linked lipids in individual cells within tissues. The method offers unprecedented precision and stability, as reported in Analytical Chemistry.

title: Robots raise productivity in Spanish manufacturing SMEs but do not increase exports
content: Spanish small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the manufacturing sector that use robots are more productive, especially those that have fewer workers and are less innovative. However, automation alone does not translate into an increase in exports. Companies' presence in international markets is closely linked to the existence of localization economies in the region. This is the main conclusion of a pioneering study by researchers from the UOC's Faculty of Economics and Business. It is the first analysis of the impact that adopting these technologies has on SMEs, firms with a workforce of 10 to 200 employees, a sector that represents a large part of the Spanish business community.

title: AI model pinpoints descriptors distinguishing water’s two liquid states
content:
Water’s unusual behavior is magnified when it is supercooled, yet scientists have long struggled to compare the many microscopic descriptors that aim to capture its structure. A team at the University of Osaka has tackled this problem by applying an artificial‑intelligence model trained on extensive computer simulations. The AI was tasked with evaluating 16 distinct structural descriptors that have been proposed to characterize liquid water at the molecular level.

The analysis revealed which descriptors most effectively differentiate between the two competing liquid states that water can adopt under supercooled conditions. By ranking the descriptors according to their predictive power, the researchers have established a clearer framework for future studies of water’s complex phase behavior. The findings streamline the selection of structural metrics for both experimental and theoretical investigations, advancing the broader effort to understand one of nature’s most enigmatic substances.
summary: Researchers at the University of Osaka trained an AI model on computer simulations to assess 16 structural descriptors of supercooled water. The model identified the most effective descriptors for differentiating the two competing liquid states, offering a clearer framework for future studies.

title: Understanding the Formation of Glassy Materials
content: If a liquid is cooled slowly to its freezing point, it becomes a crystal in which the constituent particles are arranged in an ordered pattern. In contrast, when the liquid is cooled very quickly, the particles are unable to arrange themselves in an ordered fashion, and it becomes glass. Glassy materials are all around us in everyday life. Common examples include window glass, certain metal alloys, polymers, foams, gels and even soft materials like emulsions and colloids.
summary: Glassy materials are created when a liquid is cooled rapidly, preventing particles from forming an ordered crystal structure. This cooling process results in the formation of a disordered, amorphous solid, which is characteristic of glass.

title: Sheffield United Chaplain Testifies in Maddy Cusack Inquest
content:
Dr. Delroy Hall, former chaplain at Sheffield United, has testified at an inquest into the death of player Maddy Cusack, revealing she repeatedly asked him not to disclose their conversations to the club. Cusack, found dead at her home in September 2023, spoke to Hall multiple times in August 2023, including a specific request on 23 August to maintain confidentiality. Hall, who volunteered as chaplain from 2017 until November 2023, described players approaching him as a “last resort” for support.  

The inquest heard that Hall believed Cusack sought his guidance during a period of personal and professional strain, though details of their discussions remain undisclosed due to her explicit requests. Hall’s role as a volunteer chaplain ended two months after Cusack’s death, and he emphasized the sensitivity of his interactions with players. The case has raised questions about support systems for athletes and the boundaries of confidentiality in such roles.  

The inquest continues as authorities examine factors contributing to Cusack’s death. Suicide prevention resources have been highlighted in the proceedings, with organizations such as Samaritans and the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline offering support for those in crisis. The case underscores ongoing discussions about mental health care in sports and the challenges individuals may face in balancing personal and professional pressures.
summary: An inquest into Maddy Cusack's death heard that she had spoken to former Sheffield United chaplain Dr Delroy Hall multiple times in August 2023, asking him not to inform the club about their conversations. Maddy Cusack was found dead at her home on 20 September 2023.

The fish is highly adapted to this seasonal cycle: It completes its entire life cycle—from hatching through reproduction to natural death—within a few months. title: New UI Tool for Browsing 'Who is Hiring' Posts on Hacker News
content:
A developer has launched HNWork, a new application designed to enhance the usability of Hacker News’ “Who is hiring” threads by structuring unorganized job postings into a searchable, filtered format. The tool addresses challenges posed by the free-form nature of the original posts, which often lack consistent formatting and include off-topic content. HNWork extracts and highlights key details from the original threads, removes irrelevant submissions, and provides analytics to streamline job hunting for users. The app is open to feedback and can be accessed at hnwork.app.  

The platform introduces features such as text search, filters for job type and location, and automated removal of non-compliant posts, such as those missing contact information or not aligned with hiring themes. Job posters can now create accounts to submit structured job listings, requiring mandatory fields like salary ranges and verification via company email. Additional functionalities include notifications for post comments, company coordination tools for multiple job posters, and administrative oversight for content approval. While the app does not aim to replace the original Hacker News threads, it envisions a more organized hiring experience with required formatting and verification processes.  

HNWork is available for public testing, with the developer inviting users to report bugs, suggest features, or request historical data integration. Account creation is optional for browsing, though job seekers can sign up to comment or access an API. The project builds on a concept first explored during a Y Combinator hackathon years earlier, reflecting the creator’s long-term vision for improving the hiring thread’s functionality. Feedback can be shared via the Hacker News discussion thread at the provided URL.
summary: New UI Tool for Browsing 'Who is Hiring' Posts on Hacker News.

title: 2026 Emmy Nominations Revealed in 118-Category List
content:
The 2026 Emmy nominations, unveiled in a sprawling 118-category announcement, highlighted a competitive landscape marked by unexpected triumphs and notable snubs. Apple TV+’s breakout series Widow’s Bay led the pack with multiple nods, cementing its status as a critical darling. Meanwhile, Richard Gadd’s follow-up to Baby Reindeer and the final season of Stranger Things underperformed, drawing surprise from fans and analysts alike. The nominations also saw The Pitt, Hacks, and newcomers Widow’s Bay and Pluribus emerge as key contenders across major categories.  

The announcement underscored shifting viewer and academy preferences, with streaming platforms dominating the race. Stranger Things, a longtime awards favorite, faced a muted response, signaling a potential shift in its cultural momentum. Conversely, Widow’s Bay’s success reflects growing appetite for serialized, character-driven narratives. While the final Stranger Things season secured some nominations, its limited haul contrasted sharply with the buzz surrounding its earlier seasons.  

As the 2026 Emmys race gains momentum, the nominations set the stage for a fiercely contested awards season. The absence of expected contenders like Stranger Things and the rise of Widow’s Bay and Hacks highlight evolving storytelling trends and the challenges of sustaining long-running franchises. With the ceremony approaching, the competition promises to spotlight both established favorites and fresh voices in television.
summary: The 2026 Emmy nominations have been announced, featuring a diverse range of shows including Apple's breakout series Widow's Bay, The Pitt, and newcomers Pluribus. The nominations were revealed in a 118-category megadump, highlighting the year's most notable performances and productions.

title: Microsoft Releases Flint, a Visualization Language for AI Agents
content:
Microsoft researchers have introduced Flint, a visualization intermediate language designed to enhance the reliability and quality of AI-generated data visualizations. The project addresses a critical challenge in the field: current visualization systems often force AI agents to make low-level design decisions, resulting in either simplistic, default-driven outputs or overly complex specifications that hinder performance. Flint aims to resolve this by abstracting away technical intricacies, enabling agents to produce high-quality charts from high-level instructions through a semantic-type based framework.

Flint operates as a bridge between human intent and machine execution, leveraging a layout optimization engine to automatically derive low-level details from simplified specifications. This approach ensures visualizations are both aesthetically coherent and adaptable for human users, while reducing the verbosity required in traditional systems. The technology powers Microsoft’s open-source Data Formulator project and is accessible via an open-source repository. Developers can integrate Flint into existing AI workflows through a dedicated MCP server, allowing seamless experimentation with data visualization tasks. The initiative has sparked discussion on platforms like Hacker News, where it has garnered 77 upvotes and 30 comments.
summary: Microsoft has released Flint, an open-source visualization language designed to enable AI agents to generate high-quality visualizations from simple specifications. Flint uses a semantic-type based specification and includes a layout optimization engine to produce visually appealing charts.

title: Evil Dead Burn Review: Gory Horror Film Explores Family Torn Apart
content:
Evil Dead Franchise Expands with New Installments, but Original Magic Fades

The Evil Dead franchise, a horror classic born in the 1980s, has seen a significant shift in recent years. With the release of Evil Dead Burn, the number of non-Sam Raimi and non-Bruce Campbell-led films in the series has caught up with the original team's entries. The next installment, Evil Dead Wrath, is set to release in 2028, marking a definitive milestone in this new chapter. Despite the success of these post-Raimi films, including box office success and positive critical reception, they still struggle to establish their own identity and break free from the shadow of the original 1983 horror classic.

The core issue lies in the fact that these new films aim to recapture the essence of the first movie, which introduced the world to the dark and often comedic world of the Evil Dead. The original's success has been a difficult act to follow, and many recent horror comedies have failed to replicate its unique blend of splatter and slapstick. As a result, the new films often feel like they're trying to live up to the legacy of the first film, rather than forging their own path. Evil Dead Burn, while a step in the right direction, may not be enough to entirely shake off these comparisons.

The continued success of the franchise, both critically and commercially, is a testament to the enduring appeal of the Evil Dead universe. However, as the series continues to expand, it remains to be seen whether future installments can find a way to balance their connection to the original with their own unique identity and tone. With the next film, Evil Dead Wrath, just around the corner, fans will be watching closely to see if the franchise can finally break free from the shadows of its iconic predecessor.
summary: Evil Dead Burn is the latest installment in the Evil Dead franchise, featuring a new chapter in the series with a focus on a grieving family's descent into horror. The film is a gory horror movie that explores themes of family trauma and demonic possession, continuing the franchise's legacy of intense violence and dark humor.

The possibility of a repeat of the 2022 World Cup final, in which France faced Argentina, still looms large. Deschamps' response was characteristic of his combative nature, as he faced a barrage of questions from the press. In a notable exchange, he took the opportunity to address criticism from North African media regarding the performance of French official François Letexier in the last-16 match between Argentina and Egypt. Deschamps' tone was unmistakably gruff, as he chose to answer the question begrudgingly.

Despite the controversy surrounding the officials, Deschamps remains resolute in his stance, choosing to focus on the task at hand. As France prepares to face Morocco in the quarter-finals, the team's head coach is adamant that they will not be distracted by external factors. With the stakes high and a repeat of the 2022 final still a possibility, Deschamps' determination to keep his team focused will be put to the test.
summary: France head coach Didier Deschamps stated that he is not concerned about the appointment of Argentinian officials for the World Cup quarter-final against Morocco. title: Marta Kostyuk and Linda Noskova Advance to Wimbledon Semi-Finals
content:
The women’s Wimbledon quarter-finals delivered two decisive upsets as Marta Kostyuk and Linda Noskova secured semi-final berths with commanding performances. Ukrainian 12th seed Kostyuk, who reached the French Open semi-finals in June, overpowered 2024 runner-up Jasmine Paolini 6-3, 6-2 on Centre Court, while Czech ninth seed Noskova edged out Belgian Elise Mertens 6-3, 7-5 to extend her grass-court dominance. Their victories underscore a wide-open women’s draw following the early exits of defending champion Iga Świątek and top-ranked players Aryna Sabalenka and Elena Rybakina.  

Kostyuk’s straight-sets triumph over Paolini, a former Italian Open finalist, highlighted her aggressive baseline play and consistency, with the 20-year-old winning 15 of 19 points behind her first serve. Noskova, meanwhile, capitalized on Mertens’ uncharacteristic errors to claim her 10th straight grass-court win of 2024, sealing the match with a decisive break in the third set. Both players now advance to a semi-final clash that could determine the tournament’s momentum, with Kostyuk’s recent clay success and Noskova’s grass-court form offering a compelling contrast in styles. Their progress reinforces Wimbledon’s unpredictable narrative as the tournament heads into its final stages.
summary: Marta Kostyuk, the 12th seed from Ukraine, defeated Jasmine Paolini 6-3, 6-2 in the Wimbledon quarterfinals. Linda Noskova, the 9th seed from the Czech Republic, also advanced, defeating Elise Mertens 6-3, 7-5.

content: A few tears may someday reveal important clues about a person's neurological health. Researchers reporting in ACS Omega developed a low-cost electrochemical sensor designed to detect dopamine, a neurotransmitter involved in movement, learning, motivation and emotional regulation. They tested the device using artificial human tears, where it accurately detected a range of dopamine concentrations. The technology could support the development of new tools for monitoring Parkinson's disease and other conditions linked to atypical dopamine levels.
summary: Researchers have developed a low-cost electrochemical sensor to detect dopamine levels in tears, a potential indicator of neurological health. The sensor accurately detected a range of dopamine concentrations in artificial human tears, which could aid in monitoring conditions like Parkinson's disease.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Myocardial Infarction Damage Extends Beyond Affected Area
content: A study provides significant evidence in the field of advanced cardiac imaging and clinical cardiology. It shows that the damage resulting from a myocardial infarction is not confined solely to the affected area, but may also extend functionally to remote regions of the ventricle. Identifying this dysfunction could have important implications, including improved prognostic assessment of patients, earlier detection of cardiac deterioration before symptoms or more evident changes appear, and the implementation of earlier and more personalized therapeutic strategies. The study was conducted by the INCLIVA Health Research Institute, the Clinical University Hospital of València, the University of Valencia (UV), the Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV), the Cardiac Imaging Unit of Ascires Biomédico Group, and the Ascires-UPV Joint Research Unit.
summary: A study conducted by multiple institutions found that myocardial infarction damage can extend to remote regions of the ventricle, affecting cardiac function. This discovery may improve cardiac deterioration detection and lead to earlier and more personalized treatment for patients.

title: Ketogenic Diet Shows Promise in Treating Psychotic Disorders
content: Published today in Schizophrenia Bulletin, a first-of-its-kind randomized controlled trial (RCT) from researchers at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF), adds to growing literature on the potential benefit of a ketogenic diet for treating psychotic disorders. The study, which enrolled participants with schizophrenia-spectrum or bipolar 1 disorders, demonstrated rapid metabolic improvements with a ketogenic diet compared with diet-as-usual during an initial one-month RCT open-label phase. Furthermore, those who continued with the optional four-month single-arm ketogenic diet extension saw meaningful gains across metabolic, psychiatric and cognitive measures.
summary: A randomized controlled trial from the University of California, San Francisco, found that a ketogenic diet led to rapid metabolic improvements in participants with schizophrenia-spectrum or bipolar 1 disorders. The study also showed that continued use of the ketogenic diet resulted in meaningful gains across metabolic, psychiatric, and cognitive measures.

title: Cell Division Relies on Precise Spindle Size
content: When a human cell prepares to split into two daughter cells, it must first construct a tiny internal machine called the mitotic spindle—a structure of protein fibers that physically pulls chromosomes apart and deposits one set into each new cell. Get the spindle the right size and the chromosomes segregate cleanly. Getting it wrong could result in the chromosomal errors that fuel cancer.
summary: The mitotic spindle is a structure of protein fibers that separates chromosomes during cell division. The correct size of the spindle is crucial for accurate chromosome segregation, as errors can lead to chromosomal abnormalities.

title: Biomass Distribution in Microbial Communities Examined for Fairness
content: The distribution of income and growing inequality are central themes in public debate. Far less attention has been paid to how resources are distributed in ecological communities, in the so-called state of nature, without any social contract. Species abundance distributions have been studied extensively in ecology, but descriptively. They largely follow a distribution similar to human wealth. Yet the fairness of that distribution has rarely been examined.
summary: Researchers have studied the distribution of biomass in microbial communities to understand how resources are allocated in ecological systems. The findings suggest that the distribution of biomass in these communities follows a pattern similar to the distribution of wealth in human societies, but the fairness of this distribution has not been extensively examined.

title: Twelve South's AirFly Pro Wireless Adapter on Sale for $40

The last-generation model, which costs $5 more than the AirFly SE, offers enhanced functionality for travelers and tech users. The device also serves as a universal adapter for connecting modern wireless headphones to older devices, such as rental car stereos, gym equipment, and the Nintendo Switch, via a standard 3.5mm audio jack. The AirFly Pro’s current discount underscores its value as a multifunctional accessory, particularly for frequent travelers or those navigating mixed audio ecosystems. title: Using Smart Switch to Combat Cockroach Infestations
content:
A compact robotic device is offering a novel solution to everyday tasks, from battling nocturnal pests to automating household appliances. The SwitchBot Bot Rechargeable, priced at $33.99, is a small, adhesive-mounted gadget equipped with a mechanical arm that can press or pull switches and buttons. Designed to mimic human interaction with physical controls, it allows users to activate lights, appliances, or other devices remotely via its companion app, eliminating the need for manual operation in inconvenient or hazardous situations.  

The device’s versatility extends beyond lighting. It can automate coffee makers, fans, or any equipment with a physical power switch, streamlining routines through scheduled tasks or voice commands. For users facing challenges like navigating dark rooms to avoid disturbances—such as cockroaches scurrying in the night—the SwitchBot Bot provides a proactive tool to manage environments before entering a space. Its adhesive design ensures compatibility with a range of switch types, while a rechargeable battery offers portability for temporary installations. The full story, including additional use cases and technical specifications, is available at The Verge.
summary: A home device called the SwitchBot Bot Rechargeable allows users to remotely control physical power switches using a robotic arm. This device can be used to automate various appliances with physical power buttons, including light switches and coffee makers.

title: Moana Live-Action Remake Receives Mixed Reviews
content: Johnson reprises his role from the original animation and has fine rapport with his young co-star Catherine Laga’aia, but the whole enterprise feels cynical and pointlessDisney’s animated super-hit Moana from 2016 – having been followed up by a dull sequel two years ago – now gets a competent but basically pointless and unexciting back-to-basics live-action remake. Screenwriter Jared Bush modifies his original script, Broadway stage veteran Thomas Kail makes his movie directing debut and Lin-Manuel Miranda’s songs are revived. Nineteen-year-old Australian Samoan actor Catherine Laga’aia takes the role of Moana, the headstrong teen daughter of a Polynesian chief; her wise and kindly grandma Tala, who recognises Moana’s heroic leadership destiny, is played by New Zealand actor Rena Owen. Moana has to go on a quest to restore the heart of the goddess Te Fiti, the lack of which is causing an eco-crisis on her home island of Motunui. To do this, she must join forces with the swaggeringly arrogant demigod Maui, in which role Dwayne Johnson returns in his own actual person, which is almost as cartoonishly muscly and vast as the animated version. Maui has a spurious quest of his own, to retrieve the hook which is the source of his power and to do this he must confront his own nemesis. This is the giant crab Tamatoa, which as before is voiced by Jemaine Clement and is a character which is of course just a 3D animated version of the 2D cartoon original, like Heihei, Moana’s less-than-hilarious pet chicken. Continue reading...
summary: Disney's live-action remake of Moana features a cast including Dwayne Johnson and Catherine Laga'aia, and is based on the 2016 animated film of the same name. The movie follows the story of Moana, a teenage girl from Polynesia, as she embarks on a quest to restore the heart of the goddess Te Fiti.

Replacing or correcting the blood-forming stem cells can offer the possibility of long-lasting benefit or a cure. However, before patients can receive these therapies, they usually need intensive and often toxic chemotherapy or radiation to clear space in the bone marrow for the new stem cells.
summary: Genome-edited stem cells have shown an ability to evade the immune system's rejection response, potentially eliminating the need for chemotherapy before transplantation. This breakthrough could lead to more effective and less toxic treatments for blood diseases and blood cancers.

title: The Hill Announces New Digital Subscription Product Amid Growing Popularity
content:
The Hill, a Washington-based political news outlet, is launching a new digital subscription service called Hill Insider as it solidifies its position as a top destination for political coverage. According to traffic data, the publication surpassed competitors like Politico and Axios in May as the most-visited digital-first politics site, despite often being overlooked in broader discussions of influential news organizations. While maintaining a print edition delivered to congressional offices three days a week, The Hill has continued to expand its digital footprint since its 2021 acquisition by Nexstar Media Group for $130 million, a transaction that underscored its value in the competitive political media landscape.  

Under the leadership of Bill Sammon, a former Fox News executive now serving as the Hill’s senior vice president for editorial content, the publication has reported consistent profitability, partly driven by heightened political engagement during the second Trump administration. The introduction of Hill Insider aims to capitalize on this momentum by offering exclusive content and deeper analysis to subscribers, reflecting the outlet’s strategy to diversify revenue streams amid shifting industry dynamics. The move highlights The Hill’s evolving role as a hybrid news entity, balancing its traditional congressional reach with digital innovation to meet growing demand for real-time political coverage.
summary: The Hill, a Washington-based publication, is launching a new digital subscription product called the Hill Insider. The publication has seen a surge in interest, becoming the most-visited digital-first news outlet in May, surpassing Politico and Axios.

title: MSI Katana 15 Gaming Laptop Offers Good Value at $1,133.67
content:

content: PS5, PC, Xbox Series X/S; Ubisoft Singapore/UbisoftUbisoft has removed all the boring parts of pirate life from its fantasy RPG, creating something more focused and funEdward Kenway isn’t your dad’s Assassin’s Creed protagonist. Neither sworn to ancient oaths nor given a noble destiny, he’s just a guy who likes coin, dislikes rules, and whose gold-chasing, rule-dodging lifestyle sees him embroiled in an ancient war between Templars and assassins quite by accident. After he’s shipwrecked with a man named Walpole who turns out to be a Templar, Edward assumes Walpole’s identity in the hopes of securing the bounty he mentioned. Edward wears life lightly. The world around him is violent and chaotic, and those in his vicinity are more obsessed with double-crossings than a Mission:Impossible movie writers’ room. title: Bayreuth Festival Celebrates 150 Years of Richard Wagner's Influence
content: As the Bayreuth festival turns 150, we look at the composer’s huge and enduring influence, and wonder what might have happened to classical music in his absence? One hundred and fifty years ago this summer, Richard Wagner wanted to change the world. Not only the musical world, but nationhood, political thought, even the idea of what it means to be human. The inaugural Bayreuth festival opened on 13 August 1876, with the first complete cycle of Der Ring des Nibelungen staged in Wagner’s custom-built Bayreuth Festspielhaus in Bavaria. The first audience included kings, emperors, aristocracy and politicians as well as Europe’s musical and creative elites (Tchaikovsky, Grieg, Bruckner and Liszt among them). Wagner, who had been a revolutionary on the streets of Dresden in the 1840s, intended the Ring’s four operas to usher in a new world, one redeemed and made wise by this epic story of power, love, redemption, betrayal and renewal. The titanic impact of Wagner is almost impossible to grasp today. Stage design aside (having the orchestra entirely hidden in the pit and darkening the auditorium were two of his innovations at Bayreuth) his legacies are felt across the arts from the way Wagnerism gripped German philosophers and Paris’s painters and poets in the 19th century, to the seismic changes he wreaked in cultural politics, and the toxicity of the antisemitic bearers of the Wagnerian flame after his death in 1883. Continue reading...
summary: The Bayreuth festival, founded by Richard Wagner in 1876, is marking its 150th anniversary with a celebration of the composer's significant impact on classical music. Wagner's innovative works, including Der Ring des Nibelungen, have had a lasting influence on the arts, shaping stage design, cultural politics, and artistic movements.

title: Oil prices surge 5% after US strikes on Iran
content:
Global markets experienced heightened volatility as Brent crude surged to a daily high of $79.26, driven by geopolitical tensions and inflationary pressures, while stock markets declined and government bond yields climbed amid fears of aggressive interest rate hikes. The U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, reigniting concerns over regional instability and potential disruptions to oil supplies. These developments underscored investors’ anxiety over rising energy costs and their potential to exacerbate inflation, prompting central banks to adopt a more hawkish stance.  

Amid this backdrop, consumer demand for summer travel showed resilience, with Jet2 Holidays reporting a 7.1% year-on-year increase in summer bookings. The travel operator attributed the rebound to pent-up demand, noting that many customers had postponed purchases during the Middle East conflict but are now eager to book trips. Destinations such as Turkey, Cyprus, Greece’s eastern islands, Bulgaria, and parts of North Africa saw the strongest recovery, reflecting preferences for destinations with amenities like air-conditioned accommodations. Jet2 highlighted a 1.2 percentage point rise in average load factors, signaling robust consumer confidence despite lingering economic uncertainties. The recovery in travel demand contrasts with broader market jitters, illustrating the complex interplay between geopolitical risks and consumer behavior.
summary: Oil prices jumped 5% to a daily high of $79.26 following US strikes on Iran, leading to increased gas prices and a decline in stock markets. The US and Iran have traded strikes around the Strait of Hormuz, violating a fragile ceasefire.

title: Pioneers Reunite 50 Years After First Women's Cricket Game at Lord's
content: On the eve of the first women’s Test at Lord’s, nine England players and one Australian from 1976 are gatheringOn Thursday, in a room in central London about three miles from Lord’s, a group of 10 women will gather together for a very special reunion. Fifty years ago, on 4 August 1976, they made history when they were among the first female cricketers to play a match at the so-called Home of Cricket: a one-day international between England and Australia. England strolled to an eight-wicket win, chasing down 162 thanks to half-centuries from Enid Bakewell, opening up with Lynne Thomas, and Chris Watmough, coming in at No 3. But the importance of the occasion was less about the details of the match than what it represented. After almost five decades of the Women’s Cricket Association knocking on MCC’s door, the success of the first World Cup three years earlier finally persuaded the club that it was time to host a women’s match. title: Tree Coexistence in Old Growth Forests
content: Forests are shaped by light competition. The trees that grow the tallest have access to the most sunlight, blocking the rays and rendering the shaded space around them inhospitable to shorter trees below. In this stem exclusion phase of forest succession, the shorter trees often die. Yet scientists have observed that in old-growth forests, trees of vastly different sizes successfully coexist, proving that reaching the top of the canopy is not the sole winning strategy for survival in a forest environment.
summary: In old-growth forests, trees of varying heights can coexist despite competition for sunlight. The tallest trees have access to the most sunlight, while shorter trees can still survive in the shaded areas beneath them.
author: Phys.org

title: California Wineries Face Climate Threats
content:
The United States ranks as the fourth‑largest wine‑producing nation in the world, with roughly 80 % of its output concentrated in California. Historically, the state’s most celebrated vineyards have been located in Napa Valley and Sonoma County, where a mild microclimate has supported premium wine production since the 19th century.

However, grape yield and quality are highly sensitive to local environmental conditions. Rising temperatures, altered rainfall patterns, and increased frequency of extreme weather events are already affecting vine health and harvest timing across California’s key appellations. Industry experts warn that the ongoing climate crisis could reshape the region’s wine‑making landscape, potentially reducing production volumes and prompting shifts in varietal choices and cultivation practices.
summary: The US is the fourth-largest wine-producing country, with approximately 80% of its production coming from California. California's wine industry, particularly in regions like Napa Valley and Sonoma County, is vulnerable to climate change and its effects on grape yield and quality.
author: Phys.org

title: Soil holds vast numbers of dormant viruses.
