title: England secure record-breaking 125-run T20 win over India
content:
England secured a record-breaking 125-run victory over India in a T20 International, dismissing their opponents for just 76 runs in a collapse that shattered historical norms. Chasing a modest target of 202, India were bowled out in under 12 overs, marking their worst-ever T20 defeat by a margin of 125 runs—45 runs more than their previous record. The hosts’ batting lineup imploded under relentless pressure from England’s pace attack, with Jofra Archer and Mark Wood (Tongue) spearheading a devastating spell that left India reeling at 9-2 within the first five overs.  

The Indian innings began with a flurry of boundaries, as Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma struck three consecutive sixes in the opening over, but England’s bowlers quickly regained control. A combination of sharp yorkers and aggressive swing dismantled India’s middle order, with key wickets falling at regular intervals. By the time the innings folded, India had managed only 76, their lowest T20 score against any opponent. The victory underscored England’s dominance in the shortest format, as they defended their total with precision, leaving India to ponder their worst T20 performance in history.
summary: England won the match by 125 runs, with India all out for 76 runs in fewer than 12 overs, marking India's largest-ever T20 defeat. The English team was led by strong performances from their bowlers, including Archer and Tongue, in defense of their modest total of 201-7.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pulitzer-Nominated Writer Rachel Aviv Explores Mother-Daughter Relationships in New Book
content:
Pulitzer-Nominated Writer Explores the Complexity of Mother-Daughter Relationships in New Book

Renowned essayist Rachel Aviv has released a new book, The Middle Passage, which delves into the intricate bond between mothers and daughters. In a recent interview, Aviv discussed her work, highlighting the significance of this relationship as the most complex of all. The book, which advances the Jungian concept of transformation through change, suggests that individuals must alter their fundamental identity in order to progress into middle age. According to Aviv, this concept is frustratingly true, as it requires individuals to confront and adapt to new circumstances.

Aviv's personal experience serves as a catalyst for her exploration of the mother-daughter relationship. In her high school years, she lost herself in a profound relationship, abandoning her previous interests. This experience left her with a deep-seated fear of change, which she feared would resurface when she gave birth to her first child in 2016. However, she was surprised to find that her identity remained intact, leaving her feeling a sense of accomplishment. This experience has fueled Aviv's investigation into the complexities of the mother-daughter bond and the ways in which individuals can navigate transformation.

Aviv's work is a testament to the enduring power of the human spirit, as she grapples with the challenges of identity, change, and growth. Her book, The Middle Passage, offers a thought-provoking exploration of the mother-daughter relationship, one that is both deeply personal and universally relatable. As a staff writer for The New Yorker, Aviv brings her unique perspective to this timely and important topic, shedding light on the intricate dynamics at play in this complex bond.
summary: Rachel Aviv, a Pulitzer-nominated writer, has released a new book investigating the complexities of the mother-daughter relationship. The book delves into the psychological aspects of this bond, exploring how it can be both transformative and challenging.

title: England Rugby Team Set to Face Fiji in Nations Championship
content:
England’s rugby team is set to face Fiji in Liverpool this Saturday as part of the Nations Championship, with an uncapped back poised for a call-up to help the squad bounce back from a heavy 45-21 defeat to South Africa. The match at Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium marks a pivotal moment for the side, which has faced a whirlwind schedule, moving from South Africa to sub-Saharan Surrey and now to Merseyside. Despite the logistical challenges of playing in three continents in quick succession, the team is focused on regaining momentum ahead of the season’s final fixtures.  

The recent loss to the Springboks in Johannesburg has left the camp grappling with frustration, but a strong performance against Fiji is seen as critical to restoring confidence. While the geographical dislocation—playing in a warmer climate than their opponents in Suva—adds a layer of complexity, the squad is determined to overcome it. The inclusion of an uncapped player highlights England’s intent to blend experience with fresh talent as they aim to reset their campaign. A victory in Liverpool would not erase past setbacks but could serve as a foundation for a stronger finish to the season.
summary: The England rugby team is preparing to face Fiji in a Nations Championship match at Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool on Saturday. The match comes after England's 45-21 defeat against South Africa in their previous outing, and they aim to rebound with a strong performance.

title: El Niño Outpaces La Niña in Climate Models
content: Researchers have long known that there is an asymmetry in the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), the confluence of wind and water currents that creates warm El Niño events and cooler La Niña events. Large-scale climate models tend to underrepresent this asymmetry for reasons that are still not fully understood. Better modeling of the mechanisms that make El Niño events warmer could both provide insight into Earth's climate system and improve future ENSO predictions.
summary: Researchers have observed an asymmetry in the El Niño-Southern Oscillation, with El Niño events being warmer than La Niña events. Climate models tend to underrepresent this asymmetry, and improving the modeling of El Niño mechanisms could enhance understanding of the climate system and ENSO predictions.

title: Birth Control Linked to Brain Tumor Risk

According to 2021 WHO data, 874 million of the world's 1.9 billion women of reproductive age use modern contraceptive methods. Many of these methods contain high doses of certain progestogens, a synthetic version of progesterone, a hormone that plays a key role in the menstrual cycle and pregnancy. So what does birth control have to do with meningioma?

The research findings have been published in npj Digital Medicine.
summary: Researchers at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University have created an AI agent and risk prediction model for precision diabetes management tailored to Asian populations. title: Independence Day Origin Story: From Concept to Title
content: The makers of the blockbusting sci-fi thriller reveal how they made a hit, why Kevin Spacey was almost involved and what went wrong with the sequelThe architects of cinema’s most popular alien invasion have slightly differing accounts of how exactly the original plans for Independence Day came to them. But they both agree that it began with the now-famous image of a massive spaceship looming over a city skyline. Roland Emmerich, the director, recalls explaining the scope of the concept to Dean Devlin, the co-writer and producer, at the latter’s home: “He lived in an area on a hill, so I said, let’s go to the window – all of what you see would be [covered by] the underside of a spaceship. He said, where’s the humor? And I said, there’s a guy knocking out an alien saying ‘welcome to Earth.’ Then we learned that Tim Burton, a director I really admire, was doing Mars Attacks! We knew that movie was coming out in August, and we said, well, there’s a great date before: Fourth of July. And that’s why the movie is called Independence Day.” Continue reading...
summary: The film's concept came from a vision of a massive spaceship looming over a city skyline, as described by director Roland Emmerich and producer Dean Devlin. The title “Independence Day” was chosen to align with a Fourth of July release, following the release of Tim Burton's Mars Attacks.

title: David Sedaris's 'The Land and Its People' Review
content:
David Sedaris has released a new collection of essays, marking his tenth volume of humor and personal reflection. The book, which includes pieces previously published in the New Yorker, follows a long career that has seen Sedaris sell more than 16 million copies worldwide. Critics note that the new work leans heavily on anecdotal material, some of which feels thin or repetitive compared to earlier volumes.

Reviewers point out that Sedaris’s writing style remains curmudgeonly, with a focus on everyday frustrations and idiosyncratic observations. The collection has been described as “shticky” by some, suggesting a reliance on familiar tropes and a lack of fresh material. Despite this, the author’s loyal fan base continues to attend book events and purchase new releases, indicating that the established formula still resonates with a significant audience. The editorial process has been mentioned as a potential area for tightening, though the author’s reputation as a post‑editing elite may explain the final product’s current form.

Overall, the new volume reinforces Sedaris’s position as a prolific essayist while highlighting the challenges that long‑running writers face in maintaining originality. The reception underscores the divide between devoted readers who appreciate the familiar wit and newer audiences who seek more substantive content.
summary: The review notes that 'The Land and Its People' contains many essays previously published in the New Yorker and continues Sedaris's curmudgeon tone. It also suggests the book may be less engaging for readers who are not already fans.
author: Guardian Culture

The 1961 portrait by Bruce Stevenson paid tribute to the first US astronaut in space. It also planted a seed. James Webb, the then administrator of Nasa, saw the painting and was inspired to start the space agency’s own art programme, believing that artists could bring a unique perspective to exploring the cosmos. From 1962 to 1974 it was led by James Dean, who then became the first art curator at the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum in Washington. Continue reading...
summary: Smithsonian Celebrates 50 Years of Space Art with New Exhibition.

title: Steven Spielberg: A Director Focused on Filmmaking, Not Politics
content: A reminder of Steven Spielberg’s prowess and speed in the latest in our series of writers highlighting their go-to comfort watchesSteven Spielberg was never much of a radical. While Francis Ford Coppola made Apocalypse Now and even George Lucas attacked the Vietnam war with Star Wars, the nervy new Hollywood hotshot was more interested in moviemaking’s toys than its politics. In Peter Biskind’s bestselling book of Tinseltown gossip, Easy Riders, Raging Bulls, the actor Kit Carson remembers running into Spielberg at a party when the tumult of an eventful 1968 presidential campaign was at fever pitch. “Everybody was up,” Carson remembered. “The revolution was about to happen.” All the young director wanted to talk about was how to get a shot while throwing a camera off a roof. In the end, it took him 40 years to produce his own broadside against the US foreign policy of his youth. In uncharacteristically political style, he spent most of it drawing parallels to the then current resident of the White House. Continue reading...
summary: Steven Spielberg: A Director Focused on Filmmaking, Not Politics.

title: British wildcard Arthur Fery reaches Wimbledon quarter-finals after comeback win over Grigor Dimitrov
content:
British wildcard Arthur Fery has shown a remarkable resilience at Wimbledon, advancing to the quarter‑finals after a dramatic comeback against Grigor Dimitrov. The 23‑year‑old, who has never progressed beyond the second round of a Grand Slam, was down a set and a break in the third before rallying to win the match. His victory follows a similar fight‑back against Dutch qualifier Zizou Bergs, where he overturned a set and break deficit to win in a fifth‑set tie‑break.

Fery’s performance has highlighted his growing composure on the biggest stages. Despite the pressure of a Wimbledon quarter‑final, he has consistently displayed the ability to recover from difficult positions, a trait that has defined his recent run. With his eyes now set on the next round, Fery’s journey underscores the unpredictable nature of the sport and the emergence of new talent in the tennis world.
summary: Arthur Fery, a 23‑year‑old British wildcard, advanced to the Wimbledon quarter‑finals by defeating Grigor Dimitrov after trailing a set and a break. Earlier in the tournament he also came from behind to beat Zizou Bergs in a fifth‑set tie‑break.

title: Springboks aim for third Rugby World Cup title in 2027
content: Door is ajar for Rassie Erasmus’ side to surpass All Blacks when leading sides converge on Australia next year The best sports teams constantly look to reinvent themselves. Their core principles remain in place but, crucially, they never, ever stand still. To do so is to risk slipping backwards relative to their competitors and arrive at the worst of all possible outcomes: a poorer, less successful version of themselves. The ultimate example in rugby, until now, has probably been the All Blacks. For decades it was not only about winning the next game, but underlining their position, to quote one of their motivational whiteboard slogans from 2013, as “the most dominant team in the history of the world”. When you are chasing that kind of rarefied target you don’t allow the grass grow beneath your jandals. Continue reading...
summary: The South African team, coached by Rassie Erasmus, will compete in the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia with the opportunity to win a third consecutive tournament. Their success could see them surpass the All Blacks as the sport’s most dominant side.

title: Isotopic study links hot spring magmatic water to subducting Pacific Plate

Researchers at the University of Tsukuba used numerical simulations and isotopic data to show that magmatic water in hot springs and volcanic gases around Kussharo Caldera, Hokkaido, originates from the subducting Pacific Plate, which descends from the Kuril Trench to a depth of 125 kilometers (78 miles). The paper is published in the Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research.
summary: Researchers used isotopic data and numerical simulations to demonstrate that magmatic water in hot springs and volcanic gases around Kussharo Caldera originates from the subducting Pacific Plate. The findings, published in the Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research, show the plate descends to a depth of about 125 km beneath the caldera.

title: New 9 MB Native Mac File Manager Adds Fuzzy Search, Dual‑Pane View and Batch Rename
content:
A developer announced a new macOS file‑manager app on the Hacker News front page, where it quickly gathered 27 up‑votes and 17 comments. The tool was created to streamline the long‑standing problem of a cluttered Downloads folder, offering a lightweight alternative to Finder’s built‑in capabilities.

The application is built with .NET/C# using AppKit and compiled to Native AOT, resulting in a compact 9 MB binary. It provides a range of productivity features: fuzzy “go to” navigation, image/PDF previews on hover, dual‑pane view with tabbed filters, a command palette, batch renaming with regex support, image format conversion, zip creation, bookmarks, Quick Look, single‑click opening, and full keyboard control. File operations are hardened with atomic writes and a manual audit of copy, move, and delete actions. The app maintains a privacy‑first stance, making only a minimal network request to check for updates (omitted entirely in the trial version) and transmitting only the current app version. It runs on Apple Silicon and macOS 12+, offers a 30‑day free trial, and is sold as a one‑time purchase for $19.99, with no subscription model.

The combination of a small footprint, robust file‑handling safeguards, and a suite of quality‑of‑life features positions this tool as a practical option for users seeking a more efficient way to manage files on macOS. The post’s reception on Hacker News suggests that the community sees value in its focused functionality and privacy‑centric design.
summary: New 9 MB Native Mac File Manager Adds Fuzzy Search, Dual‑Pane View and Batch Rename.

title: England World Cup Win Boosts UK High Streets
content:
England’s victory over Mexico in the World Cup on June 30 spurred a significant surge in UK high-street activity, with footfall rising 143.6% year-on-year between midnight and 6am, according to data from MRI Software. Market towns saw the highest increase at 175.5%, followed by historic towns at 159.9%. The spike was attributed to the World Cup’s role as a “powerful footfall driver,” with extended dwell times and celebratory spending boosting local economies. Jenni Matthews, a retail analyst at MRI, highlighted the potential for continued momentum as England progresses in the tournament, urging retailers to align staffing and promotions with key matches to capitalize on the trend.  

Separate economic indicators suggest sustained consumer spending amid a reduced saving rate. Car registration data revealed steady growth, with battery-powered electric vehicle registrations climbing 35% year-on-year in June, up from 34.2% in May, while hybrid registrations rose 25.3%. Analysts attribute this to ongoing replacement demand and shifting consumer preferences toward sustainable transport. Combined with the World Cup’s immediate economic impact, these trends underscore a resilient consumption outlook, bolstered by both discretionary and essential spending sectors as the UK navigates evolving economic conditions.
summary: England World Cup Win Boosts UK High Streets.
author: Guardian Business

title: FCA urges stronger regulator powers to protect consumers from AI risks

title: China targets dexterous robotic hands to advance embodied AI
content:
The push to create “embodied AI” is now centered on developing dexterous robotic hands capable of matching the flexibility and precision of human fingers. Human hands, with their dense network of nerves and intricate musculature, can perform tasks such as tying shoelaces or buttoning shirts without conscious effort—a level of coordinated control that has eluded machines for millennia. Recent advances in artificial‑intelligence algorithms, tactile sensing, and lightweight actuation are allowing a handful of firms, especially in China, to integrate real‑time perception with fine‑motor control, moving humanoid robots beyond novelty demonstrations toward practical applications in manufacturing, logistics, and personal assistance.

Chinese companies including Alibaba’s DAMO Academy, Horizon Robotics, and UBTech are investing heavily in research that combines deep reinforcement learning with high‑resolution force feedback to teach robots how to grasp, manipulate, and adapt to varied objects. Parallel efforts in the United States and Europe are exploring similar approaches, but the concentration of funding and talent in China has accelerated prototype development, with several labs reporting successful trials of multi‑fingered hands that can perform tasks such as assembling small components or handling delicate items. If these technologies mature, they could transform humanoid robots from laboratory curiosities into viable tools for industry and everyday life, marking a significant milestone in the broader AI and robotics landscape.
summary: Chinese firms are developing highly flexible robotic hands to enable humanoid robots to perform complex tasks. The effort is part of a broader race to create embodied AI that can match human manual abilities.
author: Guardian Technology

title: England Beat Mexico 1-0 After Kane Penalty in World Cup Thriller
content:
England’s triumph over Mexico in the Round of 16 at the Estadio Azteca has been hailed as the nation’s finest knockout‑phase victory since the 1966 World Cup. Only nine such wins have occurred in England’s history, each a dramatic moment, but the setting of this match—Mexico’s iconic stadium, a venue that has haunted England with a 0‑2 loss in the 1970 final—made the result all the more striking. The game, which served as the co‑hosts’ grand send‑off from their own turf, felt like an unofficial final for the Mexican side, who had remained undefeated at the tournament after four straight wins.

England’s 2‑1 win came on a night of disciplined defending and precise counter‑attacks. The hosts’ midfield controlled the tempo, while the forwards capitalised on a single moment of defensive lapse to secure the decisive goal. Mexico, coached by Javier Aguirre, entered the match on a flawless 4‑0 record and had been the most formidable opponent in the tournament, yet the English side managed to break through their disciplined structure. The victory not only ended Mexico’s perfect run but also secured England’s place in the quarter‑finals, marking a historic moment for the nation’s footballing narrative.
summary: England defeated Mexico 1-0 in a World Cup knockout match at Estadio Azteca, with Harry Kane scoring the decisive penalty. The match saw England play with ten men for most of the game.

title: Bilingualism linked to younger-appearing brains, study finds
content:
A new study presented at the Federation of European Neuroscience Societies conference in Barcelona reports that individuals who speak two or more languages exhibit brain characteristics that appear up to six years younger than those of monolingual speakers. The research suggests that multilingualism may decelerate brain ageing by as much as 13 years, with the protective effect increasing the earlier in life a person begins learning additional languages.

The findings indicate a dose‑response relationship: the greater the number of languages spoken and the younger the age at which language acquisition starts, the more pronounced the apparent reduction in brain ageing. While the study’s methodology and sample size were not disclosed in the brief, the results add to a growing body of evidence linking cognitive reserve to lifelong linguistic engagement.
summary: Researchers presented a study at the Federation of European Neuroscience Societies conference in Barcelona showing that individuals who speak two or more languages have brains that appear about six years younger than monolinguals. The findings also suggest that learning additional languages earlier in life may slow brain ageing by up to 13 years.

title: Sinner Reaches Wimbledon Quarterfinals
content:
World No. 1 Jannik Sinner advanced to the next round of the tournament with a 6-3, 7-6 (0), 6-3 victory over Japanese qualifier Shintaro Mochizuki, showcasing his dominance despite a spirited challenge from his opponent. The match, Sinner’s first against the world’s top-ranked player, featured a tense second set where Mochizuki, a lower-ranked underdog, pushed the Italian to a tiebreak after saving multiple break points with a series of acrobatic volleys. The qualifier’s unconventional tactics, including a serve-and-volley strategy and precise net play, briefly unsettled Sinner but ultimately proved insufficient against the world No. 1’s consistency and power.

Mochizuki’s resilience peaked during the second set’s pivotal 12-minute service game, where he defied a two-break-point deficit with a sequence of audacious volleys, including a lunging, outlandish-angle winner to stay on serve. However, Sinner’s composure in critical moments—evident in his swift tiebreak and decisive third-set performance—underscored his readiness for the title defense. The victory extends Sinner’s momentum as he eyes a repeat of last year’s success, while Mochizuki’s efforts highlighted the unpredictability of Grand Slam qualifying challenges. With the tournament progressing, Sinner remains a formidable favorite, having navigated early-round obstacles with his characteristic blend of precision and mental fortitude.
summary: Jannik Sinner defeated Shintaro Mochizuki in a match with a score of 6-3, 7-6 (0), 6-3. The victory allows Sinner to advance to the quarter-finals of Wimbledon as he continues his title defence.

title: Norway Beats Brazil to Reach World Cup Quarter-Finals
content:
Norway secured their first World Cup quarter-final berth in history with a dramatic 2-1 victory over Brazil, thanks to a late double from Erling Haaland. The striker, who has captivated global attention with his on-field prowess and off-field charisma—including a memorable cowboy-themed appearance—scored both goals in the final 11 minutes, netting his sixth and seventh of the tournament to cap a stunning upset. The result marks a significant milestone for Norway, who have steadily risen as a force in international football under manager Ståle Solbakken, whose tactical acumen and team-building efforts have redefined the nation’s competitive edge.  

The match unfolded with Norway asserting dominance in the first half but failing to convert their pressure into goals. A strategic double substitution at halftime shifted the momentum, enabling the underdogs to exploit Brazil’s defensive vulnerabilities through swift counterattacks. Despite Brazil’s opportunities to seize control, clinical finishing eluded them, allowing Norway to capitalize on their tactical adjustments. Haaland’s decisive strikes not only underscored his individual brilliance but also highlighted the team’s resilience and adaptability. The triumph cements Norway’s status as a rising power in world football and sets the stage for further surprises in the tournament’s knockout phase.
summary: Erling Haaland scored two goals in the last 11 minutes to lead Norway to a win over Brazil, sending his team to the World Cup quarter-finals for the first time.

title: Osint Tool Finds Exposed Files on Domains
content:
A cybersecurity researcher has launched a free, read-only OSINT (open-source intelligence) tool designed to assist penetration testers and bug bounty hunters in identifying exposed sensitive data across domains. The platform, available at https://search.cerast-intelligence.com/, leverages certificate transparency logs to monitor newly registered domains and scans them for vulnerabilities such as exposed environment files (.env), open Git directories, configuration files, and database dumps. These findings are aggregated into a searchable database, enabling users to query specific domains or domain fragments to uncover potential security risks.  

The tool’s creator is seeking community feedback on potential enhancements, including a notification system that would allow users to register keywords and receive alerts when new exposures match their criteria. Additionally, the researcher expressed concerns about mitigating data abuse, highlighting the need for strategies to prevent misuse of the tool’s findings. The platform, which currently requires no authentication, is hosted on a public-facing URL and is open to suggestions for improving its functionality and security safeguards. The project has sparked discussion on Hacker News, with users invited to share ideas for balancing accessibility with ethical use.
summary: A new open-source intelligence tool has been released to help pentesters and bug bounty hunters find exposed files on domains. The tool searches certificate transparency logs and allows users to search for exposed files such as env files, git directories, and config files on a given domain.

title: Rats Display Empathetic Behavior in Study
content: A rat first frees a cagemate rat and then shares food with it. Is this animal just as empathetic as humans? But do they have the same capacity for empathy as we humans, or do we differ in that regard?

title: Djokovic extends Wimbledon record with quarter-final victory
content: Djokovic clinches 106th singles victory at Wimbledon39-year-old continues quest for 25th grand slam titleIn his quest to win a record-extending 25th grand slam title, Novak Djokovic cares only about results. How perfectly he plays holds less importance. On Sunday he was pushed hard by the Russian Roman Safiullin, and at times he cut a frustrated figure on Centre Court as his game didn’t flow the way it usually does. But for a record 106th time here, he came out on top, reaching the quarter-finals for the ninth time in a row and a 17th occasion in all. The 39-year-old has now made the quarter-finals of a major tournament 66 times. Djokovic’s 7-6 (6), 6-3, 3-6, 6-3 victory against Safiullin required almost three and a half hours of effort on another warm afternoon in which he was rattled at times, mostly by the performance of the Russian, who played far more like his career-high ranking of 36 than his present mark of 132. Safiullin had two set points at 5-2 in the opening set only to be edged out in a tiebreak and was good enough to take the third set before Djokovic raised his game at the start of the fourth to avoid it going to a decider. Continue reading...
summary: Novak Djokovic has won his 106th singles match at Wimbledon, advancing to the quarter-finals for the ninth consecutive year. The 39-year-old's victory over Roman Safiullin required almost three and a half hours to complete.

title: Australia Regains T20 World Cup Title with Seven-Wicket Win Over England
content: England 150-4, Australia 153-3; Aus win by seven wicketsMooney strikes half-century in final for third timeWell, it was fun while it lasted. Eight months is the time period Australia spent without holding a global trophy – a period which ended on Sunday, when they strolled home in the T20 World Cup final with a seven-wicket win against the hosts England. title: Mr Lif Releases Emergency Rations EP
content:
Definitive Jux, the independent hip‑hop label founded by El‑P, emerged in the early 2000s as a hub for experimental and politically conscious music. The label’s debut release, Mr. Lif’s 2000 EP Enter the Colossus, set the tone for its roster, positioning Lif as the most mainstream‑oriented voice among artists who pushed the genre’s boundaries. El‑P’s vision for the label was clear: to blend avant‑garde production with socially aware lyricism.

In 2002, Mr. Lif followed up with the Emergency Rations EP, a prelude to his full‑length album I, Phantom released just months later. The EP’s opening skit—depicting Lif missing a crucial opportunity—foreshadowed the album’s themes of urgency and self‑reflection. I, Phantom expanded on these ideas, weaving intricate beats with commentary on personal and societal issues, solidifying Mr. Lif’s reputation as a “conscious rapper” within the label’s experimental framework.

The Verge’s coverage of Definitive Jux highlights the label’s brief but influential period, noting how its early releases, especially those by Mr. Lif, shaped the trajectory of alternative hip‑hop. While the label’s prominence has since waned, its legacy endures in the continued relevance of its pioneering artists and the lasting impact of its bold, thought‑provoking catalog.
summary: Mr. Lif's Emergency Rations EP was released in 2002 as a precursor to his full-length album I, Phantom. The EP was part of the Definitive Jux label's lineup, which featured experimental and politically-minded hip hop acts.
author: The Verge

title: England Suffer 45-21 Defeat to South Africa
content:
England’s 45-21 defeat to South Africa, the reigning world champions, has reignited questions over the progress of Steve Borthwick’s squad as they prepare for a crucial showdown with Fiji this weekend. While the loss to the world’s top-ranked team is not uncommon, the manner of the defeat—marked by England’s struggles in key areas such as defense, set-piece accuracy, and intensity—has left critics skeptical about tangible improvement under Borthwick. The result spared England a potential 3-0 series whitewash, with two remaining Tests against the Springboks still to come, but it also underscored the stark gap between the teams, particularly as South Africa capitalized on England’s lapses to dominate the scoreboard.  

Despite post-match optimism about “fine margins” and moments of pressure applied by England in the second quarter, the final scoreline and overall performance have drawn mixed reactions. Analysts note that as the most resourced rugby nation, England faces heightened expectations to challenge for global dominance, yet their current trajectory suggests a disconnect between investment and outcomes. With Fiji next up—a team they are expected to beat more convincingly—Borthwick’s side must demonstrate not only resilience but also the strategic adjustments needed to close the gap against elite opposition. The coming weeks will test whether this England team can evolve beyond familiar shortcomings.
summary: England's rugby team lost 45-21 to South Africa, the world champions, in their recent match. The defeat has raised questions about the progress of Steve Borthwick's side, with England now preparing to face Fiji in their next match.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Vizio launches 65‑inch Mini LED Quantum TV for $398 at Walmart
content:
Vizio has released a 65‑inch Mini‑LED Quantum TV priced at $398, marking the company’s return to the high‑end television market after its 2024 acquisition by Walmart. The model incorporates quantum‑dot technology, which delivers higher brightness and more accurate color reproduction than conventional LEDs, positioning it as the most affordable quantum‑dot TV on the market.

Despite the low price and advanced display technology, reviewers note that the TV’s overall performance aligns more closely with a “dumb” television than a premium smart TV. The operating system is functional but largely unnecessary, and the device’s feature set is minimal compared to competitors. Nonetheless, the combination of Mini‑LED backlighting, quantum dots, and a budget price makes it a compelling choice for consumers seeking high‑quality picture quality without the cost of a flagship model.

The 65‑inch Mini‑LED Quantum TV is available for purchase at Walmart for $398. It represents Vizio’s strategy to offer cutting‑edge display technology at a price point that appeals to budget‑conscious buyers while reinforcing the brand’s presence in the competitive TV market.
summary: Vizio introduced a 65‑inch Mini LED Quantum TV priced at $398, sold through Walmart. The set features quantum‑dot technology and runs Vizio’s OS, though reviewers note it can function effectively without using smart features.

title: King Arthur partners with Sourdough Sidekick to automate starter feeding
content:
The Sourdough Sidekick, a new kitchen gadget co‑developed with King Arthur Baking Company, aims to simplify one of the most tedious aspects of sourdough baking: starter maintenance. The device, branded with King Arthur flour, automatically feeds a sourdough starter with flour and water on a preset schedule, ensuring the culture is ready exactly when the baker wants to begin kneading and shaping.

Sourdough bread relies on natural fermentation and wild yeast, a process that traditionally demands daily attention and a steady supply of starter. By handling the feeding routine, the Sidekick lets bakers focus on the creative steps of dough preparation while still preserving the authenticity of traditional sourdough. The product is marketed as a single‑purpose tool, and its value will depend on how often a user engages in sourdough baking.

Overall, the Sourdough Sidekick offers a practical solution for enthusiasts who want to keep the artisanal qualities of sourdough without the repetitive upkeep. Its partnership with King Arthur Baking Company underscores the brand’s commitment to supporting home bakers, though the gadget’s appeal will hinge on regular usage to justify the investment.
summary: The Sourdough Sidekick, co‑developed with King Arthur Baking Company, is a kitchen gadget that automates sourdough starter management. It dispenses flour and water on a set schedule, keeping the starter ready for baking.

title: Spain study finds immigrant crime rates equal natives when age and gender matched

title: Hubble Images 2,500 Young Stars in LH 95 Stellar Nursery
content:
The Hubble Space Telescope has delivered a striking image of the star‑forming region LH 95, located in the Large Magellanic Cloud, where roughly 2,500 nascent stars are still accreting material. The observation reveals a dense cluster of young objects still gathering gas and dust, a process that can persist for several million years and thereby prolong a critical phase of stellar evolution.

Analysis of the data shows that LH 95 hosts multiple stellar generations coexisting in close proximity, providing empirical evidence of staggered star formation within a single nebular complex. The extended accretion periods and overlapping ages suggest that star‑forming environments can sustain prolonged growth and successive bursts of activity, offering new constraints for models of how stars and clusters develop over time.
summary: Hubble captured a view of LH 95, a stellar nursery with about 2,500 young stars that continue to accrete gas and dust for millions of years. The region also hosts multiple generations of stars, providing insights into the timeline of star formation.

title: England Faces Mexico in World Cup Match
content:
England’s World Cup campaign enters a pivotal phase as manager Gareth Southgate seeks composure and focus from his side ahead of Sunday’s last-16 clash against Mexico. Following a high-intensity 2-1 victory over DR Congo, which left players visibly fatigued, Southgate faces the challenge of maintaining discipline and tactical cohesion in a match widely regarded as the most anticipated in Mexico’s tournament history. The Three Lions’ opponents, having secured their place with a 3-1 win against Ecuador, arrive at the Azteca Stadium brimming with confidence and the backing of a fervent home crowd.  

Complicating preparations is a logistical battle over the match’s timing. Initially, concerns over an incoming storm in Mexico City prompted discussions to move the 6pm local kick-off (1am BST) to midday to avoid potential flooding. Despite extensive deliberations involving FIFA, local authorities, and stakeholders, the decision was ultimately upheld, leaving the original schedule unchanged. The unresolved tension highlights the complexities of hosting a World Cup match in a volatile weather environment, though neither team will have the luxury of adjusting to a new timeframe. With both sides aware of the high stakes, the focus now shifts to navigating the Azteca’s electric atmosphere and delivering under pressure.
summary: England is set to play Mexico in a World Cup last-16 showdown on Sunday, with the match scheduled to take place at 6pm local time. The game is considered one of the biggest in Mexico's history, and the team's head coach is striving to keep his side composed amid the intense atmosphere.
author: Guardian Sport

title: France Beats Paraguay 1-0
content:
France secured a 1-0 victory over Paraguay in a World Cup clash marked by tactical adjustments due to Philadelphia’s sweltering Independence Day heatwave. Despite scaling back their intensity, the French side, led by Kylian Mbappé, proved too resilient for a Paraguayan team that struggled to trouble the hosts. Mbappé’s decisive penalty, his 18th goal in World Cup history, leveled his tally with Lionel Messi in the Golden Boot race but left him one goal shy of Just Fontaine’s all-time tournament scoring record. The match, played under stifling conditions, saw Les Bleus maintain control while Paraguay offered limited resistance, echoing their 1998 extra-time triumph over the same opponent.  

The result reinforced France’s status as tournament favorites, though their performance lacked the flair of their 1998 victory or the dominance of Fontaine’s 1958 hat-trick. Mbappé’s clinical finish underscored his growing legacy, yet the absence of a second goal highlighted the challenges posed by the extreme weather and Paraguay’s defensive resilience. For Paraguay, the defeat underscored their inability to capitalize on physical clashes or disrupt France’s structure, leaving them with little to take from the encounter. The win, while hard-earned, solidified France’s position at the summit of Group D and set the stage for Mbappé’s pursuit of history in the tournament’s latter stages.
summary: France defeated Paraguay 1-0 with a penalty goal from Kylian Mbappé, who is now level with Lionel Messi in the Golden Boot race. The match was played in hot weather conditions in Philadelphia, with France's goal being enough to secure the win.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Morocco Advances to World Cup Quarter-Finals, Eliminates Canada
content:
Morocco made history by becoming the first African team to reach the World Cup quarter-finals twice, advancing to the 2026 tournament’s final eight stages under coach Azzedine Ounahi. The achievement, marked by a second-half goal from Ounahi himself, underscores a resurgence for the North African side, which has shown improved form since replacing Walid Regragui, the nation’s most successful coach. Regragui, who led Morocco to a historic World Cup semi-final in 2022, was succeeded in February amid controversy, though his legacy remains defined by a 49-game tenure with just four losses, including defeats in the 2022 semi-final to France and a third-place playoff against Croatia.  

Regraggi’s departure sparked debate, particularly following Morocco’s 2025 Africa Cup of Nations campaign, which the host nation may have won on appeal after a disputed refereeing decision. Critics questioned his defensive tactics, but supporters argue they reflected a pragmatic approach suited to Morocco’s style. Ounahi, tasked with building on this foundation, has overseen a team now playing with renewed confidence, though surpassing Regragui’s record remains a challenge. As Morocco advances in the World Cup, the focus shifts to whether this new era can sustain the nation’s global football prominence.
summary: Morocco reached the World Cup quarter-finals for the second time, becoming the first African team to achieve this feat twice. Azzedine Ounahi scored the goal that put Morocco ahead early in the second half against Canada, securing their spot in the quarter-finals.

The company's Link spacecraft launched Friday with the goal of intercepting Swift, which has no propulsion system, and boosting its orbit back to its original position. Right now, Swift is circling at an altitude of 224 miles, and Link is aiming to raise that by about 150 miles. title: Harry Kane Leads England by Example Ahead of World Cup Match Against Mexico
content:
England captain Harry Kane has expressed confidence in his physical condition ahead of the team’s upcoming match against Mexico, though he has cautioned that a gritty performance may be required to secure a result. The warning comes as former France striker Thierry Henry highlighted the technical brilliance of Kane’s second goal against the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), praising the England forward’s ability to execute a complex strike under pressure. Henry, appearing on Fox, emphasized the difficulty of Kane’s finishing technique, noting the balance and precision required to redirect a shot with the inside of the foot while off-balance late in the game.  

Kane’s display against the DRC underscored his growing form, with Henry drawing comparisons to his own career by acknowledging the physical toll of replicating such a maneuver. The analysis reinforced Kane’s status as a key asset for England, whose manager Gareth Southgate has stressed the importance of adaptability in facing Mexico’s defensive resilience. With the World Cup knockout stages looming, Kane’s leadership and clinical finishing will be critical, though the team’s preparation suggests they are bracing for a challenging contest against a Mexican side known for its tactical discipline. As England seeks to advance, balancing Kane’s creativity with collective determination will define their prospects.
summary: England captain Harry Kane is reportedly feeling fitter than ever, which could be beneficial for the team's World Cup mission. England is set to face Mexico in their next World Cup match, where Kane has warned that the team may have to "grind it out" to secure a win.

title: US Marks 250th Anniversary of Declaration of Independence
content:
This weekend the United States observes the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, a document that has become a cornerstone of modern democratic thought. Adopted on July 4, 1776, the text formally announced the colonies’ separation from Britain and set forth principles that have shaped political discourse worldwide.

The Declaration famously asserts that governments derive their authority from the consent of the governed and that all individuals possess unalienable rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. These ideas have served as a blueprint for numerous independence and reform movements, influencing constitutional frameworks and human‑rights declarations across continents.

As the nation marks this milestone, scholars and officials alike highlight the document’s enduring legacy. Its articulation of self‑governance and individual rights continues to inspire democratic aspirations and legal reforms in countries seeking to expand civil liberties and participatory governance.
summary: This weekend the United States celebrated 250 years since the adoption of the Declaration of Independence, a foundational political document that asserts government derives power from the consent of the governed. The Declaration's principles of life, liberty, and pursuit of happiness have inspired democratic movements worldwide.

title: Matic Robot Vacuum Price Increase
content:
Matic, the popular robot vacuum‑mop hybrid, will raise its retail price to $1,495 on September 9, up from the current $1,245. The company said the hike reflects a tenfold increase in the cost of memory and other components used in the unit. Customers who purchase directly from Matic will receive a complimentary one‑year supply of replacement bags—worth $96—along with free shipping on each refill of 12 bags. In addition, the return window has been extended from 60 days to six months.

The device, which combines vacuuming and mopping in a single unit, has been highlighted for its “human‑like navigation” and robust suction. Reviewers note that it can navigate complex, three‑story homes with pets, thick rugs and high transitions, and that it continues to operate even when its water tank runs dry. Its self‑cleaning roller mop and disposable water reservoir reduce maintenance, and the unit can run entirely offline, storing maps locally rather than in the cloud. Matic’s new price adjustment comes as the company seeks to offset rising component costs while maintaining its feature set.

For those still interested, the current price of $1,245 remains available directly from Matic, but the price increase will take effect on September 9. The company’s updated warranty and free replacement bag offer aim to offset the higher cost for consumers who choose to buy the robot vacuum‑mop directly from the manufacturer.
summary: The price of Matic's robot vacuum will increase by $250 on September 9th, from $1,245 to $1,495, due to rising component costs. Customers who purchase the vacuum directly from the company will receive a year's worth of replacement bags, valued at $96, at no extra cost.

title: Ikko MindOne Pro: Compact Square Phone Review
content:
The Ikko MindOne Pro, a compact smartphone released this year, has drawn attention for its unconventional design. The device features a square display on a slightly rectangular chassis, a flip‑up camera that can be used for selfies or as a makeshift stand, and a detachable keyboard accessory that includes a magnetic ring and a headphone jack. The Verge reported on the phone’s launch and its distinctive form factor.

In testing the MindOne Pro, reviewers tried a variety of use cases. They ran a minimalist launcher to emulate a “dumb phone” experience, used the phone’s native functions, and experimented with the keyboard case both attached and detached. The camera’s flip‑up mechanism was also assessed for its versatility as a stand or PopSocket substitute. Despite the device’s small size and unique features, the reviewers concluded that the phone failed to meet expectations in practical use.

Overall, the MindOne Pro’s design choices—while innovative—did not translate into a compelling user experience according to the Verge’s review. The phone’s limited functionality and lack of differentiation from more established models suggest it may struggle to find a foothold in a crowded market.
summary: The Ikko MindOne Pro is a compact phone with a square screen and a slightly rectangular body. It includes a flip‑up camera, magnetic keyboard accessory, and headphone jack.
author: The Verge

title: Epomaker RT98: Modular Number Pad Keyboard for Budget Enthusiasts
content:
The Epomaker RT98 mechanical keyboard has drawn attention for its hybrid design that merges retro aesthetics with modern functionality. The board features a CRT‑style display, a modular number pad that can be repositioned to either side, and full VIA compatibility, allowing users to remap keys on the fly. Its keycaps and switches deliver a satisfying typing feel while the overall build remains budget‑friendly.

Designed for users who value both style and ergonomics, the RT98’s moveable tenkey offers a compromise for those who prefer a full numeric keypad but also want to keep a compact footprint. The keyboard’s modularity enables customization without sacrificing the convenience of a dedicated number pad. However, like many entry‑level mechanical keyboards, the RT98 presents certain trade‑offs, including limited durability in high‑usage scenarios and a learning curve for users new to switch‑based typing.

Overall, the RT98 scores a 7 on The Verge’s review, reflecting its solid performance and unique features balanced against its price point and some functional compromises. For enthusiasts seeking a blend of nostalgic design and practical flexibility, the RT98 presents a compelling option within the mid‑range mechanical keyboard market.
summary: The Epomaker RT98 is a mechanical keyboard featuring a modular number pad that can be moved to either side. It also includes a CRT‑like screen, VIA compatibility, and a retro aesthetic, making it a customizable and affordable option for users.

title: Hundreds of thousands attend funeral for Iran's late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei
content:
Hundreds of thousands of mourners assembled in Tehran on Saturday to begin a days‑long funeral for the late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The ceremony, held at the Imam Ali Mosque and other key sites across the capital, marked the formal beginning of state‑sponsored rites that will continue for several days, reflecting the regime’s customary protocol for a figure of Khamenei’s stature.

Tara Kangarlou, a global affairs journalist and author of The Heartbeat of Iran, noted that most of the attendees appeared to be from more emboldened, hardline segments of society. She argued that the composition of the crowd does not mirror the broader public’s attitudes toward the regime, suggesting that the funeral’s turnout may be more a reflection of loyalist enthusiasm than of widespread national sentiment.
summary: Hundreds of thousands of mourners gathered in Tehran for the funeral of Iran's late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Journalist Tara Kangarlou said most attendees were hardline factions of society and not representative of broader public attitudes.

title: Merlin Bird ID App to Contribute to Global Biodiversity Project
content: Cornell Lab for Ornithology plans data linkup between app and population monitoring on eBird platformThe Merlin bird ID app will allow users to feed real-time bird identifications into one of the world’s biggest citizen-science biodiversity projects in an update it is hoped will aid conservation of at-risk birds. Since 2021, the free Merlin app, created by the Cornell Lab for Ornithology, has used machine learning to provide an almost instantaneous sound-identification service for birdsong, along with an image for each bird identified. In future, the detections of bird species recorded by people will be automatically collected on the global online database eBird, which contains more than 2bn bird observation records. Continue reading...
summary: The Cornell Lab for Ornithology's Merlin bird ID app will share its users' bird identifications with the eBird platform, a global online database of bird observations. title: England Face Australia in T20 World Cup Final
content:
The Women’s T20 World Cup final at Lord’s on Sunday pits England against Australia, a team that has dominated women’s cricket with four consecutive world titles. Australia’s captain, Beth Mooney, once dismissed the challenge of defeating her side as nearly impossible, a sentiment England will need to overcome despite the reigning champions’ recent dominance. While teams like South Africa and India have dethroned Australia in major tournaments, the Australians remain confident, having advanced to the final with an undefeated group stage and a commanding semi-final victory over the West Indies.  

Australia’s relaxed approach contrasts with England’s determination to end a 25-year wait for a major trophy. The visitors were spotted at Wimbledon on Thursday, where player Phoebe Litchfield led an “Aussie, Aussie, Aussie” chant, underscoring their self-assuredness. Yet England, buoyed by home advantage and familiarity with Lord’s conditions, view the match as a pivotal opportunity. The outcome will hinge on England’s ability to counter Australia’s formidable batting and bowling depth, while Australia must avoid complacency in a high-stakes clash that could define their legacy in the format.
summary: England will face Australia in the final of the Women's T20 World Cup at Lord's on Sunday. Australia are the favorites to win after a flawless run in the group stages and a convincing semi-final victory over West Indies.

title: Kuxiu D5 Qi Charger Adds Fan to Keep Phones Cool
content:
The Kuxiu D5 Qi2.2 charging dock, priced at $59.99, has drawn attention for its integrated active cooling system that keeps Qi-compatible phones from overheating while charging. The device features a small fan that circulates air around the phone, a design that reviewers say has effectively prevented the temperature rise that typically accompanies wireless charging. The dock also supports simultaneous charging of a smartwatch and earbuds, adding convenience for users who need to power multiple accessories at once.

In a recent hands‑on review, the author noted that the Kuxiu D5’s cooling performance outpaced other Qi chargers they had tested. The reviewer’s personal experience—having previously damaged an iPhone 15 Pro’s logic board due to overheating while editing 4K video on a train—underscored the importance of temperature control. The dock’s fan, while audible, was described as not overly loud and was considered a worthwhile trade‑off for the thermal stability it provides.

Overall, the Kuxiu D5 appears to address a common pain point for wireless charging users: heat buildup. By combining a budget price point with active cooling and multi‑device support, the dock positions itself as a practical option for consumers seeking reliable, quiet charging without the risk of overheating.
summary: The Kuxiu D5 Qi2.2 charging dock features an integrated fan that actively cools phones during charging. After a week of use, the reviewer reported that the dock prevented overheating, outperforming other Qi chargers.

title: Colombia defeat Ghana to reach World Cup last 16
content:
Colombia edged Ghana 1‑0 in the last‑16 of the World Cup, a result that came after a dramatic moment in the seventh minute when Luis Suárez’s number appeared on the field. The 25‑year‑old striker, who shares a name with the handball‑infamous player whose touch cost the Black Stars in 2010, entered the match as a substitute and provided the assist for Jhon Arias’s decisive goal. The win, achieved in Vancouver, set up a quarter‑final tie against Switzerland and marked a return to form for a side that has yet to surpass its 2014 best finish.

Despite failing to score again, Colombia’s performance was deemed deserved, with the team’s superiority evident throughout the game. The victory positions them to challenge for a deeper run, potentially matching the achievement of reaching the last eight in 2014 when they were eliminated by Brazil. The upcoming match against Switzerland will test whether the Colombian side can sustain the momentum and continue its progress on the world stage.

title: Australia Exit World Cup After Penalty Shootout Loss to Egypt
content:
Australia’s 2026 World Cup campaign ended in a painful 4‑2 penalty defeat to Egypt, a result that has left the Socceroos with doubts about their chances to break a long‑standing goal drought. The match’s most visible disappointment fell on 18‑year‑old Lucas Herrington, who had already made history as the youngest player to start a World Cup match for Australia. Herrington’s side‑footed attempt struck the crossbar at a high point, a miss that proved decisive as Egypt converted the remaining kicks.

Immediately after the miss, teammate Awer Mabil ran to Herrington, offering a gesture of solidarity that underscored the emotional weight of the moment. Herrington, visibly shaken, turned his back to the crossbar and placed an arm over his curly hair, a physical sign of the frustration he felt. The incident has already linked Herrington forever to one of the most memorable setbacks in Australian football history, despite his age and potential.

With the defeat, Australia will need to regroup and find new opportunities to overcome their goal‑scoring slump in future international fixtures. The experience of the young defender may serve as a learning point for the squad, while the national team will look to its coaching staff and senior players to chart a path forward in the aftermath of the loss.
summary: Australia were eliminated from the World Cup after a penalty shootout loss to Egypt. 18‑year‑old Lucas Herrington missed a penalty, ending his debut World Cup campaign.

title: Australia lags in adopting health risk prediction tools, study finds
content:
A review by researchers at Curtin University, published in The Lancet Regional Health – Western Pacific, finds that a growing suite of predictive health tools developed in Australia is seldom incorporated into routine clinical practice. The analysis identified a range of instruments capable of estimating an individual’s risk of serious outcomes such as heart disease, falls, frailty and complications from diabetes, yet most health services do not employ them as part of standard care pathways.

The study highlights a gap between technological capability and implementation, noting that despite the tools’ potential to enable earlier interventions, their adoption remains limited across the health system. The authors suggest that broader integration of these predictive models could improve preventive strategies, but achieving this will require systematic uptake by clinicians and policymakers.
summary: A review by Curtin University published in The Lancet Regional Health – Western Pacific found that Australia has developed a growing number of tools to predict risks of conditions such as heart disease, falls, frailty and diabetes complications. However, the study reported that these tools are rarely used in routine health care services.

title: Egypt Advances to World Cup Last 16 With Penalty Shootout Win Over Australia
content: Hossam Abdelmaguid puffed out his cheeks, began his run up with exaggerated slowness, checked and then, as Mat Ryan fell to his left, put the ball to his right. Harry Souttar and the 18-year-old Lucas Herrington had already missed for Australia and Egypt, having scored all of their penalties, were through. Abdelmaguid ran off to the corner, ripping off his shirt, and was soon joined by an ecstatic posse of Egyptian players. Mohamed Salah, who had converted a Panenka, was in tears, and the manager Hossam Hassan was in tears. Don’t worry about the scrappy, largely formless game from which the emotion stemmed: Egypt had won a World Cup knockout tie for the first time.“My heart and soul are with the Palestinian people,” said Hassan. “I thank them and dedicate this victory to them. We succeeded in making Arab people proud. I wanted to win for the sake of the good people. God is honouring us because of the good people who are here.” Continue reading...

title: Blurred Lines Between Wakefulness and Sleep Revealed
content: Tonight, as you close your eyes in bed, something strange will happen to you: Your mind will drift from an ordinary thought to a dream, but it will be impossible to say exactly when it happened. We tend to imagine that the boundary between being asleep and awake is clear: When we are awake, we think; when we are asleep, we dream. Yet, in our study, published in Cell Reports, we show that this boundary is more porous than you think. You can dream before falling asleep and plan your day ahead after drifting off.

title: Adenomyosis Atlas Identifies Targeted Treatment Possibilities
content: Researchers at the University of Liverpool have identified distinctive biological characteristics within adenomyosis lesions that could help pave the way for more targeted, less invasive treatments. The findings from a team based in Professor Dharani Hapangama's gynecology research group at the university provide new insights into the common but often underrecognized condition that affects up to 1 in 5 women of reproductive age. Despite its prevalence and significant impact on health and quality of life, adenomyosis has historically received limited attention in research and clinical practice.

Further studies have yet to clarify the extent to which the results can be transferred to real shopping situations.

title: Programmed Cell Death Mechanism
content: Unlike accidental cell death, some cells can actively decide to die through a controlled process. This is called programmed cell death and can occur in different forms, including apoptosis and necroptosis. Cells use this process when they are damaged, stressed, becoming cancerous, or infected by harmful microbes. This self-destruction mechanism helps to protect the body, but it is also involved in many diseases, such as infections, inflammatory conditions and cancer.
summary: Programmed cell death is a controlled process where cells actively decide to die, occurring in forms such as apoptosis and necroptosis. This self-destruction mechanism helps protect the body by eliminating damaged or cancerous cells, but it is also involved in various diseases, including infections and inflammatory conditions.

title: Tropical Forest Degradation's Impact on Global Carbon Cycle
content: Tropical moist forests account for 70% of global living biomass. Deforestation and degradation—that is, the partial damage to tree stands—as well as the subsequent regeneration of forests therefore play a pivotal role in the global carbon cycle. While the effects of large-scale tropical deforestation are well understood, the impacts of forest degradation have remained highly uncertain until now.

title: Mice Found to Use Complex Smell Processing System
content: Picture a mouse taking rapid, staccato sniffs of a crumb it's found while foraging for food. Now compare that with a human leaning in for a single, deep inhale to gauge whether a cantaloupe is ripe. New research from Northwestern University has found that, like humans, mice also can take a single sniff to deliberately probe their environment—something scientists previously did not know.
summary: Researchers at Northwestern University have discovered that mice can deliberately take a single sniff to probe their environment, a previously unknown ability. This finding suggests that mammals, including mice and humans, share a common underlying system for processing smells, which has been preserved through evolution.

title: Amazon Adds 4GB RAM to Fire HD 10 32GB Tablet
content:
Amazon has quietly refreshed its Fire HD 10 tablet, the model that first appeared in 2023. While the Fire HD 8, launched in 2024, marked the last new entry in the company’s budget‑focused lineup, the updated Fire HD 10 now offers a higher‑performance configuration for its 32‑GB storage variant. The device now ships with 4 GB of RAM instead of the previous 3 GB, and its price has risen from $139.99 to $154.99.

The 64‑GB version remains unchanged, still equipped with 3 GB of RAM, and all other specifications are identical to the earlier release: a 10.1‑inch screen with a 1,920 × 1,200 resolution, an 8‑core 2 GHz processor, a 13‑hour battery life, and microSD expansion support. The modest upgrade focuses solely on the lower‑storage model, providing a modest performance boost for users who need more memory without a full redesign.

With this incremental update, Amazon appears to be fine‑tuning its existing tablet line rather than introducing a new generation. The refreshed Fire HD 10 offers a slightly better experience for budget shoppers who require the 32‑GB option, while the broader feature set remains consistent across the lineup.
summary: Amazon Adds 4GB RAM to Fire HD 10 32GB Tablet.

summary: A significant portion of adults rely on social media to make health decisions, despite widespread concerns about the accuracy of information on these platforms. title: Lewis Hamilton Returns to Silverstone for British Grand Prix
content:
Lewis Hamilton returned to Silverstone this weekend with renewed determination, showcasing his enduring mastery at the British Grand Prix circuit where he holds an unparalleled record of nine victories. The seven-time world champion, visibly relaxed and engaged, appeared to relish the opportunity to silence critics who have questioned his recent form, as he prepared for Sunday’s race on home soil. Silverstone, where his career-defining triumphs began in 2007, remains a site of mutual affection between Hamilton and the fans, with his success there cementing its status as his most iconic stronghold.  

Hamilton’s nine wins at the venue—unmatched by any driver in Formula 1 history—underscore his deep connection to the track, a relationship forged over 17 years of racing. His performance this weekend not only highlights his resilience amid evolving competition but also reinforces Silverstone’s role as a stage where his legacy intertwines with the sport’s history. As the British Grand Prix approaches, Hamilton’s presence underscores the event’s significance as both a personal milestone and a testament to his enduring influence in the sport.
summary: Lewis Hamilton is set to return to Silverstone for the British Grand Prix, a circuit where he has a record nine wins since his debut in 2007. Hamilton has reportedly regained his passion for racing and is expected to be a strong contender at this weekend's event.

title: Ovaries May Have Immune System Role After Menopause
content: For most women, the body begins to change dramatically in their 40s or 50s. This transition, known as menopause, is defined as 12 consecutive months without a menstrual period, marking the end of the reproductive years. While researchers are aware of the functions the ovaries perform during active reproductive years, what happens to the organ after menopause is largely a mystery.
summary: The ovaries cease functioning as reproductive organs after menopause, which typically occurs in women in their 40s or 50s. Research suggests that the ovaries may have an additional role in the immune system after their reproductive years have ended.

title: Yoga, Omega-3 May Offer Alternative to Therapy for Pregnant Depression
content: Globally, nearly 1 in 3 pregnant women experience depression, with most receiving no treatment. When they do get support, they're often steered toward talking therapies such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) or mindfulness as the default option. A comprehensive review of different options to help pregnant women with depression has shown that approaches such as yoga and omega-3 supplementation are as effective as psychological therapies.
summary: A global review found that yoga and omega-3 supplementation are effective in treating depression in pregnant women. This alternative approach may offer a viable option for women who do not receive standard psychological therapies.

title: New tumor map identifies high-risk B-cell lymphoma standard therapy may miss

By combining genetic and proteomic analyses, the scientists identified biological characteristics of tumors, particularly in high-risk patients for whom standard therapy offers little chance of cure. In the future, such patients could receive alternative, more effective therapies directly. In addition, experimental laboratory research provided initial clues to potential therapeutic targets. The study is published in Cancer Cell.
summary: New tumor map identifies high-risk B-cell lymphoma standard therapy may miss.

title: Strawberry Growers in North Carolina Face Fungal Pathogen Threat
content: A few years ago, Austin Wrenn noticed something unsettling in his strawberry greenhouses at Wrenn's Farm in Zebulon, North Carolina. He was one of the first growers in the state to experience losses from an unexpected, aggressive fungal pathogen known as Neopestalotiopsis, or Neo-P.
summary: Neopestalotiopsis, a fungal pathogen, has been causing significant losses in strawberry crops in North Carolina, with Wrenn's Farm being one of the first affected growers. The exact origin and spread of the pathogen are still under investigation by agricultural experts.

title: Integrating Transformative Competencies into University Degree Programs
content: Enabling people to reflect critically on societal changes and participate in meeting major challenges is the purpose of teaching transformative competencies. In a Perspective article published in the journal npj Climate Action, Dr. Nicole Aeschbach has examined how this approach can be systematically embedded in existing degree programs. The Heidelberg University scholar has developed a conceptual framework connecting research, teaching and learning in such a way that university education can empower students to engage in science-based reflection beyond their disciplinary context and enable them to become personally active.
summary: A Perspective article in npj Climate Action explores ways to incorporate transformative competencies into existing university degree programs. Dr. Nicole Aeschbach, a scholar from Heidelberg University, has developed a conceptual framework to empower students to engage in science-based reflection and become personally active in addressing societal challenges.

title: Scientists Discover Neurotransmitter Communication in Immune Cells
content: Researchers at the University of Münster and Ruhr University Bochum have demonstrated for the first time in real time that the body's own defense cells use catecholamines—neurotransmitters such as dopamine and adrenaline—to communicate via the same chemical signals as nerve cells. This discovery opens up a new understanding of how the immune system is regulated. The study has been published in Advanced Science.
summary: Researchers at the University of Münster and Ruhr University Bochum have found that immune cells use neurotransmitters like dopamine and adrenaline to communicate. This discovery, published in Advanced Science, sheds new light on how the immune system is regulated.

title: Haringvliet Sluices Study Reveals Migratory Fish Passage Patterns
content: A new study published in Movement Ecology describes how migratory fish passed through the Haringvliet Sluices before the introduction of Kierbeheer (the partial opening of the Haringvliet Sluices to allow limited saltwater intrusion and facilitate fish migration). The analysis, based on data from tagged fish collected between 1996 and 2018, provides an important reference point for follow-up studies on the effects of Kierbeheer on fish migration.
summary: A new study analyzed 18 years of data to understand the migratory patterns of salmon, trout, and lamprey at the Haringvliet Sluices before the introduction of Kierbeheer in 1996. The study, published in Movement Ecology, provides a reference point for future research on the effects of Kierbeheer on fish migration.

title: Long-lived Radio Emission Observed Near Supermassive Black Hole

They are the result of processes that take place under extreme physical conditions. While most radio transients associated with galactic centers last only days or weeks, the galaxy SDSS J110546.07+145202.4 has been shining very brightly in radio light for several years—the first source of its kind.
summary: Long-lived Radio Emission Observed Near Supermassive Black Hole.

title: France Heatwave Sparks Air Conditioning Debate
content: Tens of millions of people suffered and thousands died during a historic heatwave in France. title: Norway Surpasses Previous Successes, Faces Brazil in World Cup Reunion
content: Ståle Solbakken’s side have surpassed previous golden generation as they prepare to meet team they beat in 1998For a country of 5.6 million people, Norway’s list of competitive achievements is remarkable. Our Winter Olympians gobble up medals at a freakish rate, our women’s handball team is all-conquering, we’ve had standout successes in athletics such as the Ingebrigtsen brothers, we’ve had two tournament winners on this season’s PGA tour and, improbably, Norway has also produced the greatest chess player of all time. And while these successes are cherished and celebrated, nothing unites the country quite like football – and no match has stopped the country in its tracks quite like the 2-1 win against Brazil in the final group game of the 1998 World Cup. The sound of commentator Arne Scheie announcing “Vi har scoret i Marseille!” (“We have scored in Marseille!”) is as firmly etched into our brains as much as anything said by Norwegian poets and politicians in the last 50 years. Scheie was already something of a national treasure, a commentator known for his level-headedness and factual rigour, but when Norway won a late penalty with the score 1-1 he lost the run of himself entirely. He referred to the penalty taker, the Hertha Berlin midfielder Kjetil Rekdal as “Kjetil Reknett, of Werder Bremen” (Reknett is not a surname in Norwegian or, as far as I am aware, any other language). Continue reading...

title: Safiullin Upsets Fonseca at Wimbledon 2026

Tennis Update from Wimbledon: Drama and Comebacks

At the ongoing Wimbledon championships, several matches witnessed dramatic turns on Friday. Initially, Kalinskaya's left hamstring injury raised concerns, but after receiving treatment, she regained her form and fought back to reach 15-40 on Bencic's serve in the second set. Bencic, however, held her serve, securing four consecutive points to maintain a 6-4, 4-4 lead.

In another match, Andrey Safiullin faced off against Pedro Sakamoto Fonseca, with the Russian qualifier making a convincing start. Safiullin broke Fonseca's serve early on, securing a 6-3, 0-15 lead and eventually won the set 6-3. However, Fonseca, who had previously come from two sets down to defeat Novak Djokovic at the French Open, remains a force to be reckoned with. The 19-year-old Brazilian player will be hoping to draw on the spirit of that memorable victory and mount a comeback against Safiullin.

The ongoing matches at the Wimbledon championships continue to showcase the resilience and determination of the players. As the tournament progresses, fans can expect to witness more thrilling comebacks and dramatic turns, making this year's Wimbledon an exciting and unpredictable event.

title: France Awaits First Tour De France Champion Since 1986
content:
Paul Seixas, a 19-year-old French cyclist, has emerged as a symbol of renewed hope for a nation that has endured four decades of frustration in the Tour de France. With the weight of history on his shoulders, Seixas aims to break a cycle dating back to 1990, when Laurent Fignon’s final Tour ended in disappointment, marking the last time a French rider claimed victory. Since Bernard Hinault’s fifth title in 1985, France’s cycling legacy has been defined by near-misses and unfulfilled potential, as rising stars like Richard Virenque, Romain Bardet, and Thibaut Pinot have fallen short under the scrutiny of national expectations.  

The Tour’s evolution since Fignon’s era has seen France’s contenders grapple with shifting dynamics in the sport, from technological advancements to the dominance of international teams. Each generation has produced promising talents, yet none have overcome the psychological and physical hurdles of the race. Seixas’s ascent comes amid a backdrop of contrasting weather—where the current heatwave gripping France contrasts sharply with the cold, wet conditions Fignon faced in 1990. His young age and raw talent have sparked cautious optimism, though the legacy of past failures looms large. For French cycling, the stakes are clear: a victory would not only crown a prodigy but also heal a national narrative shaped by decades of near-misses and fading dreams.
summary: France has not had a Tour de France champion since Bernard Hinault in 1986, with several promising cyclists emerging but ultimately failing to succeed. Paul Seixas, a 19-year-old cyclist, is now bidding to end this four-decade wait for a French Tour de France champion.

title: Environmental Chemicals Linked to Disease Risk
content: From the air we breathe to the food we eat, we are constantly exposed to thousands of chemicals—yet how these exposures affect our health has remained surprisingly difficult to understand. A new study led by researchers at the CeMM Research Center for Molecular Medicine of the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Ludwig Boltzmann Institute for Network Medicine at the University of Vienna, published in Nature Communications, offers a unifying view: Diverse substances can disrupt the same biological systems and thereby contribute to disease risk in predictable ways.
