title: Venezuela Earthquake Rescue Efforts Continue Amid Criticism of Response
content:
Rescuers have been sifting through rubble across Venezuela for eight days following two powerful earthquakes that struck the country, a search that is now yielding diminishing prospects of finding survivors. The twin tremors, which together have claimed more than 2,000 lives, have left extensive damage in multiple regions, prompting a massive, ongoing relief operation that continues to dig for any remaining victims amid increasingly slim odds of finding those still alive.  

Amid the disaster, Interim President Delcy Rodríguez dismissed accusations that the government’s response was delayed, rejecting criticism that officials acted too slowly in the aftermath. The administration has defended its actions while facing widespread scrutiny from domestic and international observers regarding the speed and coordination of emergency aid and recovery efforts.
summary: Rescuers are still searching for survivors eight days after two major earthquakes in Venezuela, but the chances of finding survivors are diminishing. Interim President Delcy Rodriguez has denied that the government responded too slowly to the disaster.

title: Portugal through to face Spain after VAR decision, Salah fit for Australia match
content:
The opening match of the World Cup on Friday saw Australia’s Socceroos face Egypt, a game that drew record-breaking viewership in the United States.  Fox Sports reported an average audience of 24.429 million viewers, making it the most-watched English‑language soccer broadcast in U.S. history, with a peak of 31.883 million at one point during the match.  Telemundo, carrying the Spanish‑language rights, logged 9.1 million viewers over the entire game window.

Australia’s coach, Tony Popovic, prepared his squad for both scenarios regarding Egyptian striker Mohamed Salah, noting that the team had trained for the possibility of Salah playing and for the alternative if he were absent.  “We have prepared for Salah playing, we’ve seen when he’s not on the pitch the players in those positions where he may play,” Popovic said, emphasizing the squad’s readiness to adapt to any lineup changes.

The match set a new benchmark for World Cup viewership in the U.S., underscoring the tournament’s growing popularity across both English and Spanish audiences.  As the tournament progresses, broadcasters and teams alike will continue to monitor and respond to the high engagement levels that define this global event.

title: Portugal Advances to World Cup Last 16
content: Rafael Leão dropped to his knees. His cross had just been flicked into the net by Gonçalo Ramos to take Portugal to the last 16 of the World Cup. Leão’s expression was not one of delight, but relief. Billed as the last dance for two footballing icons, it was Luka Modrić who, at the age of 40, had to leave what will surely be his final World Cup. Cristiano Ronaldo, meanwhile, plays on, and both scored and was even substituted in a match of endless incident. But this was a contest about more than two individuals, who were far from the most influential players on show, even if Ronaldo was bewilderingly named player of the match. Instead this was an old-fashioned World Cup battle between hardened teams, with momentum swinging first one way then the other then back again. It was also a match stuffed with incident, including – for the first time in World Cup history – a total of four disallowed goals, one of them denying Croatia an equaliser in the very last second of the match. title: Madonna Releases Confessions II Album
content: (Warner)After years spent chasing trends like trap and Latin pop, Madonna settles back​ nicely into​ old-school dance music to tell vivid vignettes of life in 80s New York‘Ask yourself this – what are you doing it for? / Is it for you? Is it for them?” ponders Madonna during Bring Your Love, a collaboration with Sabrina Carpenter from Confessions II. It’s a question you could ask of her decision to release a follow-up to 2005’s Confessions on a Dance Floor 21 years on. The official line is, of course, that it’s for her. Confessions II was inspired by Madonna’s 2023 Celebration tour, a rampage through her back catalogue – with staging that recreated the videos for old hits including Don’t Tell Me and Human Nature – that apparently set the singer thinking about her past. Certainly, Confessions II is rich with references to Madonna’s history, and not only the album from which it borrows its title and its initial structure, a sequence of house-influenced tracks that segue into each other like a DJ mix. There’s also the trip-hop-inspired Madonna of Bedtime Stories (the album concludes with a suite of slower, more introspective material); the club-hopping, fame-hungry Madonna of her 1982 debut single Everybody, who keeps cropping up in the lyrics; and the maternal, spiritually inclined Madonna of Ray of Light. The Test, a duet with her daughter Lourdes, is an older, wiser sequel to that album’s lullaby-like Little Star, alluded to in its opening lines. Continue reading...
summary: Madonna's new album Confessions II is a follow-up to her 2005 album Confessions on a Dance Floor and features a mix of house-influenced tracks and slower material. The album was inspired by her 2023 Celebration tour and includes collaborations with artists such as Sabrina Carpenter and her daughter Lourdes.

title: Rhythm Heaven Groove Review
content:
Nintendo has revived its beloved Rhythm Heaven series with Rhythm Heaven Groove (Rhythm Paradise Groove in PAL regions), marking a return to the studio’s signature formula of bite-sized, rhythm-driven mini-games. After a seven-year hiatus since the last entry, the new title embraces the genre’s enduring appeal by blending whimsical gameplay with tight, music-based mechanics. Players navigate a variety of quirky challenges—ranging from catching floating vegetables to conversing with extraterrestrials—by syncing button presses to auditory cues, all while navigating increasingly complex patterns. The game’s design emphasizes accessibility and variety, offering a vibrant, low-pressure alternative to more intense rhythm experiences.  

The release arrives amid a broader resurgence of rhythm games, with titles like Hi-Fi Rush and Fortnite’s rhythm action mode reinvigorating the space. While Rhythm Heaven Groove retains the core principles of its predecessors, it adapts to modern expectations by streamlining its approach. Each of its mini-games operates as a self-contained, colorful vignette, prioritizing creativity over technical precision. This aligns with the genre’s evolving identity, where rhythm mechanics intersect with diverse gameplay styles, from dance routines to puzzle-solving. As the series returns, it underscores rhythm’s enduring role as a bridge between music and interactive entertainment, offering a playful yet polished entry for both longtime fans and newcomers.
summary: Rhythm Heaven Groove is a collection of vibrant rhythm games for the Nintendo Switch that offers bitesize, rhythm-based experiences with various mini-games. The game features a range of activities, including catching veggies, practising dance choreographies, and speaking to an alien, all controlled with just a few buttons.

title: Purine‑rich DNA sequences shield Bacillus subtilis genes from Rho termination
content: In the study of bacteria, a longstanding dogma has held that two molecular machines—RNA polymerase, which leads the way in transcribing DNA into RNA, and ribosomes, which bring up the rear translating RNA into proteins—worked so closely in tandem that they were effectively attached. This close coupling of transcription and translation in bacteria was thought to be fundamental to gene expression, in part because the trailing ribosome could shield nascent gene products from an effective and omnipresent quality-control protein called Rho.
summary: Researchers discovered that purine‑heavy DNA regions in Bacillus subtilis decrease Rho‑dependent transcription termination. The finding indicates that protection of nascent transcripts can occur without tight transcription‑translation coupling.

title: Sitting Over 30 Minutes Increases Cancer Death Risk, Study Finds
content:
A new longitudinal study of more than 90,000 adults tracked over ten years has found that sitting or lying down while awake for periods longer than 30 minutes each day is linked to a higher risk of death from cancer. The researchers observed that each additional hour of uninterrupted inactivity corresponded with a measurable increase in cancer‑related mortality, suggesting that even modest extensions of sedentary time can have serious health consequences.

The analysis also indicated that incorporating light physical tasks—such as ironing, standing while cooking, or brief walks—may offset some of the risk associated with prolonged sitting. While the study does not establish a causal relationship, it underscores the potential benefits of breaking up sedentary periods with low‑intensity activity. Health officials are advised to consider these findings when updating guidelines aimed at reducing the adverse effects of sedentary behaviour.
summary: A study of more than 90,000 people over ten years found that sitting or lying down for more than 30 minutes at a time each day was linked to a higher risk of cancer death. The risk rises with each additional hour of continuous inactivity.

title: Weber Cuts Prices on Grills and Griddles Ahead of July 4th
content:
Weber is rolling out a series of discounts on its grills, smokers and griddles ahead of the July 4th holiday, offering price reductions of roughly $50 compared with typical retail listings. The Spirit E‑325, a three‑burner model, is now priced at $499 for propane (regularly $549) and $549 for natural‑gas (regularly $599), providing a 360‑square‑inch cooking area plus a 90‑square‑inch warming rack and two high‑heat searing zones. The Slate 30‑inch rust‑resistant griddle has been cut by $50 to $649, featuring a 500‑degree Fahrenheit surface, wind guards and a capacity for about 22 burgers, while the 17‑inch tabletop version is available for $249 after a similar discount, targeting portable use such as camping. Both the griddle and the Spirit E‑325 are listed on Weber’s website at the reduced rates, with comparable pricing noted at Home Depot and Ace Hardware.

For customers seeking higher‑end equipment, Weber’s Searwood XL 600 pellet grill is $100 off, now $1,199, offering a 972‑square‑inch cooking space, temperature range from 180 °F for smoking to 600 °F for searing, and the ability to handle roughly 20 burgers across its dual layers. A smaller Searwood 600 model is also discounted, though it carries a $200 price gap relative to the XL version. These promotions position Weber’s lineup as a cost‑effective option for both occasional backyard cookouts and more elaborate grilling setups as the summer holiday approaches.
summary: Weber is offering significant markdowns on a range of grills and griddles for the July 4th holiday, with the Spirit E‑325 grill discounted to $499 propane and $549 natural gas. title: Statins narrow cholesterol and blood pressure gaps between obese and healthy-weight adults
content:
A new study has found that among adults over the age of 40, the typical gaps in cholesterol levels and blood pressure between individuals with obesity and those of a healthy weight have largely vanished. Researchers reported that the convergence of these health markers is primarily linked to the widespread use of statin medications among the obese population, which appears to equalize cardiovascular risk profiles across weight categories.

The analysis also noted instances where participants with obesity exhibited more favorable cholesterol or blood pressure readings than their normal‑weight counterparts, suggesting that pharmacological management can offset some of the metabolic disadvantages associated with excess weight. The findings highlight the impact of medication adherence on cardiovascular health outcomes in middle‑aged and older adults, underscoring the importance of treatment strategies alongside lifestyle interventions.
summary: A study of adults over 40 found that cholesterol and blood pressure levels of people with obesity were largely indistinguishable from those of healthy-weight individuals, largely due to statin use. title: Ebola wildlife origins key to preventing future outbreaks
content:
A recent surge of the Andes virus on a cruise ship has drawn attention to the broader threat posed by emerging hemorrhagic fevers. The outbreak, which has produced 13 confirmed cases and three deaths, underscores how quickly a pathogen can spread in close quarters. Meanwhile, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola—responsible for the current epidemic—has continued to circulate quietly, with more than 1,250 reported cases and at least 362 fatalities.

Bundibugyo virus is a highly lethal hemorrhagic disease that manifests abruptly with severe headaches, diarrhea, renal and hepatic failure, and, in some instances, internal and external bleeding. Its transmission remains a concern even after death, as family members preparing bodies for burial can be exposed. The lack of a clearly identified source for either virus hampers containment efforts and heightens the risk to both human populations and wildlife that may act as reservoirs or spillover hosts.

These concurrent outbreaks highlight the critical need for rapid source identification and robust surveillance. Without pinpointing the origins of these viruses, public health authorities cannot fully mitigate the spread to humans or prevent unnecessary harm to animal populations. Continued investment in epidemiological investigation and cross‑sector collaboration will be essential to control current cases and avert future epidemics.
summary: The Bundibugyo strain of Ebola virus is driving an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with more than 1,250 cases and at least 362 deaths. Identifying the virus’s wildlife reservoir is considered essential to reduce human risk and avert future epidemics.

title: British Columbia unveils public lands map identifying thousands of parcels for affordable housing
content:
A new research platform, the B.C. Public Lands Map, is identifying publicly owned parcels that could be repurposed for affordable housing across the province. Early analysis from the tool shows more than 50,000 publicly owned parcels in British Columbia, including vacant government buildings, empty plots and surface parking lots, and estimates that up to 273,000 housing units could be built on underused land in Metro Vancouver alone.

The map is the first of its kind in Canada, integrating federal, provincial and municipal data to highlight prime sites for development. By consolidating information on land ownership and availability, the tool aims to assist policymakers, developers and community groups in locating suitable locations for affordable‑housing projects, potentially easing the region’s housing shortage and informing future land‑use planning.
summary: A new British Columbia Public Lands Map combines federal, provincial and municipal data to pinpoint publicly owned parcels suitable for affordable housing. title: Sponges Contribute to Coral Reef Productivity
content: In marine environments, sponges tend to eat other organisms to get their nutrients. But a study published in Functional Ecology by researchers at the University of Amsterdam's Institute for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Dynamics (IBED), demonstrates how sponges may also use photosynthesis, just like plants. This phenomenon can help with productivity—the amount of energy and food produced—in tropical coral reefs, and perhaps in other ecosystems where sponges are also common.
summary: Researchers at the University of Amsterdam's Institute for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Dynamics found that sponges can use photosynthesis to generate nutrients. The study suggests that sun-powered sponges may produce up to 11% of the productivity in tropical coral reef ecosystems.

title: Novak Djokovic Advances to Third Round at Wimbledon
content:
Novak Djokovic advanced to the third round of the tournament with a commanding 6-3, 6-4, 6-2 victory over 25th seed Arthur Rinderknech, showcasing his enduring form at age 39. The Serbian tennis legend, a seven-time champion at the event, will next face Stefanos Tsitsipas, the 25th seed, after the Greek player secured a straightforward second-round win. Djokovic’s performance underscored his dominance, particularly against a Tsitsipas who has struggled to replicate his peak-level consistency in recent years.  

Once a frequent rival in high-stakes grand slam finals, including the 2021 French Open and 2023 Australian Open, Tsitsipas now finds himself as a significant underdog against Djokovic, having tumbled down the rankings. In their previous encounters, Tsitsipas had led Djokovic by two sets in Paris in 2021, but the tables have turned as Djokovic continues to thrive. This match highlighted the stark contrast in their trajectories, with the Serb’s tactical precision and physical resilience prevailing over Tsitsipas’s fading form. The outcome reinforces Djokovic’s status as a formidable contender, even as challenges from younger stars have reshaped the men’s tennis landscape.
summary: Novak Djokovic won a second-round match at Wimbledon with a score of 6-3, 6-4, 6-2 against Stefanos Tsitsipas. Djokovic will face Arthur Rinderknech, the 25th seed, in the third round of the tournament.

title: Belgium Advances to Last 16 in World Cup with Tielemans Penalty
content: A seesawing classic of a contest had just ticked into the 122nd ­minute, penalties all but a formality, when the referee, Saíd Martínez, wandered back towards the centre circle to award Belgium a stoppage-time penalty. The VAR, Guillermo Pacheco Larios, had highlighted Lamine Kamara swiping away Youri Tielemans’s left ankle in the seconds before Dodi Lukébakio had skimmed the crossbar. For Belgium, it was a get out of jail card, Tielemans converting the spot-kick to propel Rudi Garcia’s side into the last 16. After 85 minutes, they trailed Senegal 2-0. Just as it seemed Belgium would join Germany and the Netherlands in the World Cup departures lounge, Garcia’s side rallied to take an entertaining game to extra time. With an early exit and second-half stoppage time looming, Romelu Lukaku, a half-time substitute, and Tielemans scored a goal apiece as Belgium struck twice in three minutes to cancel out goals by Habib Diarra and Ismaïla Sarr. Continue reading...
summary: Belgium came back from a 2-0 deficit to tie Senegal 2-2 and advance to the last 16 in the World Cup. The game went to extra time before Youri Tielemans scored a penalty in the 122nd minute to secure Belgium's spot in the next round.

title: Mechanical Restraint Linked to Short-Term Blood Clot Risk in Psychiatric Hospitals
content: Mechanical restraint is associated with a small increased short-term risk of blood clots among inpatients at psychiatric hospitals, finds a Danish study published by The BMJ. summary: A Danish study found a small increased short-term risk of blood clots associated with mechanical restraint in psychiatric hospitals. The absolute risk remains low, but the findings support ongoing efforts to reduce mechanical restraint use.

title: Obesity's Impact on Heart Risk Factors in Adults Over 40 Erodes
content: Over the last three decades, differences in unhealthy cholesterol levels and blood pressure between older adults with obesity and those with a normal body mass index (BMI) have narrowed or disappeared in several high-income countries, suggests a study published in The Lancet. The authors propose that this trend is due to the greater, and possibly more intensive, use of cholesterol-lowering medication (such as statins) and blood pressure medication in people older than 40 living with obesity in high-income countries.
summary: A study in The Lancet found that the gap in unhealthy cholesterol levels and blood pressure between adults over 40 with obesity and those with a normal BMI has narrowed in high-income countries. This trend is attributed to increased use of cholesterol-lowering and blood pressure medications in adults over 40 with obesity.

title: Mobile Phone Voice Analysis Detects Asthma and COPD Symptoms

title: New Study Reveals Origins of Defect Peaks in Carbon Materials
content: Carbon materials, such as carbon fibers and activated carbons, are essential across a wide variety of fields, encompassing everything from aerospace engineering to fuel cells and thermal insulation. For decades, Raman, infrared and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) have been the primary tools used to analyze carbon materials. However, because of their diverse structural conditions and inconsistencies in their interpretation, researchers have found it challenging to assign specific spectral peaks to exact, localized chemical structures.
summary: Researchers have been using Raman, infrared and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) to analyze carbon materials for decades, but have struggled to assign specific spectral peaks to exact chemical structures. The study aims to unlock the 'black box' of carbon materials by understanding the origins of defect peaks.
author: Phys.org

title: Reducing Emissions Could Save Thousands of U.S. Lives Annually
content: Published in Nature Climate Change, new research from the University of Wisconsin–Madison finds that reaching net-zero emissions by midcentury would substantially improve public health in the United States. However, climate strategies that heavily depend on carbon dioxide removal are likely to lead to worse pollution, air quality and climate-related premature deaths than scenarios that prioritize direct emissions reductions and rely less on carbon dioxide removal (CDR).
summary: New research from the University of Wisconsin–Madison suggests that reaching net-zero emissions by midcentury could save around 33,000 lives in the United States each year. The study found that prioritizing direct emissions reductions over carbon dioxide removal strategies is likely to improve public health and reduce climate-related deaths.
author: Phys.org

title: Charged dust grains may influence solar corona heating, study reports
content: A researcher at The University of Alabama in Huntsville (UAH), a part of The University of Alabama System, has published a new study in The Astrophysical Journal suggesting that tiny charged dust grains near the sun may significantly influence how energy moves through the solar corona, the outer atmosphere of the sun. The discovery potentially rewrites how scientists understand why the corona is millions of degrees hotter than the surface of the sun itself.
summary: A University of Alabama in Huntsville researcher published a paper in The Astrophysical Journal proposing that tiny charged dust particles near the Sun can significantly affect energy transport in the solar corona. The result could alter current explanations for why the corona is millions of degrees hotter than the Sun’s surface.
author: Phys.org

title: Rise of Antibiotic-Resistant Superbug in Hospitals Tracked Over Decades
content: Decades-old hospital samples have helped University of East Anglia (UEA) researchers uncover how a deadly antibiotic-resistant "superbug" quietly tightened its grip across the globe. It lurked in hospital corridors for decades, largely unnoticed by the wider public.
summary: Researchers at the University of East Anglia analyzed decades-old hospital samples to understand the spread of a deadly antibiotic-resistant superbug. The superbug's presence in hospitals peaked in the mid-2000s after building resistance over several decades.

title: New star activity catalog to aid in exoplanet discovery
content: Searching for habitable worlds beyond our solar system involves more than having a planet orbit within its star's habitable zone, the region where temperatures could be just right for liquid water to exist on the surface. On Earth, where water comprises approximately 75% of the planet's surface, life is abundant. But what about the exoplanet's star, specifically its activity and rotation? How could this influence how exoplanets are identified for current and future missions?
summary: Scientists have developed a new catalog of star activity, which could help identify exoplanets more effectively. The catalog considers factors such as a star's rotation and activity, which can impact the search for habitable worlds beyond our solar system.

title: Early Native Americans Focused on Hunting Megafauna Across Americas
content: New research led by a University of Alaska Fairbanks archaeologist reveals that the earliest Native Americans had highly specialized diets, primarily hunting the largest animals on the landscape, and they targeted these megafauna consistently from Alaska to South America.

title: Microsoft Xbox Division Prepares for Significant Changes and Layoffs
content:
Xbox is undergoing a strategic overhaul under new CEO Asha Sharma and chief content officer Matt Booty, with internal challenges prompting a corporate "reset" and potential restructuring. In a June 10 memo to staff, the executives outlined significant pressures facing the division, including a 3% "accountability margin," soaring component costs driven by memory and storage shortages, and an "over extended" studio system. The same day, reports emerged of planned layoffs in July, with closures or spinoffs of at least five game studios, including possible cancellations of titles like Blade. The Verge and Bloomberg confirmed the cuts, which could see studios such as Hellblade creator Ninja Theory shuttered, while Tom Warren later detailed the risk of losing Blade and developer Arkane.  

Sharma’s leadership has already introduced sweeping changes, including price hikes for Xbox consoles, reduced Game Pass subscriptions with the exclusion of new Call of Duty titles, and a rebranding to "XBOX." The division is also redefining its exclusives strategy, making Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution console-only titles, while exploring "radically different" console business models amid supply chain challenges like the "RAMaggedon" crisis. Microsoft has not ruled out spinning off Xbox entirely, as it navigates financial and operational pressures. Meanwhile, the company continues to balance its gaming portfolio, retaining projects like Hideo Kojima’s OD while facing staff departures and closures at other studios.  

The upheaval reflects a broader effort to streamline operations and prioritize profitability. As Xbox grapples with rising costs and market competition, Sharma’s leadership faces the dual challenge of stabilizing its game development ecosystem while adapting to shifting consumer demands. With layoffs and studio reorganizations imminent, the division’s future hinges on its ability to redefine its strategy without alienating a fanbase increasingly vocal about exclusives, backward compatibility, and online multiplayer access. Microsoft’s next steps will likely determine whether Xbox can navigate this reset toward long-term growth or further consolidation.
summary: Microsoft Xbox Division Prepares for Significant Changes and Layoffs.

title: England Advance to Last 16 with Late Comeback Against DR Congo
content: Thomas Tuchel’s mission to put a second World Cup star on the England shirt did not look as though it would reach the second knockout round. On a fraught and chaotic occasion in Atlanta, his team flirted aggressively with disaster. For 75 minutes, England mixed loose defending with an inability to take their chances. Which were plentiful. The Democratic Republic of the Congo goalkeeper, Lionel Mpasi, had the game of his life. Who needs Lionel Messi. It was easy for England’s long-suffering fans to feel their minds being taken to dark places. Iceland 2016, anyone? They had only ever lost once to an African team – to Senegal in a friendly in June of last year. The DRC, who have brought the romance to this tournament, a team to unite a war-torn nation, led through Brian Cipenga’s seventh-minute goal. They were primed to do something utterly extraordinary. Continue reading...

title: Study shows low-angle subduction zones can generate giant earthquakes contrary to classic theory
content:
A research team headed by Professor Satoshi Ide of the University of Tokyo has shown that the long‑standing theory of earthquake generation fails in regions where tectonic plates subduct at shallow angles. Published in Science Advances, the study demonstrates that the mechanics of fault rupture differ markedly when the downgoing plate dips less steeply, allowing large earthquakes to develop in places previously thought to be too stable for such events.  

The findings clarify why great seismic events have occurred in low‑angle subduction zones and provide a theoretical framework that could broaden the scope of monitoring programs. By identifying previously overlooked structural features that can accommodate significant strain, the research offers a new basis for targeting future observational and risk‑assessment efforts in these vulnerable regions.
summary: Researchers from the University of Tokyo found that classic earthquake generation theory fails in low-angle subduction zones. Their findings, published in Science Advances, explain how giant earthquakes can occur in these areas and suggest expanding observation efforts.

And, in a country with questionable attitudes to gun control, it often ended in tragedy. Continue reading...

You wake up in the mind of a person called Sid at the same time as she’s waking up in the river of a city. You’re coming to understand what you are, why it is that you’re in the mind of this person who doesn’t know that you’re there, along with what your capabilities are, and what the world is, through Sid.” Continue reading...

title: Horror Movies Explore Themes of Therapist Mental Health Struggles
content:
Recent cinema has increasingly spotlighted psychoanalysts as central figures in narratives exploring the fragility of the human psyche, reflecting a growing cultural fascination with the vulnerabilities of those tasked with healing others. Films such as Mary Bronstein’s If I Had Legs I’d Kick You, in which Rose Byrne portrays a therapist spiraling into personal and professional chaos, and Smile (2022), where a psychiatrist confronts a supernatural manifestation of her mental health struggles, underscore a recurring theme: even mental health professionals are not immune to the traumas they seek to address. This trend builds on a long-standing cinematic tradition of therapists as supporting characters, from Good Will Hunting (1997) to The Sopranos, but modern films are now placing them squarely in the role of protagonists grappling with their own unresolved issues.  

The motif gained fresh momentum in late 2023, with UK cinemas screening two notable entries. In Backrooms, Norwegian actress Renate Reinsve delivers a harrowing performance as a once-stable psychiatrist unraveling amid surreal, labyrinthine mental challenges, while Jodie Foster’s A Private Life reimagines the actress as a therapist-turned-detective, driven to investigate a client’s death as a proxy for confronting her own familial failures. These films echo Sigmund Freud’s assertion that analysts must themselves undergo analysis, highlighting the cyclical nature of psychological healing. By casting therapists as both observers and subjects of trauma, cinema interrogates the boundaries between professional expertise and personal vulnerability.  

This shift signals a broader societal reckoning with the complexities of mental health, moving beyond clichéd portrayals of therapists as infallible guides. As filmmakers dismantle the myth of emotional invincibility, they invite audiences to confront uncomfortable truths about the universality of suffering. In doing so, these narratives not only humanize mental health professionals but also reflect a deeper cultural curiosity about the limits of self-understanding—a theme as timeless as psychoanalysis itself.
summary: Recent films such as Smile and If I Had Legs I'd Kick You feature therapists as main characters, showcasing their struggles with mental health and trauma. These movies offer a departure from traditional portrayals of therapists as supporting characters, instead giving them center stage to explore their own psychological complexities.

title: Reese Witherspoon Produces Legally Blonde TV Prequel Starring Lexi Minetree
content: The original star is behind this TV spin-off, and the casting of charismatic Lexi Minetree. Sadly, the tropey script and lack of campness mean it fails to really sparkleIt’s 25 years since you became a bona fide film star. In the intervening quarter of a century you have stayed a respected actor and become a powerhouse producer. An appetite grows for teen-led dramas that for reasons of nostalgia or muscled ice-hockey players appeal to the generation or two above. You are Reese Witherspoon. What do you do? Take down the Legally Blonde IP, dust it off and make a small-screen prequel to the box office hit that became a cult classic, of course! You maximise your chances of success by casting a charismatic mini-me (Lexi Minetree) who can capture all the sassiness and sweetness of the original protagonist, Elle Woods, and recreate the genius of your own performance by making her un-self-aware without being imbecilic. Continue reading...

Maria Avila was working at Brown’s house in Tarzana, California, in 2020 when she was attacked by Hades, a Caucasian shepherd used as a guard dog. At the trial in Van Nuys, California, Avila said she was left with serious injuries to her arm and face, requiring dozens of sutures and skin grafts from her abdomen to her arm. She said was also left with post-traumatic stress disorder, and nerve damage which made it difficult to work. Continue reading...

title: Netflix Experiences Decline in Viewership for Second Seasons of Popular Shows
content: Hit shows like Beef, The Four Seasons, Avatar: The Last Airbender and A Man on the Inside have suffered giant drops for their follow-up seasonsIf you haven’t seen the second season of Netflix’s Avatar: The Last Airbender, then at least you can console yourself that you’re not alone. Variety recently noted that, while season one debuted with 21.2m views in the first four days after its launch in 2024, season two has been viewed just 8.7m times. Which isn’t nothing, but it does mean that the show lost 59% of its audience between seasons. And this would be fine if it was an isolated case, but it is starting to look as if Netflix is struggling across the board when it comes to getting viewers back to shows they once watched in droves. The first season of Tina Fey’s relationship comedy series The Four Seasons had 11.9m views, but the recent second outing only garnered 4.4m; a drop of 63%. The opening week of Beef’s second season gained 2.4m views, a 58% drop from season one. The second season of A Good Girl’s Guide to Murder posted an 80% drop in viewership. And people are only able to estimate the drop in views for Ted Danson’s A Man on the Inside, because the second season didn’t even crack Netflix’s top 10. Continue reading...
summary: Netflix Experiences Decline in Viewership for Second Seasons of Popular Shows.

title: England's Alex Coles Seeks Higher Meaning in Rugby Clash with South Africa
content: The son of two vicars, the smart-cookie Saints forward is eager to front up to South Africa after a chat with their captainThe general view in South Africa is that England do not fully understand what they are up against. To be a Springbok is to represent the hopes and dreams of millions and feel a uniquely powerful force. Siya Kolisi must have been taken aback, consequently, to be approached after a Test at Twickenham by a young English opponent seeking to arrange a chat on the subject of racial unity. The curious Englishman was the Northampton forward Alex Coles, a player far removed from the average rugby jock. The son of two Church of England vicars – his mum, Olivia, writes her sermons on a Friday so she can attend his Saturday matches – he is a similarly firm believer in having a purpose in life beyond the weekend result. Continue reading...

content: Updates from Wednesday’s action in SW19 Order of play | Joint ends Williams comeback | Mail DanielYara El-Shaboury was watching on No 2 Court, and has this quick report:Naomi Osaka cruised to a second-round 6-3, 6-2 win against the Russian qualifier Anastasia Gasanova. There was little worry for the four-time grand slam champion, whose serves and groundstrokes were stellar as she makes it to the third round at Wimbledon in back-to-back years. There was a small moment of frustration in the second set, with Osaka stating “What the hell?” after hitting the ball out, which garnered some chuckles from the No 2 Court crowd. She then turned to her team to complain about Gasanova’s grunting but got on with business to win in straight sets. The Japanese was candid in her on-court interview about her nerves, saying: “​I don’t rate my performance. I have to wait a bit to do that. My current emotion is that I am happy to win. I am glad to do it in straight sets. “Tomorrow is my daughter’s birthday so I didn’t want to make her get on a plane on her birthday. I will practise a bit in the morning and then maybe take her to the park. She loves making new friends.” Continue reading...
summary: Naomi Osaka won a second-round match at Wimbledon 2026, defeating Anastasia Gasanova in straight sets with a score of 6-3, 6-2. Osaka's victory marks her second consecutive year advancing to the third round at the tournament.

The onward march of rising seas around a sinking city was unsettling, but the study is “more focused on generating publicity and clickbait headlines” than coming up with solutions, said Helena Moreno, New Orleans’ mayor. There is flooding in Miami, and wildfires and earthquakes near San Fransisco, Moreno pointed out, “yet no serious movement exists to declare those cities lost causes”. Continue reading...

title: ESA Plans Enceladus Lander for 2050
content: Saturn's moon Enceladus has become a prime solar system target for astrobiologists. This is because the small moon, which is just over 10% the diameter of Earth's moon, harbors a vast subsurface ocean beneath its icy crust. This subsurface ocean, combined with the geysers at Enceladus' south pole that discharge bits of this ocean into the void, provides scientists with a treasure trove of opportunities for scientific research into whether Enceladus could harbor ingredients for life as we know it, or even direct evidence of life.
summary: The European Space Agency is planning to send a lander to Enceladus, a moon of Saturn, in 2050 to study its subsurface ocean. Enceladus is a prime target for astrobiologists due to its unique combination of a subsurface ocean and geysers that discharge ocean material into space.

title: Martian Dust Storms May Produce Electrical Activity
content: A new study by a doctoral researcher at The University of Alabama in Huntsville (UAH), part of The University of Alabama System, suggests global dust storms on Mars may organize the Martian atmosphere into regions favorable for electrical activity, increasing the potential for electrostatic discharges that could affect missions to the red planet by interfering with electronics, causing arcing between conductive surfaces, and damaging exposed scientific instruments and spacecraft systems. The research, conducted by Chali Idosa Uga, a third-year Ph. D. Student in the Department of Space Science at UAH, is published in The Planetary Science Journal.
summary: A new study suggests that global dust storms on Mars may create conditions favorable for electrical activity in the planet's atmosphere. The research, published in The Planetary Science Journal, indicates that this electrical activity could potentially interfere with or damage future missions to Mars.

title: Trump family crypto earnings exceed $1 billion in first year back in White House
content:
Senate Banking Committee Chairman Elizabeth Warren and a group of Democratic lawmakers called on Congress to tighten regulations governing cryptocurrency activities by elected officials and their families after recent financial disclosures showed that the Trump family’s crypto investments generated more than $1 billion in the first year of Donald Trump’s return to the White House. The disclosures, part of routine ethics filings, revealed that the former president’s relatives earned sizable profits from a range of digital‑asset holdings, prompting Warren to label the situation “brazen crypto corruption” and to argue that existing rules are insufficient to prevent conflicts of interest.

Warren said the pending crypto‑related legislation moving to the Senate floor must explicitly bar the President, Vice President, senior administration officials, members of Congress and their immediate families from profiting from the cryptocurrency industry. She warned that without such safeguards, the law could “turbocharge” the alleged misconduct and erode public confidence in government. Lawmakers are now reviewing the proposal, which aims to close loopholes and impose stricter disclosure and divestiture requirements for public officials engaged in digital‑asset transactions.
summary: Financial disclosures show that Donald Trump’s family earned more than $1 billion from cryptocurrency investments during his first year back in the White House. Senate Banking Committee member Elizabeth Warren urged tighter rules on political figures’ crypto dealings, citing the disclosures.

title: Gallup poll finds over half of Russians pessimistic for first time in 20 years
content: Nadia Massih is pleased to welcome Benedict Vigers, Senior Global News Writer at Gallup. For much of the war in Ukraine, conventional wisdom suggested that Russians had largely rallied behind the state despite mounting international sanctions and military costs. Gallup's latest research challenges that picture. Drawing on more than two decades of continuous polling, Vigers argues that Russia is experiencing not merely a deterioration in economic sentiment, but a broader psychological turning point. After years in which public confidence remained unexpectedly resilient, the latest data indicate simultaneous declines in perceptions of the economy, trust in key state institutions, confidence in the military, faith in elections, and even perceptions of media freedom.
summary: Gallup's latest survey shows that more than 50% of Russians expressed pessimism, the highest level in two decades. The poll also recorded simultaneous declines in confidence in the economy, state institutions, the military, elections and media freedom.

title: Serena Williams Returns to Wimbledon
content:
Serena Williams’s dramatic Wimbledon match against Maya Joint has captivated fans and critics alike, blending admiration for the tennis legend’s enduring skill with poignant reflections on her legacy. Facing a resilient Joint, Williams staged a comeback that defied expectations, despite ultimately falling short. The match, played under the Centre Court lights just after 7:30 p.m. on a warm evening, showcased Williams’s signature flair—her deliberate, almost theatrical pre-serve rituals and fluid footwork—reminders of her decades-long dominance in the sport. Spectators, some clutching vintage photos of her prime, stood in silent awe, as if witnessing a living history lesson unfold in real time.  

The atmosphere carried an almost ceremonial weight, with fans grappling with the duality of Williams’s presence: a once-unstoppable force now navigating the twilight of her career. Her ability to rally from a deficit, marked by explosive serves and strategic precision, underscored her resilience, even as the match’s outcome highlighted the shifting tides of time. The emotional resonance of the encounter was palpable, with Joint’s tenacity and Williams’s indomitable spirit creating a narrative of mutual respect. As the final point was played, the crowd’s sustained applause reflected both reverence for Williams’s achievements and a bittersweet acknowledgment of her evolving role in the sport. The match, a microcosm of her storied career, left an indelible mark on Wimbledon’s hallowed turf.
summary: Serena Williams made a comeback at Wimbledon, where she was defeated by Maya Joint. The crowd showed significant devotion to Williams, with some spectators bringing old photos of her to the match.

title: Genetic Link to Toddler Activity and ADHD
content: A toddler's activity levels are influenced by genetic differences, with some of the same genetic markers also linked to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), according to new research from the University of Surrey. In the first study of its kind, an international team of scientists, led by Professor Angelica Ronald, analyzed data from nearly 80,000 infants from multiple national and international cohort studies to discover the genetic differences that influence toddler activity levels. Genetic differences (or genetic variation) refer to the differences in DNA sequences between individuals.
summary: Researchers have found that genetic differences influence toddler activity levels and some of these genetic markers are also associated with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). The study analyzed data from nearly 80,000 infants from multiple national and international cohort studies to identify the genetic differences that affect toddler activity levels.

title: Mbappe scores twice as France beats Sweden 3-0, ties Messi for World Cup top scorer

The plan is part of a broader strategy to lure more than $50 billion in data‑centre investment, with the government seeking to balance the interests of the tech sector and the creative community.

Industry groups and individual creators have called for firm guarantees that the arrangement will not dilute existing copyright protections. They argue that any concession to AI companies must be matched by transparent, enforceable mechanisms to ensure that artists receive the promised remuneration and that the integrity of Australian copyright law remains intact. The proposal, reported by Guardian Australia, is now awaiting cabinet deliberation.
summary: The Albanese government has received a proposal to grant AI companies exemptions to mine creative content in exchange for a $350 million annual fund for artists. title: Venezuela Earthquake Aftermath: 1,700 Dead, Thousands Missing
content:
Venezuela’s Caribbean coast was struck by twin earthquakes last Wednesday, adding to a nation already in crisis after the United States removed its long‑time leader earlier this year. The seismic events, recorded by fishermen off the coast, produced sudden tremors that left buildings collapsed and dust plumes rising from the wreckage. In the aftermath, more than 1,700 people have been confirmed dead, while tens of thousands remain missing, prompting relentless search efforts by families and volunteers amid streets littered with rubble.

The footage captured by a cameraman, who described the ground as “shaking,” shows men rushing to the shore in search of loved ones, their faces etched with fear. Official reports indicate that the damage has overwhelmed local emergency services, and the scale of the disaster has strained an already fragile state apparatus. With limited governmental presence on the ground, many communities are relying on informal networks and international aid to coordinate rescue operations and provide basic necessities.

Rebuilding in Venezuela will require a concerted effort to restore infrastructure and governance capacity. International organizations have pledged assistance, but the effectiveness of aid will depend on establishing reliable channels of communication and resource distribution in a country where state institutions have been weakened by political upheaval. The long‑term recovery will hinge on rebuilding both physical structures and the public institutions needed to manage them.
summary: Twin earthquakes struck Venezuela on Wednesday, killing more than 1,700 people and leaving tens of thousands missing. Search and rescue operations continue amid widespread rubble and collapsed buildings.

title: Earth Microbes Can Withstand Martian Hazards and Evasive Astronaut Immune Systems
content: Hopefully, we're about to travel back to the moon relatively soon. And while the original "giant leap for mankind" was taken by a human, Neil Armstrong brought a plethora of other forms of life along with him. Humans themselves are essentially walking ecosystems, and understanding how our microbial companions survive in the harsh environments of space will be critical to ensuring the health and safety of future astronauts, no matter where their giant leaps might be. A new Ph. D. Thesis from Tommaso Zaccaria at Radboud University showcases just how well suited terrestrial pathogens actually are to some of these harsh environments.

title: Ireland's Haughey's Fort Unveiled as Ancient 'Town-like' Settlement
content: A major prehistoric center in Ireland was among the first large, organized settlements to develop in Western Europe more than 3,000 years ago, new research reveals. The study, published today in Antiquity, identifies Haughey's Fort, near Armagh in Northern Ireland, as the focal point of a vast and carefully planned landscape where settlement, craft production and ritual were brought together at an unprecedented scale from around 1200 BC.
summary: Researchers have identified Haughey's Fort in Northern Ireland as a large, organized settlement dating back over 3,000 years. The site, which emerged around 1200 BC, is believed to be one of Europe's earliest 'town-like' settlements, featuring a planned landscape with areas for settlement, craft production, and ritual activities.

title: Quantum computer simulates hadronization process
content: By remotely accessing an IBM quantum computer, a research scientist at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory has successfully simulated a key process in particle physics: hadronization. Although based on a simplified model of quantum mechanics, the project lays the groundwork for how physicists can leverage the power of quantum computers to make large scientific calculations beyond the capabilities of classical supercomputers. The research is published in the journal Physical Review D.
summary: Researchers at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory successfully simulated hadronization using a 104-qubit IBM quantum computer. The simulation, published in Physical Review D, demonstrates the potential of quantum computers for complex scientific calculations.

title: DNA Repair Mechanism Vulnerabilities Exposed in Cancer Cells

summary: A key gene involved in DNA protection is found to be compromised in cancerous cells, exposing vulnerabilities. This gene plays a crucial role in maintaining genome integrity by preventing damage or errors during DNA replication.

title: Grasslands' Carbon Uptake Threatened by Future Droughts
content: The effects of individual climate factors on ecosystems are usually considered in isolation. However, in reality, they occur simultaneously and influence each other. Increasing CO2 concentrations in the atmosphere contribute to climate warming, which in turn fosters more frequent and intense drought periods. A study from Innsbruck shows that the consequences of drought on grasslands in a future climate will be more severe than previously assumed. The work of a team led by Maud Tissink and Michael Bahn from the Department of Ecology has been published in Science Advances.
summary: A study led by researchers from the University of Innsbruck found that grasslands may lose four times more carbon uptake under future drought conditions. The increased frequency and intensity of drought periods, driven by climate warming, will have a more severe impact on grasslands than previously assumed.

A narrow defeat at Manchester City in mid-April had left the momentum with the hosts, and it appeared as though Arsenal's chances of winning the title were dwindling. However, Rice, who was a key player for the team, remained resolute, famously stating "it's not done" on the Etihad Stadium pitch.

Rice's words proved prophetic as Arsenal went on to win all of their remaining league games, securing the title for the first time since 2004. In contrast, Manchester City's losing streak ultimately cost them the championship. The midfielder has since looked back on the experience with a sense of relief, acknowledging that the outcome could have easily gone the other way. Rice's words on the pitch that day have become a defining moment of his season, a testament to his unwavering commitment to the team.

The experience has also taught Rice the importance of patience, particularly when facing teams that are unwilling to attack. His time at Arsenal last season has provided valuable lessons that he can draw upon in the future, as he continues to develop as a player and a leader on the pitch.
summary: England midfielder Declan Rice is set to face DR Congo in the World Cup last 32 stage. Rice's experience with Arsenal last season taught him the importance of patience against teams unwilling to attack.

title: Norway Advance to Last 16 in World Cup with Haaland's Late Winner

As Solbakken said, the decision would stand or fall on the result of this game. Norway are in the last 16, and therefore his policy can be considered justified. It was, though, a mightily close-run thing. Having taken a first-half lead through Antonio Nusa, Norway had seemed to be in control, Côte d’Ivoire’s possession sterile. But then Amad Diallo produced one of the great substitute interventions, making a remarkable clearance to keep out a Torbjørn Heggem volley before scoring a stunning equaliser. A specific version of active sensing is infotaxis, which describes how animals move strategically to maximize the information they gain from their surroundings. title: iOS Installation of Cursor App Alters User Privacy Settings Irreversibly
content: Just hit this today and I'm furious. I installed the Cursor iOS app to see what it had. I've been on `Privacy Mode (Legacy)` for a long time, which is the "Do not store my code" setting. A year or so ago they marked this as "Legacy" and hid it under a "Extra options" menu. They added a new Privacy Mode which is significantly more wishy-washy about what it might store - it includes a clause of "Code may be stored for Background Agents or Other Features", so I've never touched it or wanted to enable it. Pic: https://us1. Discourse-cdn. Com/cursor1/optimized/3X/0/9/09412f800cb07a713d13c034f40eaf28e165e8f4_2_1032x1000. JpegUpon installing and logging in to the iOS app, my account was changed to the softer Privacy Mode and the previous setting I was on has disappeared from all menus. I contacted support and they've said:> Really sorry about this. When you set up the mobile app, the prompt to turn on Cloud Agents switched you from Privacy Mode (Legacy) to our current Privacy Mode,> without making clear what that meant or that it's hard to undo. That wasn't right, and we're working on making that prompt clearer.>> To be straight with you: I'm not able to switch your account back to Privacy Mode (Legacy). The option to move back isn't available in the app today. So just a PSA I guess; do not install or set up the app if you want to keep your privacy settings. I honestly don't understand how it's legal to make logging into the iOS app change your privacy settings at all. Making the option then disappear from all menus so you can't get it back is doubly ridiculous. Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=48737226 Points: 108 # Comments: 17
summary: The Cursor iOS app automatically changes users' privacy settings from "Privacy Mode (Legacy)" to a more permissive "Privacy Mode" upon installation, without providing clear notice. This change is permanent and cannot be reversed, according to the app's support team.

title: ITV Secures 2027 Rugby World Cup Rights and England Men's International Deal
content:
ITV has secured a landmark agreement to broadcast the 2027 men’s Rugby World Cup, reinforcing its role as the primary UK broadcaster for international rugby. The deal, which grants the commercial network live rights to the tournament, also extends its coverage of England men’s internationals through to 2029. This follows an existing partnership that includes a shared Six Nations Championship arrangement with the BBC, under which ITV holds two-thirds of the tournament’s live games and all England matches.  

In addition to the World Cup, ITV has acquired live rights for all matches of the 2026 and 2028 editions of the Nations Championship, a new global competition set to debut this Saturday. The inaugural tournament features six teams, including high-profile fixtures such as New Zealand v France and South Africa v England. The extended coverage cements ITV’s dominance in the UK market for international rugby, offering viewers a comprehensive schedule of live action across multiple global events.  

The agreement underscores ITV’s strategy to consolidate its position as the go-to platform for rugby fans, combining major tournaments with consistent international match coverage. With rights secured through 2029, the broadcaster aims to provide uninterrupted access to England’s rugby campaigns and global competitions, ensuring sustained engagement with the sport’s growing audience.
summary: ITV has acquired live rights to the 2027 Rugby World Cup, solidifying its coverage of international rugby in the UK. The broadcaster will also have live coverage of every England men's international until at least 2029, as part of its existing contract.

title: Quantum Computers Fail to Deliver Practical Applications
content: To this day, we have yet to see a quantum computer conclusively perform a single useful task. Existing machines are simply too small and error-ridden to solve commercially relevant problems. That hasn't stopped Donald Trump's science adviser from promising a "quantum computer powerful enough for scientific discovery by 2028" and Trump from issuing a new executive order to speed up the US quantum computing industry in its competition with China, both on June 22nd. Companies drive the hype, too. In June, Microsoft announced a new quantum computing chip named Majorana 2. It claimed the chip was a hardware advancement that accelerates its timel … Read the full story at The Verge.
summary: Quantum computers have yet to perform a useful task due to their current limitations of size and error rate. Despite promises of advancements, existing machines are not yet capable of solving commercially relevant problems.

title: Bose Soundlink Max receives $120 discount ahead of July 4th weekend
content:
Bose SoundLink Max Sees Significant Price Drop at Major Retailers

The Bose SoundLink Max, a high-end Bluetooth speaker known for its powerful sound and durability, has been discounted by $120 at several major retailers, including Amazon, Best Buy, and Bose itself. The speaker, which typically retails for $399, can now be purchased for $279. This move offers consumers a significant opportunity to acquire a premium product at a more affordable price.

The SoundLink Max boasts an impressive IP67 rating, making it suitable for outdoor use, and features a built-in battery that lasts up to 20 hours on a single charge. Additionally, the speaker includes a USB-C port for charging other devices and a removable handle for convenient transport. While some features, such as speakerphone capabilities and Wi-Fi connectivity, are missing, the speaker's colorful finishes and robust soundstage make it an attractive option for those seeking a high-quality Bluetooth speaker.
summary: The Bose Soundlink Max Bluetooth speaker is currently available for $279, a $120 discount from its usual price of $399. The speaker features a 20-hour battery life and IP67 rating, making it suitable for outdoor use.
author: The Verge

title: Google to Discontinue Tenor GIF Search API in Other Apps
content: The GIF-picking interfaces in some of your favorite online platforms might look different going forward, as Google prepares to shut down the Tenor API today. While the Tenor website, along with its searchable GIF library, will remain live, platforms like X, Discord, Bluesky, and WhatsApp that previously integrated the API are now having to migrate to alternative GIF picker services. Google acquired the Tenor GIF platform in 2018. Both its website and API allow users to search for GIFs using keywords, similar to competing services like Giphy and Klipy. Google will continue using Tenor across its own services, including Google Messages and Gb … Read the full story at The Verge.
summary: Google is shutting down the Tenor API, which allows other apps to integrate GIF search functionality, effective immediately. The Tenor website and its searchable GIF library will remain operational, but apps like X, Discord, and WhatsApp will need to find alternative GIF picker services.

title: Moto Tag 2 Tracker Available in US at Discounted Price
content:
Motorola has launched the Moto Tag 2 in the United States, a Bluetooth tracker with enhanced features and a discounted introductory price. Announced at CES 2026, the device is priced at $19.99 (down from $29.99) for a single unit on Motorola’s website, with a four-pack available for $69.99. The tracker is currently offered exclusively in the “Laurel Oak” color option, while the “Arabesque” variant remains unavailable.  

The Moto Tag 2 improves upon its predecessor with ultra-wideband (UWB) sensing for precise tracking, a replaceable CR2032 coin battery lasting up to 600 days, and an IP68 waterproof rating. It integrates with Google’s Find Hub network and includes a 77-decibel speaker for easier location identification. The device’s button can be programmed for functions like locating a nearby phone or activating a camera shutter, adding versatility to its core tracking capabilities.  

Priced competitively against other Android-compatible trackers, the Moto Tag 2 emphasizes durability and functionality. Its special launch pricing and feature set position it as a compelling option for users seeking a reliable tracking solution. Availability through Motorola’s direct channel ensures immediate access for customers, though the limited color selection may affect some buyers’ preferences.
summary: Moto Tag 2 Tracker Available in US at Discounted Price.
author: The Verge
